general: Tell me honestly. Do you know where we are going?
I know where we have been. That has to count for something.
We have been walking since before it was light.
And we will be walking after it is dark. That is the arrangement.
If this all ends badly, I want it written down that I said so.
It is written down. You say it every week.
Do you ever think about going home?
Home is wherever the packs are.
That is a very sad thing to be at peace with.
You have been quiet all day.
I was thinking. It happens.
Tell me again why we took this road.
Because you asked, and I said yes. Fool that I am.
I would not have made it this far alone.
Nor I. Do not let it go to your head.
How is that wound of yours holding up?
It has stopped bleeding, which is something.
If we get paid, I am buying the first round.
You said that in the last three towns.
Do you trust the people we met back there?
I trust nobody I cannot outrun.
You carry too much. Give me half.
I can manage. Ask me again on the hill.
One of these days we should stop for a whole week.
A week. Listen to us.
What did you do before all this?
Something quieter. I do not miss it as much as I should.
How much money have we actually got?
{gold}, and half of it is spoken for.
So the answer is no, then.
Say we found somewhere decent tomorrow. Would you stop?
Ask me tomorrow. I am too tired to be honest tonight.
Who is leading this, exactly?
{leader} walks in front. That is not quite the same thing.
I dreamed we were still walking.
That is a memory arriving early.
I had a dream about this place. Do not ask.
You always dream about the wrong things.
One of these days I will dream about the right one and you will owe me an apology.
Do you think anyone is looking for us?
Somebody always is. It is who that changes.
We should agree on what we do if it goes wrong.
We run. That is the plan. It has never let us down.
I have been counting the days.
How many?
I lost count. That is my point.
Nobody warned me the boring parts would be the worst.
Nobody warned me about any of it.
Your boots are finished.
My boots have been finished since spring. They have not been told.
I keep expecting somebody to come and take charge.
That was the job nobody applied for.
What is the first thing you buy, if we ever come out of this rich?
Silence. A whole room of it.
We are getting good at this.
We are getting used to it. Do not confuse the two.
If I go down, do not carry me. Take the pack and go.
I will carry you and complain the entire way.
I have stopped asking what is over the next hill.
Good. The answer has been disappointing four times running.
Say something interesting. Anything.
The word for a group of crows is a murder.
I regret asking.
Are we the good ones in this?
We are the ones still walking. Ask a historian about the rest.
Do you remember the name of that town? The one with the bells?
No. But I remember the bells.
I want one day where nothing at all happens.
You would be unbearable by noon.
We have not talked properly in weeks.
We are talking now.
This is not talking. This is walking with noise.
What would you be doing right now, if none of this had happened?
Something with fewer hills in it.
That is not an answer. That is a complaint with a hat on.
You have not asked me a single question about myself in a month.
I assumed you would say it when you wanted to.
That is either very considerate or very lazy.
Who taught you to fight like that?
Nobody. That is rather the problem.
I have been keeping a list of everything we are owed.
By whom?
That is the weakness in the list, yes.
Do you think we have changed?
You have got quieter and I have got worse. So yes.
If you could take one thing back out of all of it, what would it be?
Ask me something easier. Ask me about the weather.
Nobody out here knows our names.
That has been the single best part of the last year.
We are going to run out of money before we run out of road.
We have been in that state since the day we met. Keep walking.
Watch out for that one. They are pleasant, and pleasant is expensive.
Noted. And if they are simply pleasant?
Then I will have been wrong twice this year.
How do you sleep, out here, with all of it?
Badly, and then all at once.
That is the most honest thing you have said to me.
We should decide now who carries what if we have to run.
You take the money, I take the water. Neither of us takes the tent.
Say we finish this. Say it actually ends. Then what?
Then I find out whether I am any good at ordinary days.
I do not think either of us is doing this for the money any more.
Speak for yourself. I am doing it entirely for the money.
You could at least pretend to think about it before answering.
Every town we pass is somebody's whole life.
And we are two strangers walking through the middle of it. Try to be polite.
There is something I should have told you a while ago.
Then tell me on the road. I would rather hear it moving.
You can see the Tower from here if you stand on the bank.
I have seen it from four countries. It never looks any further away.
Somebody told me the Tower holds the ninety-two dimensions together.
Like the stick through a sandwich. That was the phrase they used.
That is not reassuring and I have thought about it every day since.
Would you go in? The Tower, I mean. If somebody paid.
I would go in. I would not go up.
They say the door opened on its own in ninety-nine.
Two billion people died that night and a door opened. Those are related.
Ninety-two floors of dimensions and somebody has put a department store in it.
There are camping tents in the corridors. I have seen photographs.
If the Tower is a spear, somebody threw it.
And whatever she was aiming at is still down there under all that rock.
The Foundation charges to go past the third floor now.
They charge to go anywhere. It is neutral ground with a till on it.
Do you believe there is a goddess doing the paperwork?
I believe somebody put a bounty on me for a broken window. Call that what you like.
Everything we do is watched by somebody who is bad at justice.
That is the whole century, summarised.
Have you ever seen a judicial ghost?
Once, from a long way off. It walked in a straight line through a wall.
Then let us keep doing nothing worth a straight line.
A god only exists while people believe in them.
Which means the small ones die of being forgotten. That is a horrible way to go.
They say Draghi is a god now, and he is a number.
Every note in your pocket has his name on it. Do the arithmetic.
Do you pray?
I keep my head down. It works out to about the same thing.
If she were killed, the throne would be empty for a few days.
And every ambitious idiot in ninety-two dimensions would start climbing.
You have thought about this in more detail than I am comfortable with.
Two thousand and twelve. Everyone says it like a date.
It is a deadline. That is why they say it like that.
Do you ever think we are living in the last ordinary years?
I think every generation has believed that. Ours has the arithmetic to back it.
Keep under eighty on this stretch. There is a bubble marked at the bend.
I know. I have driven it before. I would like it noted that I know.
What happens if we go into one?
The same day, forever, until somebody drives out of it at speed.
And nobody outside can telephone in to tell us. Wonderful.
There are people who live in the bubbles on purpose.
You cannot die in one unless something hits you fast enough. That is a bargain some people take.
They send pigeons between the bubbles. Actual pigeons.
With memory sticks tied to their legs. It is the only post that works.
Somebody said the bubbles are getting bigger every year.
They are. That is the point of the deadline.
I would not want to be the one who lives the same day forever.
You already are. You simply have worse weather.
Every road in every world is the same road, apparently.
The Encompassing Road. Take the wrong turn off it and you are somewhere else entirely.
If the engine is calibrated right, a turn-off goes to another dimension.
And if it is calibrated wrong you arrive somewhere with no ground. Choose your mechanic.
There is a god of asphalt, they say. He made the first road.
And was the first thing run over on it. Somebody has a sense of humour.
A man built an engine in a camper and made himself rich.
He built it to get away from somebody. That is what I heard.
Do you think the road knows we are on it?
Ask me again after dark and I will give you a different answer.
The archivists stopped a party ahead of us and read out their messages.
They call it making things public. It is reading somebody's post in the road.
The Collective sells water and buys memories.
And every other liquid on the shelf has something in it. Drink from the well.
Nobody has ever seen an Esoteric Heavy Industries factory.
The crates simply appear in the warehouse when nobody is looking. I have asked.
Their goods ignore the loop. Move it slowly and it still does not reset.
Which is why one of their kettles costs more than this vehicle.
The Guild is the richest faction and it achieves nothing.
It is two halves that hate each other holding the same purse.
Vatican City floats eight hundred metres over Rome now.
And it shoots at anything that comes close. Progress, of a kind.
Would you take work from the Foundation?
I would take their money. I would not sign the release.
The truckers keep the bubble towns alive. That is not a small thing.
They are the only faction I have never been lied to by.
The Naguka came up out of a Soviet borehole. That is the actual history.
Somebody drilled too deep and the world got worse. Twice, if you count the oil.
Hurt one Naguka and the whole species knows.
So do not. It is the simplest rule in the world and people keep breaking it.
The Verden lay eggs and speak better than we do.
And they came from a world that threw its technology into a sun on purpose.
Why would anybody give up everything they had built?
Perhaps they found out what it was for. That is the version that frightens me.
Half the goblin hordes worship a Norwegian band.
And the band has become gods, because enough of them believe it. That is how it works now.
Do not separate the words of a spell. Ever.
I know the law. The universe sends the bill and it is not money.
Say it in one breath and joined up, or do not say it.
CamelCase. It is the first thing anybody learns and the last thing anybody respects.
I saw a grimoire eat a notebook once.
Then it was badly written. A bad spell spreads. Burn the book, not the shelf.
Standing on a leyline makes everything stronger and nothing controllable.
Which is why the good mages are the ones who read maps.
Break a leyline and nothing works there for a generation.
Except the divine ones, and they answer to somebody with opinions.
Lava does not burn you any more. It drains you.
Unless it was conjured. Then it does both, out of spite.
Nobody can leave the atmosphere any more.
There is a mill of scrap going round the planet at eight kilometres a second. Nobody is going anywhere.
They are building rockets out of armour and volunteers.
Free of charge, both directions, and nobody comes back. Very generous.
Mexico looks like Africa from orbit now. In one day.
And everybody who lived there is still there. That is the part people skip.
Somebody in New York lost their soul to a bomb that left the buildings standing.
Do not say that word out loud on this road. Not with the Guild in the next valley.
My grandmother remembered before the sky broke.
Mine claimed to. Everybody's grandmother claims to.
What is the least we could live on?
Less than this. We have proved it twice and I do not want a third proof.
Do you ever count what we are owed?
I stopped. The number stopped being funny.
We could take honest work.
We take honest work. It is the pay that is dishonest.
If one of us came into money, would the others hear about it?
You would hear about it. You would hear about it at length.
Who holds the fund tonight?
Whoever sleeps worst. That is how it has always been settled.
We have never agreed on what a fair split is.
We have never had enough at once for it to be a real argument.
Say we get paid properly, once. What is the first thing?
Boots. Then a room. Then boots again for whoever is still complaining.
What would you have made of me, if we had met in a town?
I would have thought you were somebody's problem. I would have been right.
How long have we been doing this now?
Long enough that I do not count it in weeks any more.
Do you ever want to travel with anybody else?
No. That is arithmetic. New people get killed.
I would tell you if I was thinking of leaving.
I know. That is why I sleep.
You went ahead without me at the ford.
I did. I have been waiting for you to say so all afternoon.
We have not had a proper argument in a month.
Give it a week. There is one coming and we both know the subject.
If we stopped tomorrow, would you say it had been worth it?
Ask me somewhere warm and I will lie beautifully.
You are the only person who knows all of it.
And I have never once used it against you. Consider that.
Tell me something you have never told anyone.
No.
That is fair. I would have said no as well.
We should decide now who tells the family, if it goes badly.
Neither of us has one. That is why we are out here.
How many kilometres today, honestly?
More than yesterday. Less than we said this morning.
We have walked past four villages without stopping.
Stopping is how we lost the last three days.
The map is wrong about this whole valley.
Every map has been wrong since ninety-two. They are historical documents now.
Which way at the fork?
The one with the traffic. Traffic means somebody thinks it goes somewhere.
I want a road with a name on it.
You want a road with an inn on it. Say what you mean.
We should be somewhere by dark.
We are always somewhere by dark. It is what sort of somewhere that varies.
Do you know where we are, exactly?
I know where we are roughly, and roughly has kept us alive.
There is weather coming off that ridge.
There is. Walk faster and stop admiring it.
We have been going downhill for two hours and I do not trust it.
Downhill is always paid for. Somewhere ahead there is the bill.
What is the worst road you have ever walked?
This one, eventually. Everything becomes the worst road eventually.
The tent has one more season in it. Maybe.
It had one more season three seasons ago. It is a very brave tent.
We are down to the food nobody wanted.
Then somebody is about to discover they wanted it after all.
Whose turn is the second watch?
Mine. It is always mine, because I am the only one who wakes up.
I have mended this strap four times.
Mend it a fifth. We are not buying a strap in this country's prices.
Everything in this pack is either broken or nearly.
Same as everything carrying it.
Do we have anything for a fever?
We have something for a fever, something for a cut, and a great deal of hope.
I would trade the lamp for a dry coat.
You would trade the lamp and then walk into a hole. No.
That family has been ahead of us since the bridge.
Then let them stay ahead. A road with people on it is a road that goes somewhere.
Would you take a passenger?
Depends who is looking for them.
Everybody out here is going somewhere they will not talk about.
Including us. That is why nobody asks.
Do you trust a man who tells you his whole story in ten minutes?
I trust him to be lying. Whether it matters is another question.
Somebody will offer us work in the next town.
Somebody always does. That is not the same as somebody paying.
The last party we met had one fewer than when they set out.
They did not mention it and we did not ask. That is the etiquette.
Nothing has happened for two days and I am uneasy about it.
Enjoy it. Being uneasy about peace is a habit, not a warning.
What do you think about when there is nothing to think about?
Doors. Rooms with doors. It is not interesting but it is honest.
I have started talking to myself.
I know. I have been answering some of it.
Say something. Anything at all.
There is a bird on that post that has been watching us for a kilometre.
Thank you. That was worse than the silence.
Do you think anyone writes any of this down?
Somebody in the Foundation, probably. Badly, and without our names.
One day I will tell all of this properly, in order.
You will tell it out of order, and better, and half of it will be untrue.
Do you want the good news or the arithmetic?
The arithmetic. The good news is always the arithmetic with a hat on.
We have not been paid in full once this year.
We have not finished a job in full once this year. I am not defending them, only counting.
I have worked out what we spend a week.
Do not tell me.
It is more than we earn.
I asked you not to tell me.
If a stranger offered us honest work at honest pay, what would you say?
I would say no, out of habit, and think about it for a month.
We are good at this and nobody knows.
That is the business. Nobody knows any of the good ones.
What would make you turn a job down?
Children in it. That is the whole list and it has never been added to.
The last man who hired us knew our names before we said them.
Then somebody sold him our names. That is a service now.
Do we have a reputation?
We have four, in four countries, and only one of them is accurate.
I have been thinking about doing something else.
Everybody thinks about doing something else. On this road, at this hour, everybody.
What else could you do?
Anything with a roof and a grimorie. I would be terrible and I would be warm.
Say we save enough. What would you buy?
Somewhere with a door I own. That is the entire fantasy.
The Collective would take us on tomorrow.
The Collective takes everybody on tomorrow. It is what happens on the day after that.
I would not work for the archivists.
You would work for the archivists if it was winter and we were hungry. So would I.
Everything we own is on our backs.
Everything we own is on our backs and nobody can take it in the night. There are worse arrangements.
I have started giving the boots names.
That is the second stage. The third is arguing with them.
We should keep a proper record of the routes.
You keep saying that and then we walk instead.
What is the furthest east you have been?
Further than I will admit to on a road with people on it.
Do you know what today is?
It is a walking day. They are all walking days.
It is the solstice.
Then it is a long walking day.
What month is it, honestly?
I know what month it is. I am simply not going to say it out loud, because of the number after it.
Somebody ought to name this road.
It has a name. Everything has a name. Nobody uses them any more, that is all.
Do you think the roads will still be here after?
After? The roads are the one thing that will be here after. Ask the truckers.
Eleven years.
Do not do that. Do not count down out loud.
Everyone talks about the deadline like it is weather.
It is weather. That is exactly what it is, and you cannot argue with weather.
Some of the dimensions are already gone, they say.
Not gone. Emptied. The people came here. That is why the roads are busy.
Where do you think the goblins actually came from?
Downwards. And they have every right to be annoyed about the drilling.
The Verden woman in that market spoke better than I do.
She has spoken it for two years. You have spoken it your whole life. Sit with that.
Do you believe the story about the band?
I believe enough goblins believe it, which is the only part that matters.
I met a man who claimed to have been inside a petrodemon contract.
Then he was lying or he was rich. Which was he?
Rich.
There you are, then.
Everything runs on oil that used to be a lizard with opinions.
Say that again in a town and see what happens to you.
I saw an Anoki phone on a trucker's dash. An actual one.
Then he is somebody. They do not hand those out.
Could you telephone a god on one, do you think?
You could telephone something. Whether you would like the answer is the question.
The banknotes have Tower scrapings in them.
Which is why they do not reset in a bubble. Everything in this century is held together with paint.
Who is actually in charge? Of anything?
Whoever answers when you telephone. And nobody answers.
There are three Americas and none of them are free.
There is one Britannia and it owns a coast of one of them. Do not start.
Was there ever a time when the world was simple?
There was a time when the lies were more consistent. People call that simple.
Do you remember television?
There is still television. It is simply mostly a man reading numbers.
I would like to see the sea from the other side once.
There is no other side any more. Not without a rocket and a bad plan.
A whole cage of scrap going round the planet.
And volunteers queuing up to be fired through it for nothing. People are extraordinary.
Do you ever want to know how it ends?
No. I want to know where we sleep. Those are different sizes of question.
We have walked further this year than most people walk in a life.
And seen the same four things in eleven countries.
Which country was the best?
The one where nobody asked for papers. I have forgotten which one that was.
Which was the worst?
The one we are in tomorrow. It is a good system, this pessimism.
Do you keep anything from the places we pass?
A stone from each. It is stupid and the pack is heavy and I am not stopping.
I have started forgetting the order of it.
Then it has become a life instead of a journey. That is not the worst thing.
Say we are still doing this in ten years.
Then somebody has been very lucky and it is not going to be both of us.
Would you want to be remembered?
I would want somebody to know where I stopped. That is different and it is enough.
Nobody has written our names down anywhere.
The Foundation has. Twice. In the wrong spelling.
What was your first road?
A short one, out of somewhere I do not talk about. Ask me a different question.
We have never had this conversation properly.
We have had it four times. You forget it every time and I let you.
Tell me about the winter before we met.
It was cold and I was alone and I have made it sound better every year since.
Do you think we are friends, or something else?
We are something else. There is not a word and I am not going to invent one on a hill.
I would notice if you were gone.
That is the most romantic thing anybody has said to me in a decade.
You have never asked me for anything.
I have asked you for everything. You have simply never noticed, because you gave it.
If I asked you to turn round now, would you?
Yes. Do not ask, because I would want a reason afterwards and you would not have one.
We should agree on a signal.
We have a signal.
We have four and none of us can remember which is which.
What do we do if we are separated in a town?
The gate we came in by, at dusk, two days running. Then the road.
I do not want to be carried, if it comes to that.
You will be carried and you will complain. That is the arrangement and it is not open.
Nobody out here says thank you enough.
Thank you.
Not to me. Generally.
Generally, thank you.
I am glad it is you.
Do not go soft on a good road. Save it for the mud.
We should have a rule about the last of the water.
There is a rule. Whoever is worst has it, and nobody admits to being worst.
Who is the sensible one, out of the two of us?
Whichever of us is not talking. It changes hourly.
I have been wrong about something for a long time.
About me?
About me. It will keep. But I wanted it said today.
Do you sleep better when I am on watch?
Yes. Do not make anything of it.
What happens to whoever is left?
They keep walking. That is the whole answer and we both knew it before I said it.
I have made a list of everybody we have lost.
Burn it or carry it. Do not read it on the road.
Some days I cannot remember why we started.
For money. Then it became habit. Then it became this. That is most lives.
We could have been ordinary.
We could have been ordinary somewhere that got emptied. Do not romanticise it.
What is the best day you have had out here?
One with nothing in it. A dry road and nobody wanting anything.
Then today is a candidate.
Today is a candidate. Do not tell it.
Everything hurts and I am content. Explain that.
You are tired and safe at the same time. It happens perhaps twice a year.
Do you ever talk to people who are not here?
Every night on the second watch. It is the only thing that keeps me awake.
Somebody is going to ask us for help in the next town.
Somebody always does. Say yes to the small one and no to the interesting one.
I have stopped being able to say no.
Then I will say it for you, and you can be cross with me and grateful later.
We have never once turned round because it was hard.
We have turned round twice because it was stupid. That is a better record.
Have we ever done anything that mattered?
Twice. You were asleep for one of them.
What would you change?
Nothing that is in my hands. Everything that is not.
Sometimes I think we are only walking to stay ahead of thinking.
That is exactly what we are doing. It is a working method.
The next town, I am going to sit down and not stand up for a day.
The next town has a hill in it. I have seen the map.
Everything east of here is somebody else's story.
Then let us go and be a minor character in it for a week.
Do you want to know what I want?
Yes.
A quiet week and somebody else's roof.
That is a shopping list.
We are going to be all right, are we not?
We are going to be all right today. I do not do further than that any more.
Keep talking. It makes the hill shorter.
It does not make the hill shorter. It makes it possible, which is better.
I have run out of things to say.
Then say nothing well. That is a skill and you have never had it.
We have another two hours in us.
We have another two hours in us and then a very honest conversation about the tent.
Tell me it is worth it.
It is worth it.
You said that too quickly.
I have had a long time to practise.
I want it on record that I was here.
You are on record. I am the record. It is not a good one but it is yours.
What do you think about when you walk?
Doors, dinners, and whether the strap will hold. In that order, all day.
Nobody ever writes about the walking.
Nobody ever writes about the waiting either, and that is most of it.
One more ridge and then we stop.
You said that at the last one.
I will keep saying it until one of them is true.
Is there anything you would not tell me?
One thing. And this is not the road for it.
Then tell me on a better road.
There is not going to be a better road. But I will tell you anyway, eventually.
That is the sun going.
Then walk faster and admire it later.
Twelve hours and we have not argued once.
Give it until the tent. The tent is where the arguing lives.
Same time tomorrow?
Same time tomorrow. Same road, worse weather, probably.
Right. Onwards, then.
Onwards. It is the only direction with anything in it.
Are you going to tell me what happened at the ford, or do I guess?
Guess. You are usually kinder than the truth.
What is the plan if neither of us can walk?
Then we are somewhere with a roof, or we are not, and there is no third case.
I would like one day where nobody wants anything from us.
That day exists. It is always the day after tomorrow.
Do you think about what we are walking towards, or only away?
Away. It has been away for a long time now.
Somebody said the roads are getting safer.
Somebody says that in every town, and it is always somebody who does not travel.
We should write down what we are owed and by whom.
You have. Twice. You lost both.
If we found a place, would you stop?
I would stop for a winter. That is as far as I will commit on a hill.
I have been counting the days again.
How many?
I lost count. That is what I keep discovering.
Everything about this year has been slightly wrong.
Everything about the last twelve has. This one is only closer.
Tell me the plan out loud so I can hear how bad it is.
There is no plan. There is a direction and some food.
That is the second time you have said that today.
Then it is the second time it has been true today.
We are going to be fine.
Say that again with something behind it.
We are going to be fine.
Do you want to know what I have decided about all this?
Not on a hill. Tell me when we are sitting down.
Whoever lights the stove first gets to choose the tea.
That is why I have been waking up at five. It was never about the sunrise.
You fold the map the wrong way every single morning.
There is no right way. There is only your way, and you have made it a religion.
It is a religion with fewer tears in it.
Socks on the line, boots by the fire, bread in the tin. Same every night.
Some people would call that a home, {name}. We simply carry ours.
I can pitch the tent in the dark now without swearing.
Not without swearing. Only more quietly.
Your turn to fetch water.
It was my turn yesterday.
It was. You were very good at it. Do it again.
That is not how turns work and you know it.
I have started counting steps between the milestones.
And how many is that?
Eleven hundred and something. Then a cow distracts me and I lose it.
Funny how the camper smells of us now.
It smells of wet wool and onions. I am choosing to call that us as well.
Every morning you check the sky, I check the boots, and nobody checks the pan.
The pan has been on its own since the spring. It is coping.
We wash the cups in the same order every night.
Mine first, because mine is the clean one.
Yours is the clean one because you never drink anything out of it.
I know your snoring well enough to tell when you are pretending.
I never pretend. I snore with complete sincerity.
{other}, you put the salt in the left pocket again.
The left pocket is the salt pocket. It was decided at a meeting.
I was not at that meeting.
You were asleep at that meeting. It still counts.
When I was small we had a kitchen with a yellow door.
Why yellow?
My mother lost an argument with a paint shop. She stood by it for twenty years.
I used to catch the same tram at the same minute every day.
Do you miss it?
I miss knowing where I would be at eight in the morning. Not the tram.
Before all this I worked behind a counter selling buttons.
Buttons.
Thousands of them. I can still tell bone from horn at ten paces.
There was a boy on my street who could whistle with two fingers. I never learned.
I can teach you, {name}. It takes a week and costs you your dignity.
What was your house like?
Narrow. Three floors, one room on each, and a staircase everybody fell down once.
My father kept every newspaper. Stacks of them in the hall.
Did he read them again?
Never. He said they were proof the days had happened.
That is either very wise or a fire hazard.
I had a bicycle with one gear and enormous opinions.
So the bicycle was you, then.
I miss school bells. Is that not strange?
Not strange. Somebody told you when things ended. Nobody does that out here.
Once I ran away from home for a whole afternoon.
Where did you go?
The end of the garden. There was a tree and a sandwich and I felt enormous.
You tap the doorframe twice every time you go through one.
Once for leaving, once for coming back. It is not complicated.
Why do you always sit facing the door?
Because the one time I did not, a goat came in.
You hum when you are counting money.
I hum when I am counting anything. Money is simply the only thing worth counting aloud.
{other}, you have eaten the crusts first again.
The crusts are the hard part. Get the hard part over and the rest is a holiday.
You apply that to everything.
I apply that to bread. Do not make a philosopher of me.
You talk to the stove.
The stove listens. That is more than I can say for some people.
Is that aimed at me?
It is aimed at the stove's competitors in general.
Why do you fold your shirts like letters?
So they fit in the pack, and so I can pretend somebody sent them.
You always leave one bite on the plate.
For luck. Or manners. My grandmother never told me which.
So you have done it for no reason your whole life.
For a very old reason. That is different.
You sharpen pencils with the knife you use for cheese.
The knife does not mind. The cheese has never complained.
Every time you lie down you sigh like a door closing.
It is a door closing. The day goes out and I lock it.
I would give a great deal for a plate of my aunt's lentils.
What was in them?
Lentils, a bay leaf and a level of patience I have never met since.
What I want right now is fresh bread with too much butter.
Stop. I can smell it, and we have nothing but biscuits.
At home we made soup out of whatever the week left behind.
Every family has that soup.
Ours had a name. We called it Thursday.
Have you ever had chestnuts roasted in a pan with holes in it?
Every autumn. My grandfather burned his thumbs on purpose, I am sure of it.
At the next market I am spending {gold} on proper rice and real cheese.
Cooked in what pot?
The small pot and a great deal of patience. Do not argue with a craving.
You put sugar in tomato sauce.
A pinch. To calm the tomatoes.
That is not a recipe. That is a bribe.
Name one food you could eat every day forever.
Oranges. Peeled in one go, the skin in one long curl.
That is not a food. That is a performance.
It is both, and I am very good at it.
My mother's rule: never trust a cook who does not taste as they go.
So you have been watching me taste the stew.
For weeks. You pass, narrowly.
I could eat a whole jar of pickles tonight.
You ate a whole jar of pickles on Tuesday, {name}.
And look how well I am.
When this is done I will learn to make pasta by hand.
Flour, eggs and your elbows. My grandmother did it on the kitchen table.
Would she teach a stranger?
She would teach the postman if he stood still long enough.
Cheap cheese in a good place tastes better than good cheese in a bad one.
That is either very deep or you are very hungry.
Both. Pass the cheese.
I have had the same song in my head since the bridge.
Which one?
I do not know the words. Only the part that goes up at the end.
That is every song, {name}.
The cassette in the camper is starting to stretch.
It was always slow. It only sounds sadder now.
My grandmother sang one tune while she shelled peas. No words, only the tune.
Hum it.
Not here. It only works with peas.
The radio has found a station that plays nothing but accordions.
Leave it on. It has more feeling in it than the news.
Could you sing something? Anything.
If I sing, the birds leave and so do you.
Then sing quietly and only the birds will leave.
I made a mixtape once for somebody I never gave it to.
What was on it?
Eleven songs, and the sound of me being too shy to press stop at the end.
Every station out here fades in the middle of the chorus.
The radio knows. It is saving the good bits for somebody else.
That tune you whistle every morning. What is it?
A dance from the village I grew up in.
It sounds very sad for a dance.
You have not seen the village.
{leader} hums the same tune every time we break camp.
I noticed. It seems to be the only song with a verse for folding a tent.
I bought a cassette in the last town without looking at it.
What is on it?
A man singing about his boat. Forty minutes about one boat.
I dreamed I was back at school and nobody had told me there was an exam.
I have that one every year. The exam is always in a language I do not speak.
Last night I dreamed the camper could fly.
Did it go anywhere useful?
It went to my cousin's wedding. It was still raining.
You laughed in your sleep last night.
Did I? I hope it was a good joke.
You said the word spoons and laughed for a full minute.
I had a dream that you were a baker, {other}.
Was I any good?
No. But you were over the moon about it.
Last night I dreamed of a house with a room I had never noticed.
Everybody has that dream.
Mine had a piano in it, and my own handwriting on the walls.
Then yours was better than everybody's.
Did you sleep?
I dreamed I was carrying the stove up a staircase all night. I am tired in two worlds.
I dreamed I could breathe underwater and was very smug about it.
That sounds like you awake as well.
I dreamed my grandmother was cross with me about a spoon.
What spoon?
I do not know. She knew. That was the frightening part.
In my dream I could fly, but only about a metre off the ground.
So you were walking, but smug.
That is the whole dream, yes.
I dreamed {leader} was a lighthouse.
Still leading the way?
Standing very still and blinking. So, not much of a change.
Do not put your hat on the bed.
Why not?
I do not know. But my mother would know, from four hundred kilometres away.
You still carry that button?
It is from the coat I wore the day I survived something. It stays.
Never thank somebody for salt. It is bad luck.
So I simply take it and stare at you?
Stare warmly. That is permitted.
You knocked on the wooden spoon again.
There was no table. The spoon is wood. The rules are flexible.
A black cat crossed the road this morning.
Left to right or right to left?
Does that matter?
Enormously. Neither of us knows which way is the bad one.
I keep a coin in my boot for luck.
Which boot?
The left. The right one has a hole and the luck would fall out.
You will not start a journey on a Tuesday.
Nothing good ever started on a Tuesday. Name one thing.
We met on a Tuesday.
Then I rest my case.
Do not whistle indoors. You will whistle the money away.
We have no money to whistle away, {name}.
Then I am protecting the money we will have.
You wear that ring on the wrong hand.
It was my grandfather's. He wore it on the wrong hand too. It is a family error.
I wrote a postcard to my sister and then forgot which town I posted it from.
She will work it out from the stamp. Sisters always do.
Who are you writing to?
Nobody yet. I write the letter first and decide who deserves it afterwards.
I bought a postcard of a castle we never actually saw.
Send it anyway. Let them think we are cultured.
A letter from home took six weeks to find me.
What did it say?
That the cat is fat and the roof is fine. Six weeks well spent.
How do you end a letter when you do not know when you will see them?
With the weather. Everybody understands the weather.
I have kept every letter anybody ever sent me.
How many have you got?
Nine. It is a small box. It goes everywhere.
A stamp home costs {gold} now.
For that money the letter ought to deliver itself and stay for dinner.
I started a letter to you once, and then remembered you were standing next to me.
What did it say?
Dear {other}, you are standing next to me. I got no further.
Postcards are better than letters. Nobody expects you to be honest on a postcard.
Wish you were here.
Exactly. Four words, and three of them are polite fiction.
I found a grey hair this morning.
Just the one?
Just the one I am admitting to.
When we are old, I want a bench somewhere with a view of a road.
So you can watch other people walk it.
So I can criticise their boots.
My knees have started forecasting the weather.
Mine forecast stairs. They are always right.
Will you be a nice old person or a difficult one?
Difficult, but with excellent biscuits. People forgive a lot for biscuits.
My grandfather lived to ninety-four on bread, wine and spite.
Which part do you think did it?
The spite. The other two were only keeping it company.
I used to think forty was ancient.
And now?
Now I think forty is somebody who still has good knees.
When you are old, will you tell people about all this?
Only the parts where I look brave. It will be a short story.
I am getting reading glasses in the next town.
You have held the map at arm's length since the spring, {name}.
I was admiring it from a distance.
You were admiring it from another postcode.
I want to grow old somewhere with a lemon tree.
You would talk to it every morning.
Somebody has to. Lemon trees are very lonely.
{leader} will be the old one shouting directions at the bus driver.
And the bus driver will listen, which is the worst part.
I want to learn to swim properly. Not that paddling thing I do.
That paddling thing has saved your life twice. Show it some respect.
Teach me to read the stars.
Start with one. Find it every night for a week. Then we talk about a second.
Before I die I will learn to dance something properly.
Which dance?
Any dance where my feet know what my hands are doing.
I would like to learn another language. A whole one.
Which?
Something with a lot of words for rain, so I can complain accurately.
You could teach me to fix the camper engine.
I could. Then whenever it broke you would have opinions.
I have opinions now.
Yes, but at present they are uninformed and I can ignore them.
I want to learn to sew properly. My mending looks like an accident.
It holds, {name}. That is all a mend has to do.
It holds like a grudge. Nobody is happy about it.
I bought a book on mushrooms, to learn them.
And?
I now know eleven ways to die in a wood. It has been very educational.
Who taught you to tie knots like that?
A fisherman who never caught anything. He had plenty of time to practise.
I wish I had learned the piano when there was a piano.
There is a piano in every second inn, {name}.
Yes, and a landlord standing next to it.
I want to learn to cook one thing perfectly. Just one.
Then make it eggs. Eggs are always there and they never lie about how you did.
I want to learn the names of the birds before I get old.
Start with the one that wakes us at four. I would like to know whom to blame.
{gold} left until the end of the month, and I want to learn chess.
Chess is cheap. Losing to me every evening costs nothing at all.
I would like to learn to draw, so I could keep some of this.
Draw the camper first. It does not move and it will not complain about its nose.
You still write the date on the inside of your wrist every morning.
Out here the days run together. My wrist is the only calendar that does not get wet.
Do you still have the photograph of your mother's garden?
In the inside pocket. It has been rained on so often it looks like a garden in fog.
It suits it.
It does. She always said it looked best in bad weather.
The radio in the camper only works if somebody holds the aerial.
Then whoever wants the music holds the aerial. That is democracy.
You tie your bootlaces in a double knot and then a third for luck.
The third one is not for luck. It is for the hill outside the last town.
The heater only works if somebody kicks it.
It works if I kick it. When you kick it, it sulks.
Who moved the radio dial off the news?
Nobody. It drifts on every pothole.
Then this road has taken us to a farming report in Slovenian.
I want the top bunk tonight.
You said the top bunk was a coffin with a view.
I have come round to the view.
The camper makes a new noise. Left side, behind the sink.
That is not new. That is the old noise, louder.
Is that better or worse?
It means it trusts us enough to complain.
The water tank is empty again, {other}.
Then somebody had a long shower and it was not me.
I will not be cross-examined in my own camper.
There is a sock in the glovebox.
It has been there since autumn. It is a resident now.
Whoever folded the table into a bed last night did it backwards.
It goes both ways.
It goes one way, and the other way is the one that ruined my back.
The fuel gauge says half.
The fuel gauge has said half since we bought it. Trust the smell instead.
Somebody in this camper snores, and I am too polite to say who.
You are too polite because it is you.
I spend half the night awake not snoring. I would know.
The windscreen wiper on your side has given up.
It gave up in the rain, which is a choice I respect.
We should name the camper.
It has a name. I call it that thing, mostly when it will not start.
If I had a fortune I would buy a house with a library and never answer the door.
You would answer it. You would want to know who it was.
Then I would answer it and be rude.
We have {gold}. What does that buy, these days?
Two nights somewhere modest, or one night somewhere that thinks it is not.
My father kept his savings in a biscuit tin.
So did mine. Then one Christmas somebody ate the biscuits and found the money.
Was it you?
I was eight and I bought a bicycle. I regret nothing.
Would you lend me money, if I asked?
Yes. Then I would mention it at every meal for a year.
Rich people never carry cash, have you noticed?
That is how they stay rich. Nobody can ask them for any.
I have counted the purse twice and it comes to {gold} both times.
Count it a third time. Sometimes it is generous on the third go.
If we won the lottery, would you keep travelling?
In a better camper. With a heater that does not need kicking.
So the same life with fewer bruises.
That is all anybody wants from money.
You tip far too much.
I waited tables for three summers. I tip what I was never given.
What is the most you ever spent on something stupid?
A coat. Purple. I wore it twice.
Where is it now?
Somebody in Graz is very warm and very purple.
I have started saving. A little, every week.
For what?
I do not know yet. That is the nice part.
The new euro coins have a different picture on the back in every country.
So the change in your pocket tells you where you have been.
Mine says I have been nowhere interesting.
The train was forty minutes late and they apologised for the inconvenience.
Forty minutes is not an inconvenience. It is a short holiday on a bench.
Did you see the evening news?
The man with the moustache read it as if it were his own bad week.
It might have been. He looked tired.
The payphone ate my coin and gave me a dial tone for it.
Then you bought a dial tone. Some people pay more for less.
Have you tried the Hypernet?
Once, in a library. A page took four minutes to load and it was about cats.
That is most of it, from what I hear.
There is an election somewhere every week now.
And the posters all promise the same thing in different lettering.
I bought a newspaper just for the crossword.
And read the front page anyway.
And now I am in a bad mood and the crossword is unfinished.
I have one roll of film left. Twenty four pictures.
Then do not waste them on me.
I already used six on you. You blinked in all of them.
Somebody at the station asked me for my Hypernet mail address.
What did you tell them?
That I had a postal one and it had worked fine for years.
The photo shop says our pictures will be ready Thursday.
We will be two countries away on Thursday.
Then somebody in that town is going to see a lot of you blinking.
Newspapers are thinner than they used to be.
There is less news, or less paper. I have never worked out which.
The weather man on the television promised sun.
He always promises sun. It is the only thing keeping him in work.
What game did you play most, as a child?
Hide and seek. I had a gift. Once nobody found me until supper.
That is not winning. That is being forgotten.
I was terrible at mathematics at school.
You count our money every night.
Badly. That is why it always comes out differently.
Did you have a teacher who frightened you?
One. She could hear a whisper at the back of the room from the corridor.
Mine threw chalk. He never missed.
I used to collect stickers for a football album.
Did you finish it?
One missing. A goalkeeper from Belgium. I still think about him sometimes.
Were you the clever one at school, or the loud one?
The one by the window, looking out at roads like this.
I fell out of a tree at nine and broke my arm.
Which tree?
That is your question? Not the arm?
Some trees deserve to be remembered.
We played marbles in the dust behind the church.
We played in the corridor until the headmaster slipped on one.
Was he all right?
He was never quite the same, and neither was the corridor.
I still know the capitals of every country in Europe.
Half of them have changed since you learned them.
Then I know the old ones. Somebody has to.
Did you ever get sent out of the classroom?
Every Tuesday. I had a regular spot in the corridor. People visited.
Skipping rope. I could do a hundred without a mistake.
Prove it at the next town.
My knees are not nine years old any more, {other}.
You stir your coffee anticlockwise.
It tastes different the other way.
It does not.
Then why have you started doing it too?
I cannot think until I have had a coffee.
I have noticed. Before the coffee you agreed to carry everything.
Shaving in a camper mirror is an act of faith.
So is watching you do it while we are moving.
Hand me the darning needle. Another heel has gone.
You walk on your heels like you are angry at them.
I am angry at them. They keep wearing through.
Every morning you check the sky before anything else.
Habit. My grandmother did it. She was never once wrong about rain.
You fold your shirts as if somebody is going to inspect them.
Somebody did, once, for two years. It does not leave you.
Why do you always wind your watch at exactly nine?
Because at ten I have forgotten, and at eleven it has stopped.
First coffee is mine. I have earned it.
Earned it by opening your eyes?
Have you ever watched me wake up? It is a battle.
You leave the cup by the sink every night. Never in it.
The sink is for things that are finished. That cup has a future.
I have sewn the same button back on this coat four times.
Then the button is telling you something.
It is telling me I sew badly. I knew that.
Do you always make the bed, even here?
Especially here. A made bed is the only thing in the day that goes to plan.
When my hair is white I want a bench with my name on it.
You want people sitting on you after you have gone?
I want to be remembered by somebody tired. That is a kind of honour.
What will you do when you are seventy?
Complain about the young, loudly, on trains.
You do that now.
Then I am ahead of schedule.
I would like a small house by water.
Sea or lake?
A lake. The sea is always going somewhere. I would like water that stays.
Promise me that when we are old you will not tell this story wrong.
I will tell it better. That is a different promise.
Do you think you will ever settle down?
Somewhere with a garden. Then I will spend all day looking at the road out of it.
In ten years I want to be able to sleep past six.
That is your whole ambition?
You have never slept in a camper beside a road full of lorries. It is a big ambition.
When I retire I will write a guidebook. Every bad inn from here to the coast.
Nobody will buy it.
Everybody will buy it. People love to know what to avoid.
Do you want children, one day?
I want to be the relative who turns up with presents and leaves before bedtime.
That is not having children. That is having an audience.
When we are old, will we still talk like this?
Slower. And with more pauses where we have forgotten the word.
So exactly like this, then.
My plan for old age is a rocking chair and a view of a car park.
Why a car park?
Something should happen, but not to me.
Five years from now, where are we?
Somewhere with chairs. That is as far as I can see.
I never wrote back to my brother.
It is not too late. There is a post office in every town.
There is a stamp in my pack. It has been there a year.
Do you regret leaving your job?
Every Friday, at about five, for one minute. Then it passes.
If you could go back and say one thing to somebody, who would it be?
A woman on a train in ninety-six. I let her carry her own case up the steps.
That is your great regret? A suitcase?
She was very old and I had too much pride. It stays with you.
I was unkind to you the week we met.
You were unkind to everybody that week. I did not take it personally.
Do you ever wish you had stayed?
Some mornings. Then I remember what staying looked like.
I got a second chance once and wasted it.
Then this is the third. Do not tell anyone, they are not usually handed out.
I should have learned to swim properly.
It is not too late.
It is too late for the river last month. That was my point.
Is there anybody you would apologise to, if you could find them?
A landlord in Lyon. I left through the window and owed him a month.
And now?
Now I would pay him and use the door.
We could have taken the other road, that time.
We could have. Then we would be complaining about that one instead.
I am trying to be less stubborn this year.
How is it going?
Very well. I refuse to hear otherwise.
You still owe me for the umbrella.
The umbrella that blew into the river in a breeze.
It was a gale and you were holding it wrong.
Tell the one about the goat.
No. You laugh for ten minutes and I have to walk next to you.
Do you remember the inn with the parrot?
Nobody could forget the inn with the parrot.
It still owes me an apology.
You have mispronounced that town every day for a week.
And every day it has stayed a town. No harm done.
{other}, the map. Which way up does it go?
You ask me that every morning.
And every morning you take too long to answer.
One day you will win at cards and I will have nothing left to say.
I won on Tuesday.
You won one hand. I am counting games.
You were going to learn to fold a map back properly.
I am learning. It is a very long course, and the map is not helping.
Tell me again about the time you nearly met a prince.
It was a duke, and I very nearly did.
You held a door open for his driver.
Very nearly, I said.
We are not lost.
Nobody said lost.
You were about to.
I was about to say scenic.
You promised you would stop collecting matchboxes.
I promised I would stop buying them. People keep giving them to me.
Let me guess. You knew a shortcut.
I knew the shortcut, {name}. The shortcut did not know me.
We had a dog called Professor when I was small.
Why Professor?
He looked at everything as if it had disappointed him.
Did you ever have a cat?
A cat had me, for six years. I was allowed to open the tins.
A goose chased me across a farmyard in Bavaria.
Did you win?
Nobody wins against a goose. You only reach the gate.
There was a horse on my uncle's farm that only liked me.
Lucky.
Not luck. I was the one carrying the apples.
That cat at the campsite followed you for a kilometre.
She had good taste.
She had smelled the sausage in your pocket.
I kept a hedgehog in a shoebox for a week as a child.
What happened to it?
My mother made me let it go. It left without looking back. Very hedgehog of it.
Do you think animals know when we are leaving a place?
The dogs do. The cats know and pretend not to care.
My grandfather kept pigeons on the roof.
Did they always come back?
Every one. He said it was the only loyalty he ever trusted.
The farmer's dog slept against the camper door last night.
Guarding us or keeping us in?
I did not ask. He seemed very sure of himself.
Cows stare at you as if you owe them an explanation.
Perhaps we do. We are walking through their kitchen.
What are you reading?
A detective novel. Somebody has died in a library and everybody is lying.
Sounds like a library.
You have been on page forty of that book for a month.
It is a very good page forty. I keep going back to it.
Do not tell me how it ends.
I would not. The ending is the worst part anyway.
Then why did you say so?
So you would stop expecting it to be good.
I borrowed this book from a library in Ghent.
When is it due back?
Last March. I think about the fine more than the book.
You read the last page first. I have seen you do it.
I like to know who survives before I get attached.
Is that book any good?
It is eight hundred pages about a family who never say what they mean.
So it is about us.
Shorter chapters, but yes.
I swapped my book for yours on the hostel shelf.
That was my book, {name}. I had not finished it.
You were on page forty. You were never going to finish it.
Read me a bit of yours while I drive.
It is about a lighthouse keeper who does nothing for three hundred pages.
Perfect. Read slowly.
There is a paperback in the camper with no cover and no first chapter.
I know. I have read it for weeks and I still do not know the hero's name.
Make one up.
I have. I call him {leader}.
battered: Nobody here is in a fit state to fight anything.
Then we do not fight. We sit down and we mend.
Look at us. All three of us, if we are counting.
I would rather not be counted just now.
We are one bad afternoon from being buried in a field.
Then let us have a good afternoon. For once.
Everyone is hurt. Not one of us is pretending otherwise any more.
That is the first honest thing said all day.
If something comes at us now, it takes us.
Then we stop. Here. Whatever it costs us in hours.
Say it. Somebody say it.
We are in a bad way and we need to stop.
Thank you.
Everybody sit down. All of you, now.
And then what?
And then we find out what we have left.
Count the bandages and say the number out loud.
Three. Three, and one of them has been used.
Then nobody takes a risk until the next town.
We cannot take another fight today. Not one.
Then we walk round whatever is next, however far round is.
Look at the state of the three of us.
I would rather not. I have been avoiding it since noon.
Somebody has to say we are in trouble.
We are in trouble.
Thank you. It is easier now it is out.
If anything finds us in the next hour it takes us.
Then we make sure nothing finds us. Off the road, under cover, no fire.
I can walk. I cannot fight, but I can walk.
That is all today asks of you.
Who is worst? Honestly, not bravely.
Not me. And that is all I am going to say about it.
We should have turned back at the bridge.
We should have. It is said. Now bind that arm.
The plan is to stop being hurt. That is the whole plan.
It is a good plan. It has no steps in it, but it is a good plan.
Nobody carries their own pack for the next hour.
There is nobody who can carry two.
Then we make two trips. It is that or leave things.
I have stopped feeling the worst one. Is that bad?
That is bad. Sit down and let me look.
We are one bad afternoon from a field with three graves in it.
Then let us have a good afternoon, for once, out of spite.
How far to anywhere with a roof?
Two hours at this pace. Three at the pace we are actually managing.
Everybody drink. Everybody. It is not optional.
There is not enough for everybody.
Then everybody drinks half and we find water.
I would like it noted that we survived that.
It is noted. Now stop talking and let the bleeding stop.
Do we tell anyone what happened?
We tell nobody. A hurt party is a party people follow.
Nothing is broken. Everything hurts. There is a difference.
There is, and it is the only good news of the day.
I am not being brave, I am being slow.
That is allowed. Slow gets there.
We stop here. Whatever it costs in hours.
Agreed. Nobody argues. That is the first thing all day we all agree on.
Nobody is walking point in this state.
Then we all walk slowly in a line and hope. That is the plan.
I have used the last of the bandages.
Then we use shirts, and we find a town tomorrow whatever it costs.
Say what we do if somebody cannot get up in the morning.
Then we do not go in the morning. That is the whole answer.
Nobody carries their own pack for the next hour.
Then we make two trips. It is that or leave things.
needAll: Hungry, filthy, and none of us has slept. Have I missed anything?

There was a postcard of your home town in the last shop.
