It has been in your coat pocket since Tuesday.
The scarf is a loan. Give it back in spring.
And if I do not?
Then it was a gift, and I will pretend I meant it.
Remember the goat at the border?
Do not start. I will laugh and wake the whole camp.
I patched the hole in your sleeping bag.
So that is why I slept through the night. Thank you, {name}.
Lean on me for the hill.
Only for the hill. Do not tell anyone.
I kept the last of the chocolate. Half each.
You broke it so my half is bigger. I can see it.
Take the window seat in the camper.
You always say that, and then you always mean it.
I did the washing. Yours too.
You folded my socks into pairs. Nobody has done that since I was a child.
Quiet now. Let the others sleep a little longer.
Then we will have the sunrise to ourselves.
Write to your mother. I will post it at the next town.
You remembered she worries.
You talk about her every time it rains.
I told the innkeeper you were a famous poet.
Whatever for?
We got the good room. Recite something if he asks.
I will recite your debts.
Your hands are shaking.
It was close today. Closer than I said.
I know. I was there. Give me your hands.
I found a cassette of those old songs you hum.
Now I will have to hum them in tune. Thank you, {name}.
Supper is mine tonight. That is {gold} you get to keep.
You paid last time.
And I will pay next time. Stop counting.
Fine. But I am still counting.
sore: You've been slowing us down lately.
Not everyone can be perfect like you think you are.
I'm just saying we need to stay focused...
You went through my pack?!
I was looking for healing items. Relax.
That's my private stuff! You had no right!
Fine. Next time I'll let you bleed out.
This is just like that time in the caves.
Are you seriously bringing that up again?
You never apologized!
Because it wasn't my fault!
You spent HOW much at the tavern?!
I needed information. It was necessary.
You needed ale is what you needed!
Don't lecture me about money.
That was MY portion of the rations!
You had yours this morning.
That was yesterday! Are you even paying attention?
Don't take that tone with me.
Your snoring kept me up all night!
I don't snore!
You sound like a dragon with a cold!
Well, your tossing and turning kept ME awake!
When's the last time you bathed?
I've been busy, alright?
That's no excuse to smell like a troll!
You're one to talk!
Why did you take the better weapon?
I found it. Finders keepers.
We're supposed to share equally!
Then find your own next time.
I cannot stand how you eat.
I cannot stand how you breathe, so we are even.
That does not even make sense.
Neither does complaining about someone eating.
You left the fire to go out.
I fell asleep.
We all fell asleep. I am the one who woke up cold.
Stop walking ahead. I cannot watch your back from behind it.
Then keep up.
That is not the point and you know it.
The purse is lighter than it should be.
Are you accusing me?
I am asking. There are three of us and one purse.
You drank the last of the water.
There was a mouthful left.
There was my mouthful left.
Do not use my knife for that.
It was the sharpest one there.
It is the sharpest one because I am the one who sharpens it.
You have not taken a watch in four nights.
Nobody asked me to.
Nobody should have to ask.
Wash the pot when you are done with it.
I will get to it.
You said that yesterday and I got to it instead.
Every time we make camp you vanish for an hour.
I need an hour to myself.
Then say so, instead of leaving me to search the treeline.
Whose turn is the washing up?
Yours. It is on the list.
You wrote the list.
And you agreed to it, in writing.
Where is my comb?
Three towns back, I think. I will buy you another.
You hum when you pack.
I hum when I am happy.
Then be happy more quietly.
We said we would leave at dawn.
It is nearly dawn.
It is nearly lunch.
You told {leader} about the map.
I said it was a little torn.
You said I sat on it.
Somebody has been reading my diary.
Nobody would want to. It is mostly weather.
You owe me {gold}.
I owe you nothing. You owe me a pair of bootlaces.
Bootlaces do not cost {gold}.
Stop cracking your knuckles.
Stop listening to my knuckles.
You ate the pickled eggs.
One. I ate one.
There were six this morning.
You lent my rain cape to a stranger.
She was soaked. You were dry.
I was dry then. Look at me now.
Your travel clock went off at four.
It does not know we changed country.
You always take the last match.
Somebody has to light the fire. I notice it is never you.
I asked you to buy bread, not a hat.
The hat was cheaper than it looked.
The hat is not edible.
You ran the camper battery flat with the radio.
It was the final.
The final of what?
It does not matter now. We lost.
Move your boots off my side.
There are no sides in a tent.
You laughed when I fell in the stream.
I pulled you out first. Then I laughed.
You took the credit for that bargain at the market.
I did the talking.
I did the haggling. You did the nodding.
Why is my good shirt in your pack?
It was cold.
It is a shirt, not a blanket, and it is mine.
Late again.
I stopped for directions.
We have a map. You stopped for pastries.
There were directions on the bag.
You told me you could swim.
I said I could float. You never asked the important part.
road: Do you ever wonder why we're really doing this?
Sometimes. But dwelling on it won't change anything.
I suppose you're right. Just thinking out loud.
It's your turn to cook tonight.
Already? Feels like I just cooked yesterday.
That was three days ago.
Time really blurs, doesn't it?
Look, deer tracks.
Fresh ones too.
Means water's probably nearby.
Good observation.
How much further before we stop?
Until the light goes, if the ground stays like this.
Whose turn is it at the front?
Yours. It has been yours since the ford.
We should count what is left before we buy anything.
I counted this morning. It holds for three days.
Do you want to sleep near the fire or near the road?
The road. I would rather hear it coming.
I marked the map where we turned off.
Good. I could not have found that twice.
What do we do if the pass is closed?
We go around, and we complain about it for a week.
Wake me for the second watch.
I will wake you for the third. You did two last night.
Are we lost, or are we exploring?
The two words mean the same thing until supper.
Your boots or mine will go first, and I say mine.
Mine. Yours have another winter in them.
We have not talked about what happens when this is over.
No. And we are not going to, tonight.
Laundry in the next town. Everything I own smells of smoke.
Mine smells of you, which is worse.
Rope, lamp oil, plasters. What else?
Coffee. Without coffee the rest does not matter.
The left strap on your pack is fraying.
I saw. I will stitch it tonight.
Use the waxed thread, not the cotton.
You take first watch, I take the dark middle.
Then I owe you the dawn one tomorrow.
Valley road or ridge road?
Valley. It is longer, but the ridge has nothing to drink.
Valley, then. Tell {leader}.
What are we cooking?
Beans.
We had beans yesterday.
And we will have beans tomorrow, unless someone goes shopping.
Do we need a second pot?
Only if you want tea and soup at the same time.
I always want tea and soup at the same time.
Pack the heavy things low and close to your back.
I know how to pack.
Then why does your bag swing like a church bell?
How much is left in the purse?
{gold}, and that is before the camper wants fuel.
The tent pole bent in the wind.
Splint it with a peg and some tape. It will hold until town.
Spare socks drying on the line, or in your pocket?
Pocket. Last time the line blew into the river.
If we split up at the market, where do we meet?
The fountain. Every town has a fountain.
And if this one does not?
Then the bakery. Every town has one of those.
I want new boots before the mountains.
Buy them two towns early, so they are broken in.
Wake me if you hear anything bigger than a fox.
How do I know how big it is?
If you have to ask, wake me.
The lamp wick is nearly gone.
There is a spare in the tin with the matches.
There was a spare. I used it in the cellar.
Who has the train timetable?
{leader} does. Folded into a paper boat, last I saw.
Salt, soap, and a needle that is actually sharp.
Write it down. You will buy cheese and forget the lot.
Fill every bottle at the pump. The next one is a long way off.
How long?
Long enough that I am filling the cooking pot too.
Your turn to drive the camper.
I drove through the night.
You drove for an hour and stopped for a sausage.
It was a long sausage.
We should sell the old lantern.
It still works.
So does the new one, and we carry both.
Rain coming. Cover the firewood.
Already done. The boots are under the flap as well.
Cheaper to eat at the inn, or buy and cook?
Cook. The inn wanted {gold} for soup that tasted of the pot.
Grease the camper door before it wakes the whole valley.
I greased it yesterday.
Then it is squeaking out of spite.
You are holding the map upside down.
The road is upside down. I am holding it correctly.

driving: Whose turn is it to watch the road? Properly watch it.
Mine, apparently, since I am the one holding it.
I could sleep sitting up. I have proved it twice this week.
You snore sitting up. You proved that too.
Every mile in this thing is a mile we are not walking.
Say that again in an hour, when your back has an opinion.
Slow down for the corners. Just the corners.
I slow down for the ones that need it.
They all need it. That is the point I am making.
There is a noise. Under the floor, on the left.
There has been a noise under the floor since we bought it.
Then it is a noise we own. Wonderful.
Nothing out there for miles and we are still checking the mirrors.
That is why there is nothing out there. We check.
Do you want me to take over? Say yes before you have to.
Ask me at the next straight bit. I will have a better answer.
Anyone else find it strange, sitting still while the ground moves?
Give it a week. Then walking feels strange instead.
Pass me something to eat that does not need two hands.
Everything we have needs two hands. That is the state of the larder.
We should have named it. It has carried us far enough to deserve a name.
It has broken down far enough to deserve a worse one.
Keep it under eighty on this stretch.
I am under eighty. I have been under eighty for two hours and I am bored of it.
What happens at eighty-one, exactly?
The nearest bubble takes us and we live today again until somebody drives out fast.
Seventy-nine, then. Seventy-nine forever.
There is a bubble marked on the map at the next junction.
Marked when? Those markings are older than the bubbles.
Somebody watch the verge for the distortion.
You cannot see them until you are a few metres off. That is the whole problem.
If this thing had a liminal engine we would be there by now.
If this thing had a liminal engine it would be worth more than all of us.
Fantablack in the lining. That is what the black panels are.
Scraped off the Tower. Somebody scraped that off the Tower with a knife.
Whose turn is the map?
Nobody's. The map has been wrong since the second border.
Every road we take is technically the same road.
Do not start that. Not while I am driving.
Slow through the village. People live in it.
People live everywhere. That is what makes driving difficult.
There is a lorry behind us and it wants past.
Then let it past. Truckers know the road better than the map does.
Flash him. He has been good about the corners.
Done. He flashed back. That is the whole of trucker society, that exchange.
We are burning fuel to save days. I keep having to remind myself.
Then remind yourself out loud less often.
That was a checkpoint sign.
Then papers out and nobody be clever.
The heater works on one side only.
It has always worked on one side only. Swap seats and stop the campaign.
Can we have the window open?
We can have the window open and the map in the hedge. Choose.
I have not seen another vehicle in an hour.
Then either this road is very good or very bad. We will know shortly.
Somebody has painted over the milestones.
Border moved. Somebody always paints the milestones after a border moves.
What is that light on the panel?
It has been on since we bought it. It is decorative.
I could drive all night on a road like this.
You could not, and we have discussed it, and there is a rota.
Do you ever think about how far we have driven?
I think about how much of it was the same forty kilometres in different countries.
Pull in at the next place with a roof.
There has not been a roof for two hours. I have been looking.
The engine is happier at this speed.
The engine is not happy. It has simply stopped complaining in that one particular way.
Somebody has left a shrine at this bend.
Then somebody came off at this bend. Slow down.
I like driving at dusk. Everything is one colour.
You like driving at dusk because nobody can see how badly you take corners.
Watch that dog.
I have watched it. It has watched me. We have an understanding.
Road surface changes in about a kilometre. It gets bad.
How bad?
Bad enough that I am telling you now instead of then.
Two hundred kilometres to the border.
Say it in hours. Kilometres are optimism.
Somebody put a mattress on the roof of that car.
Somebody is moving house. In this year. That is either brave or forced.
The wipers are going and it is not raining.
Leave them. It is the only part of the dashboard that still enjoys its work.
Do we stop for that man waving?
No. Not out here, not on this road, not at this hour.
We have passed the same burned-out van twice.
Then either we have turned round or we should not talk about it.
I have run out of things to look at.
There is a whole country going past the window.
I have looked at that. It repeats.
Nobody has said anything for forty minutes.
That is the best forty minutes of the day, and you have ended it.
Tell me if you see a phone box.
Who are you going to call from a phone box?
Nobody. I would just like to know they still exist.
This is the furthest east any of us has driven.
Then somebody should be paying attention and it should not be the driver.
The tank gauge and the odometer disagree.
They have always disagreed. One of them is lying and I have never found out which.
Sit still. You are making the whole vehicle move.
I am making the whole vehicle interesting. There is a difference.
Do you want the radio?
Is there anything on it?
There is a man reading numbers. There is always a man reading numbers.
Keep both hands where I can see them.
I am driving. Where else would they be?
You would be surprised.
Keep it steady and we will make the border by dark.
Steady is all this thing does now.
What is that light on the panel?
Decorative. It has been on since we bought it.
transit: Somebody else driving. I do not know what to do with my hands.
Sit on them. That is what the rest of us are doing.
We paid for this and we are still sitting on our packs.
We paid for the distance. The seat was optimism.
Look at them all. Going somewhere ordinary, every one of them.
Do not stare. Ordinary people notice being looked at.
I cannot get comfortable and I refuse to stop trying.
You have tried four positions. There are not five.
It stops at every single halt on the line.
Then we sleep between them. Two minutes at a time is still sleep.
Strange, being carried. Nothing to do but arrive.
Enjoy it. Nothing carries us where we are going next.
Somebody else is doing the difficult part.
And doing it worse than any of us would. That is the price.
This carriage has been full since the border.
Then stand, and be pleased that the standing is not walking.
Nobody on here has looked at us twice.
That is the whole reason to pay for a seat.
Is this thing liminal?
Everything public is liminal now. That man got very rich making it so.
We are doing a hundred and forty and nothing is happening.
Nothing is happening because it is calibrated. Do not think about it further.
A day of walking in forty minutes.
And forty minutes of not being able to get off. Both are true.
The woman opposite has been reading the same page for an hour.
So have you been watching her. Stop.
I do not know what to do with my hands on a train.
Hold something. That is what luggage is for.
There is a trolley coming and it is going to be expensive.
Then look out of the window with great interest.
Everyone on this coach is going somewhere ordinary.
You do not know that. Half of them are looking at us thinking the same thing.
I have slept better on this seat than in the last three beds.
That says nothing good about the last three beds.
It stops at every halt on the line.
Then we sleep between them. Two minutes at a time is still sleep.
Where does the driver sleep?
The driver does not sleep. That is why the fare is what it is.
Somebody has left a newspaper. It is four days old.
Four days old is current. Take it.
We could have walked this in three days.
We would have walked this in six and you know it.
Do we tip the driver?
We thank the driver and we do not make ourselves memorable.
My pack has been on somebody's foot for twenty minutes.
Then move it before they say something and we are remembered.
I hate being carried.
You hate not deciding. It is not the same thing and it is worth examining.
The windows do not open on this one.
They are not meant to. Do you know what is outside at this speed?
Two children behind us have described their whole family.
And you have listened to all of it. So have I.
Is this the express or the other one?
It is whichever one stopped when we were standing there.
Everything smells of oil and other people.
It smells of getting somewhere. Breathe through it.
Somebody is going to ask where we are going.
Then somebody gets a true answer that explains nothing.
Somebody is going to ask where we are going.
Then they get an answer that is true and explains nothing.
cabin: It is smaller inside than it looks from outside.
Everything is. Including the plans we make in here.
Whose kit is this on my bunk?
It is the party's kit. It sleeps where there is room, same as us.
Rain on a roof you own is a completely different sound.
We do not own it. We are two payments from the road again.
First still evening in a week. Nobody move.
I was not going to. I cannot, actually. My legs have finished.
Do we talk about what happened out there, or do we not?
Not tonight. Tonight we sit inside and let it be behind us.
Someone should cook. I am saying it, not volunteering.
Noted, and ignored, and I will do it anyway.
Rain on a roof we are inside. I could weep.
Do not. It will be on your side by midnight.
Whose turn is it to cook in here?
Whoever is nearest the stove and least honest about it.
We are four people and this is two people wide.
Then be two of the people who do not move about.
I can hear all three of you breathing.
That is company. In a month you will miss it.
It is the first evening nobody has to stand a watch.
So sit down and stop pacing it out.
Somebody has left their kit on my bunk again.
That is party kit. It sleeps where there is room, same as us.
Do we talk about what happened, or do we not?
Not tonight. Tonight we are inside and it is behind us.
This lamp uses less oil than the lantern.
Then it is the lamp from now on and nobody argues.
The door does not shut properly.
It shuts. You have to lift it. Everything in here has a trick.
I want a night where nobody knocks on this.
Nobody knows we are here. That is what tonight is for.
It is warmer with all of us in it.
That is the only argument in favour of all of us being in it.
Somebody has stolen the good blanket.
Somebody is asleep under the good blanket and looks very peaceful.
Two payments and it is ours properly.
Two payments and something will break. That is the arrangement.
I have not taken my boots off inside in a week.
Take them off. That is an order from everybody's nose.
We could stay parked here for a week.
We could stay parked here for two days before somebody official arrives.
It is smaller inside than out and I do not understand how.
Everything is. Including the plans we make in here.
Play something. Anything with rules.
I have cards. They are damp and three of them are missing.
Whose is the coat on the hook? Nobody's coat is that good.
It came with the vehicle. Nobody has claimed it and nobody has worn it.
I can hear the engine cooling.
That is the best sound there is. It means today is finished.
Somebody should say something about how far we have come.
We have come far. There. It is said and it is not enough.
The window over the bunk leaks in a particular place.
Then move your head twenty centimetres and stop being a martyr.
Are we happy? Genuinely. As a group.
We are dry and fed and nobody is bleeding. Do not push it.
I will do the washing up if somebody else does the water.
That is not a division of labour. That is the whole of it in two halves.
I can hear the engine cooling.
That is the best sound there is. It means today is over.

ill: This {illness} has decided it lives here now.
Then it can start paying rent.
Do not stand so close. The {illness} is not fussy about who it visits.
I have shared a tent with you for a year, {name}. It has already met me.
I read about the {illness} in a pamphlet at the last chemist.
And?
I stopped reading at the word eventually.
Today the {illness} is only a two out of ten. Yesterday it was a nine.
Then today we walk slowly and call it a holiday.
I am fine. Stop looking at me like that, {other}.
You coughed up something with a colour, {name}.
It was a nice colour, at least.
Drink your tea.
Whoever gave me this {illness}, I hope they kept a little for themselves.
That is the fever talking.
The fever and I agree on most things lately.
I keep thinking the {illness} will get bored and leave.
Illnesses do not get bored. People do. Stay stubborn.
If the {illness} takes me out here, bury me somewhere with a view.
You are not dying. You are being dramatic in a blanket.
Both can be true.
My mother had a cure for everything. Onions, mostly.
We have onions.
Then I suppose I have no excuse.
The chemist said rest. As if rest were a place you could walk to.
It is. It is called stopping, {name}. Try it tonight.
I can hear my own chest when I breathe. It sounds like a kettle.
Then we stop at the next town and find a doctor.
And pay with what?
With whatever it costs. Do not argue with me today.
Tell the others the {illness} is getting better.
Is it?
No. But tell them anyway.
You have been carrying my pack since breakfast.
You have been carrying the {illness}. Seems fair, {name}.
Does the {illness} make everything taste of metal, or is it just this soup?
It is the soup. I made it. Do not blame the disease.
I dreamed the {illness} was a little man sitting on my chest, reading a newspaper.
Was it a good paper?
Racing results. He lost.
Sorry I am slowing us down.
We were never fast, {name}. Nobody has noticed the difference.
I have had the {illness} so long I have started to give it a personality.
What is it like?
Petty. Slow. Hates hills.
So it is you, then, {name}.
Keep your distance tonight, {other}. One of us with the {illness} is enough.
I will sleep on the far side. Shout if you need water.
wounded: My {part} has an opinion about every step.
Tell it to keep it to itself until the next bench.
Do not touch my {part}. Look at it, by all means. Do not touch it.
I was only going to check the splint, {name}.
Check it with your eyes.
I heard something go crack in my {part} and I have been pretending I did not.
That is not a plan, {name}. That is a hope with a limp.
How long does a {part} take to knit, do you think?
Longer than you will wait. Shorter than you fear.
You sound like a fortune teller, {other}.
I can still fight. Mostly.
Mostly is the word that worries me, {name}.
Remind me never to block an axe with my {part} again.
I reminded you before. You blocked it anyway.
The bandage on my {part} is too tight.
It is meant to be tight.
Then it is doing a wonderful job of it.
Carry my pack? Just to the crossroads. My {part} is singing.
Give it here. And stop calling the pain singing, {name}.
It has a tune. Mostly the same note.
If anyone asks, I fell off something heroic.
You fell off a stool in {place}, {name}.
A heroic stool.
The most heroic stool I have ever seen.
Sleep came twice last night and my {part} sent it away both times.
Take the soft side of the tent tonight. No arguing.
I keep forgetting it is hurt until I try to use it.
Then stop trying to use it, {name}. That is the whole cure.
The doctor said my {part} would be fine if I rested it.
And have you rested it?
Spiritually.
That does not count.
Do I look as bad as I feel?
Worse. But you walk like someone who has decided not to care.
I have decided. It is the only thing holding me up.
My {part} has swollen up like a loaf of bread.
Then we keep it well away from the bakers, {name}.
You did a good job with the splint, {other}.
I have had a lot of practice. Mostly on you, {name}.
Is it bad that I am starting to like the way my {part} predicts the rain?
Yes. But it is useful. Keep it.
Rain by evening, then.
I will fetch the tarp.
maimed: I still reach for things with a hand that is not there.
And I still hand them to you. We will both learn.
The new piece clicks when it is cold.
Then we will call it the weather clock, {name}.
It is not funny.
It is a little funny. You are smiling.
People stare in the market.
Let them. You were worth staring at before, {name}.
I used to be good at climbing.
You are still good at climbing. You are just slower and swear more.
The swearing was always there.
The fitter said the augment would feel like mine in a month.
And?
It feels like a rented one. Polite, but not mine.
Some mornings I forget, and then I remember. Every single morning.
Then every single morning I will be here when you remember.
Do not help me with the strap. I need to do it myself.
I was not going to help. I was going to watch and look supportive.
That is worse.
I know.
It aches where there is nothing left to ache.
The old soldiers in {place} called that the ghost. They said it fades.
Did they say when?
I am going to give the prosthetic a name.
Please do not.
Too late. It is called Gustavo.
You can stop walking on my bad side, {other}.
I am not walking here for you, {name}. The view is better.
I was afraid you would all leave me at the next town.
Nobody even suggested it, {name}. Not once.
Oil for the joint, oil for the boots. I am becoming a machine.
A machine that still eats all the cheese, {name}.
Funny thing. I am braver now. There is less left to lose.
Do not say it like that.
Then I will say it better tomorrow.
I learned to tie my laces again. One handed. It took a week.
I saw. I did not say anything.
I noticed you not saying anything. Thank you.
Does it bother you? Honestly.
It bothers me that it hurt you. The rest is just you, {name}.
The fitting rubs when we walk downhill.
Then we stop at the bottom and I find you some padding.
You are going to fuss.
Loudly, {name}. Get used to it.
craving: I can feel the {substance} calling from three streets away.
Then we walk the other three streets. I will come with you.
Just a little {substance}. A small one. To take the edge off.
The edge is how you know you are winning, {name}.
I hate it when you are wise.
My hands are shaking. Do not look.
I am looking at the road. Talk to me about anything else, {name}.
The weather, then. It is being dreadful.
Nine days without {substance}. Feels like ninety.
Nine is a real number. Ninety is just the craving lying to you.
Everyone in {place} seems to be having {substance} except me.
Everyone in {place} is not walking where you are walking.
Where am I walking?
Forward. Slowly. With me.
Keep the money tonight, {other}. Do not give it to me even if I ask nicely.
Especially if you ask nicely. I know your nice voice.
I dreamed about {substance} again. I woke up guilty for something I did not do.
Then you woke up clean. That is the part that counts.
I am not angry with you. I am angry with everything.
I know. Be angry. Just be angry here, with us.
Here is very boring.
Boring is safe, {name}. For tonight.
The worst part about {substance} is how reasonable it sounds.
It always has a good argument. That is how you know it is lying.
Could you hold on to my purse until morning?
Of course. And I will not ask why.
You know why.
If I slip, will you still walk with me?
If you slip, I pick you up and we keep walking. That is all it ever is.
Have you still got that ginger root?
Here. My aunt swore it beat any craving for {substance}.
Your aunt was a liar.
A kind one. Chew.
The smell of {substance} in that inn nearly had me.
I saw you leave. That was the bravest thing I have seen all week.
I nearly turned back.
Talk to me. Say anything. My head is loud.
Fine. Did you know {leader} snores in three different keys?
I did not. Keep going.
I used to think {substance} was the only thing that made me interesting.
You were interesting before, {name}. You were just tired.
I am still tired.
Some days the craving for {substance} is a whisper. Today it has a trumpet.
Then we make more noise than it. Sing badly with me.
drunk: I am not drunk. I am exactly the right amount of happy.
You called a lamppost madam, {name}.
She was very elegant.
Why is the road moving?
The road is not moving. Sit down before you join it.
I love you. I love all of you. Even {leader}.
Especially {leader}, an hour ago. You hugged them twice.
Tell me a secret, {other}. I will not remember it.
That is why I am not telling you one.
Somebody used to wait up for me. Before all this.
Do you want to talk about it?
No. Yes. Tomorrow. Ask me when I am sober and I will lie.
Water? Why would I want water?
Because tomorrow you will wish you had wanted it, {name}.
I am going to fight that sign.
The sign has not done anything to you.
It said {place}. Twice.
That is because you are seeing double.
Hold my hair if I am sick.
I always do. Hold on to the fence, {name}.
The stars are spinning. Make them stop.
I will have a word with them. Lie on your side.
You are a good friend, {other}. A good, blurry friend.
The last drink was a mistake. The four before it were very good decisions.
That is the most drunk sentence I have ever heard.
Why did nobody stop me?
We tried, {name}. You said you were celebrating Tuesday.
Is it Tuesday?
It is Friday.
I think I sang in that tavern.
You did. Nine verses of something with no tune.
They clapped, though.
Everyone is so far away and so loud.
Nobody is talking, {name}. That is your heart.
It is very dramatic, my heart.
I drink because the road is long, {other}.
The road is longer when you walk it sideways.
Do not tell the others I cried.
Nobody saw but me. And I have already forgotten.
Thank you. I am still going to cry a bit more.
Cry all you like. I will hold the lamp.
Which way are we sleeping tonight?
This way. Follow my voice and not the fence.
The fence seems more reliable.
high: The trees are breathing, {other}. Did you know the trees breathe?
They do. Not that loudly, {name}. Sit down by me.
I think I can hear colours.
What does the sky sound like?
Like somebody sighing in a church.
Who put the mushrooms in the stew?
You did, {name}. You said they were the friendly kind.
They are very friendly. Too friendly.
My hands are enormous. Look at them.
They are normal hands. Keep them out of the fire.
I have understood everything. The whole world. It is all one soup.
Write it down, then.
I cannot. The pen is laughing at me.
Of course it is.
Why is {leader} glowing?
{leader} is holding a lantern, {name}.
That powder from {place} was a mistake.
The man who sold it had no eyebrows. That was the clue.
I am frightened and I do not know of what.
Then hold my sleeve. It will pass. I will be right here when it does.
Promise?
Promise.
The smoke in that tent tasted like old magic.
It tasted like trouble. Drink some water, {name}.
Time has gone soft. Like butter.
It has been ten minutes. Sit.
Ten minutes is a very long butter.
Am I talking very loudly?
You are whispering everything. Very intensely.
That is the opposite of what I meant to do.
The {biome} has a face. It is watching us kindly.
Good. Let it watch while you lie down.
Never let me buy from a wizard at night again.
I said that last time, {name}.
I did not hear you. I was busy being a cloud.
Everything is very funny and nothing has happened.
That is how it starts. Then comes the sad part.
I do not want the sad part.
Nobody does. We will get through it with tea.
Can you tell the ground to hold still, {other}?
The ground is holding still. You are the one swaying.
I saw my grandmother in the fire. She told me to wear a coat.
Then wear a coat. She was not wrong.
She was never wrong. That is what is frightening.
pregnant: The baby kicked during the fight. I think it wanted to join in.
Tell it to wait its turn. About eighteen years.
I need to stop. Again. I am sorry.
Stop as often as you like, {name}. The road is not going anywhere.
I would kill for pickled herring and jam.
Together?
Do not judge me. Judge the baby.
What if it comes early, out here in the {biome}?
Then we manage. I have read the book twice.
Which book?
The one from the last town. It has pictures. Too many pictures.
Everyone keeps telling me to sit down.
Because you keep climbing things, {name}.
Do you think I will be any good at it? Being a parent.
You keep this lot alive on the road every day. You will be fine.
This lot does not cry at night.
{leader} does. Just quietly.
My feet are twice their size. I am walking on bread.
I will rub them tonight. Bread and all.
I keep thinking of names.
Anything good?
Not one. They all sound like innkeepers.
Sleep is a rumour. The baby has opinions about lying on the left.
Then lie on the right and I will tell you boring stories until it gives up.
I am frightened of the road now. I was never frightened before.
Being frightened is a sign you are paying attention, {name}.
I do not want to pay attention. I want a house.
Do not carry my pack. Well. Carry half.
I am carrying all of it. You are carrying enough already.
I cried at a sunrise this morning. A sunrise.
It was a very nice sunrise.
It was an ordinary one. That is the problem.
The midwife in {place} said to eat more greens.
Then we eat more greens. All of us. In solidarity.
You are going to regret saying that.
Feel. There. It is moving.
Oh. That is a whole person in there, {name}.
Half a person. The rest is soup and hope.
When it is born, it travels with us. I have decided.
Then we will need a smaller tent and a bigger patience.
We have neither.
We will find both by then.
Stop staring at my belly, {other}.
It is hard not to. It enters rooms before you do, {name}.
levelUp: Something clicked today. My hands knew what to do before I did.
I saw. You moved like you had done it a hundred times.
Level {level}, {other}. I counted.
Nobody counts that, {name}.
I count everything. It helps me sleep.
I learned a new trick. Want to see?
Is it dangerous?
Only for whoever is standing there.
Then I will stand over here, {name}.
My aim is steadier. I can feel it.
Good. Last week you shot a hat off a scarecrow by accident.
That was a very threatening scarecrow.
I feel taller. I am not taller, but I feel it.
You walk taller, {name}. That counts.
I think I finally understand what my old teacher kept shouting about.
Took you long enough.
Twelve years and a lot of bruises. Yes.
Level {level}. Does it show?
You stopped tripping on tree roots. It shows, {name}.
That fight felt slow. Not because it was easy. Because I was quick.
Do not let it go to your head. Let it go to your feet.
I can lift the full pack now without groaning.
Then you are carrying it tomorrow, {name}.
I walked into that one.
Being stronger is strange. I keep breaking door handles.
And a mug this morning.
The mug was cracked already.
It was not, {name}.
Did you see that? I did not even think about it.
I saw it. Do it again when it matters.
That is the thing. It will matter, and I will be ready.
Reached level {level} somewhere back on the road and nobody threw a party.
Here. A stale biscuit. Happy level {level}, {name}.
I feel like a new blade. Sharp, a little nervous.
Sharp is good. Nervous keeps you careful.
Then I will stay a little nervous.
My spells come easier now. Less like pulling teeth.
More like pulling smaller teeth?
Milk teeth. Very manageable.
I used to be afraid of the {biome}. Today I was only curious.
That is the best kind of getting stronger.
Do not tell anyone. It ruins the mystery.
Your secret is safe, {name}.
Teach me what you know next, {other}. I am ready for it now.
You are. That is new. I like it.
rich: We are carrying {gold}. I keep touching the pocket to check.
Stop touching it. Everyone in town now knows which pocket.
{gold}. I have never been this near so much money, and I do not like how it looks at me.
Money does not look at anyone. People look at the money.
That is worse. Thank you.
With {gold} we could buy the camper a new gearbox.
Or a whole new camper.
Do not say that where it can hear you.
I want a proper mattress. Not a good one. Just one that is not the ground.
Dream bigger. We are rich, for about a week.
{leader} has started walking like someone with a bank account.
It will pass. It always passes by the second shop.
We should split the {gold} into three pockets, just in case.
In case of what?
In case of everything we have ever met on this road.
I priced a decent sword in the last town. We could afford it now.
We could afford two. That is how people end up owning two swords.
My mother would faint if she saw {gold} in one purse.
Then do not show her. Send a postcard instead.
With what on it?
A nice view. Nothing about money.
Someone at the inn asked how we were doing. I said badly, out of habit.
Good. Keep saying it until the money is spent.
I keep doing sums in my head. {gold}, minus food, minus fuel, minus repairs.
And what is left?
Enough to worry about losing.
When I was small I thought rich people never had to walk anywhere.
And now?
Now I think they just walk in better shoes.
Keep me away from the market today.
Why?
I have {gold} in my head and no sense in it.
We have {gold}. We could actually pay back what we owe.
Pay it back? Who taught you that? It was not me.
I bought oranges. Real ones, from Spain. Nobody tell me what they cost.
I saw the stall. I will take it to my grave.
With {gold} we could stop for a month somewhere warm.
And then?
And then we would be poor somewhere warm.
Still sounds better than being poor here.
The thieves in {place} can smell a full purse.
Then we leave before they finish sniffing.
broke: We have {gold}. I counted it twice to make it more.
Did it work?
It went down by a coin. I dropped one.
{gold}. That is a loaf, a candle and an apology.
Skip the apology. We will need the candle.
I could sell my good knife.
You could, and then you would be broke with a worse knife.
We are down to {gold}.
I know. I have been walking past bakeries with my eyes shut.
When I was a child we ate soup made from the bones of the soup before.
That is not a recipe. That is a family history.
It got us through winters. It can get us through {place}.
There is work in the next town, they say.
They always say. It is never the kind that pays on the day.
Last time they paid us in eggs.
{gold} will not buy fuel for the camper.
Then the camper learns to walk like the rest of us.
I have started looking at the ground for dropped coins.
Found any?
A button. I am keeping it, out of principle.
Tell me honestly how long {gold} lasts.
Two days if we are careful. One if {leader} sees a pastry.
We could put on a show in the square. You sing, I hold the hat.
I do not sing.
Then they will pay us to stop.
That is still being paid.
Being poor is mostly arithmetic. I was never good at arithmetic.
Then you were always going to be good at being poor.
{gold}. The purse does not even jingle any more.
I miss the weight. It kept me from blowing away.
{gold}. My father earned more than that before breakfast, and spent it by lunch.
So it runs in the family.
Only the second half.
Do not look at the inn. We are not sleeping at the inn.
I was only looking. Looking is free.
In {place}, I would not be so sure.
We still have {gold} and a spare blanket. We could sell the blanket.
Then we would be broke and cold. One of those at a time, please.
{other}, lend me a coin for the payphone.
We have {gold} between us. Who are you calling, a bank?
We have been poorer than this.
When?
That winter in the mountains. We had one turnip and a debt.
And now we only have the debt.
I bought bread with the last of it. Do not be angry.
Angry? That is the best decision this party has made in a week.
holiday: It is {holiday}. Every shop in {place} has its shutters down.
And here we are, needing laces.
Back home we would be eating until we could not stand, on {holiday}.
Here we are, standing. Something has to give.
Lunch, I hope.
Do you celebrate {holiday}?
I celebrate any day the shops are shut and nobody asks me for money.
Families everywhere today. Prams, grandmothers, the lot.
And us, with packs and a map and a smell.
Speak for yourself.
I am speaking for all of us. Honestly.
Happy {holiday}.
Is it? Nobody told the road.
I wonder if they are setting the table at home for {holiday}.
They are. And they are leaving a chair for you, out of spite.
Out of love.
Out of both. That is what family is.
The bakery opened for an hour this morning for {holiday}. I got the last cake.
You ate the last cake.
I got it. What happened next is private.
Everyone has the day off but us.
We never have the day off. We just have days.
The church bells have been going since dawn.
It is {holiday}. They are allowed. We are the ones out of place.
I used to hate {holiday} as a child. All those relatives.
And now?
Now I would give a lot to be bored at that table.
A man in {place} just wished me a good {holiday} and gave me an orange.
Did you thank him?
I was too surprised. I will thank the orange instead.
Do monsters keep holidays, do you think?
If they do, they picked a poor one to skip.
No buses, no post, no market. {holiday} has shut the whole country.
Good. Nobody can sell us anything we do not need.
I meant to send a card for {holiday}.
Send it late. Late cards are the honest ones.
The square is full of music. We could stop for one song.
One song. Then we work.
Two songs.
Fine. Two, and you carry my pack.
Somewhere a family is arguing over the roast right now.
Lucky them. We argue over directions.
weekend: Weekend. Half the town is still in bed.
And the other half has a headache. We picked a good day to pass through.
People are washing their cars. Washing them. On purpose.
That is what a weekend is for, apparently.
When did you last have a weekend?
I had one once. I spent it moving house.
So, never.
So, never.
The market is on. It is always on at the weekend.
Then keep your hands in your pockets and your eyes on the cheese.
I remember weekends. Long breakfasts. The radio on. Nowhere to be.
Stop it. You will make me cry on a hill.
Children everywhere. Kites, bicycles, a football in every yard.
One of them asked me if I was a knight.
What did you say?
I said yes. It seemed rude not to.
Does the weekend count if you are walking through it?
It counts for the people watching us walk.
The fishermen are out on the bank. Every single one with a flask.
That is the real weekend. A flask and nobody asking anything.
My brother lives for the weekend. Football, a beer, a nap.
And you?
I live for the next stop. Different hobby.
Nobody in {place} is in a hurry today.
Except us. We stand out like a fire bell.
I used to work weekends at my uncle's shop.
So you have trained for this.
I have trained for disappointment. Close enough.
Weekend traffic. Every family in the country is on this road.
Going to the seaside, all of them. With the dog and the grandmother.
And a crate of wine in the boot.
Let us pretend it is a weekend for us too. One slow hour.
One hour. I am timing it.
The radio has stopped doing news and started doing requests.
Request something for us.
Like what?
Anything about walking. They will know.
Someone is mowing a lawn. That sound means weekend wherever you go.
It means rest to them. To me it means somebody else is working.
Shops shut early here at the weekend.
Then we buy now and complain later, as usual.
That is the whole philosophy of this party.
night: Still awake?
The fire keeps talking. I keep listening.
Look at that sky. You never see that many stars in a city.
You never see that many anything in a city. Except bills.
I cannot sleep when it is this quiet.
Then I will snore for you. A public service.
What time is it?
Late enough that it does not matter.
Early enough that it will matter tomorrow.
My grandmother used to say nothing good happens after midnight.
Then go to sleep and let nothing happen to someone else.
I will take first watch.
You took first watch last night.
I like first watch. Second watch is when the noises start.
Something is moving out there.
A fox. Or an owl. Or something we will meet in the morning.
That is not as comforting as you think.
It was not meant to comfort. It was meant to be accurate.
Tell me something. Anything. Keep me awake.
When I was eight I ran away from home. I got as far as the bakery.
Then what?
Then I had a bun and went back. I was never a great adventurer.
The fire is going down.
Let it. I want to see the embers. They are the best part.
Do you think {leader} is really asleep?
With one eye. That one never fully sleeps.
I keep thinking about everything I should have said today.
Say it tomorrow. Night thoughts are always longer than they need to be.
There is a light in a farmhouse over the hill. Someone else is awake.
A baby, maybe. Or a worrier like you.
We should wave.
From here? Go to sleep.
My feet hurt in a way I can hear.
Take your boots off.
If I take them off now, they are never going back on.
Nights in {biome} are colder than I was promised.
Nobody promised you anything. You promised yourself.
Is that a radio?
Somebody in {place} playing dance music at this hour.
Good for them. Somebody should be dancing.
I miss my bed. Not any bed. Mine, with the dip in the middle.
You will find another dip. The world is full of bad mattresses.
Tea?
At this hour? Yes. Obviously yes.
If I fall asleep mid sentence, finish it for me.
I always do. You never like how they end.
That is because you always end them with a moral.
dawn: The birds start before the light. Every time.
They have a schedule. Unlike us.
Morning. Is there coffee?
There is hot water and hope.
I will take both.
I love this hour. Nobody wants anything from you yet.
Give it twenty minutes. I will want breakfast.
Frost on the packs again.
And on my eyebrows. Do not laugh.
{leader} was up an hour ago. Folding things.
Folding what?
Everything. Even the map. Wrongly, but neatly.
Look at the mist over the {biome}. It looks like the ground is breathing.
It looks like the ground is cold. Same as me.
Did you sleep?
Some. I dreamed of a breakfast I will not be eating.
Was it good?
It had eggs. It was perfect.
First light always makes me think we could still turn back.
And by midday?
By midday it is too late, and too hot to argue.
The bakery in {place} opens at six. I can smell it from here.
Then why are we still standing here?
My father got up at five every day of his life.
Was he happy?
He was awake. In our family that counted.
Red sky this morning.
Shepherd's warning. Pack the oilcloth.
I do not talk before the sun is fully up.
You are talking now.
Under protest.
We should walk while it is cool.
We should, yes. My legs have not agreed yet.
The milk van just passed. The driver waved like he knew us.
Everyone is friendly at dawn. They have not had their day yet.
Up. Up. The road will not walk itself.
Five more minutes.
You have said that four times already.
And every one was worth it.
The world looks clean at this hour, like it has been rinsed.
Give it until noon. We will dirty it again.

rain: My socks have given up.
Mine gave up an hour ago. They are just along for the ride now.
I love the smell when rain starts.
And then it keeps going and you stop loving it.
Is your pack waterproof?
It was in the shop.
The shop was indoors.
We could shelter under that bridge.
With whoever is already under it?
I will knock first.
Rain on {place}. Every roof is singing.
Every gutter too. Mostly out of tune.
When I was little I would stand in the rain with my mouth open.
Please do not start again now.
The map is wet. The road has gone soft. {leader} has gone quiet.
That last one is the worst sign.
I keep thinking of a hot bath.
Stop. You are making the rain colder.
There is something nice about walking in the rain, if you stop fighting it.
When did you stop fighting it?
About ten minutes ago, when I lost.
My hair is going to be a disaster.
It was a disaster this morning. The rain is just helping.
The farmers will be pleased.
Good. Somebody should be.
They might even sell us something cheap.
Now I am pleased too.
Listen to it on the canvas tonight. Best sound in the world.
From inside, yes. From out here it is just wet.
Rain in {biome} smells different. Like iron and moss.
Everything wet smells like my old school to me.
Then you went to a very damp school.
Do you have a dry match?
I have a dry sense of humour. Nothing else.
My boots have filled up. I am walking in two small lakes.
Then you are the only one of us with a view.
We could wait it out in a café.
It will not stop.
Then we wait it out forever, with cake.
A strong plan. I have heard worse from you.
storm: That one was close.
Count the seconds. One, two.
Stop counting. I do not want to know.
Get away from the tall trees.
There are only tall trees here.
Then get away from the tallest.
My grandfather said thunder was the saints moving furniture.
They are rearranging the whole house tonight.
Do not hold that sword up.
I was not going to.
You were thinking about it. I could see it in your face.
I used to hide under the kitchen table in storms.
Did it help?
No. But my sister was under there too, so it was company.
The camper will rock all night in this.
Like a cradle.
Like a cradle somebody is very angry with.
Every flash, I see the whole {biome} for a second. Then nothing.
That is enough. I do not want to see it for longer.
The sky went green before it broke. Did you see?
I saw. I am pretending I did not.
Is it bad that I like storms?
Not bad. Just worrying in a travelling companion.
The power is out all over {place}.
Good. Candlelight makes everyone look kinder.
My ears are ringing.
That is the thunder. Or your conscience.
My conscience is quieter than that.
Not from where I stand.
We should have stopped an hour ago.
We should have stopped yesterday. Hindsight is very dry.
Somebody count us. Is everyone here?
Everyone. Wet, frightened and here.
The rain is going sideways now.
Then we walk sideways. Keep up.
When this passes, the air will smell of iron and clean stone.
When this passes, I will kiss the ground.
The ground will be mud.
I will kiss it anyway.
Do you think the monsters hide from this too?
The sensible ones. We should take notes.
snow: Snow. Real snow.
You say it like it is a present.
It is. It just comes with frostbite.
My fingers have stopped belonging to me.
Put them in your armpits. Dignity is a summer thing.
Everything is so quiet in snow. Even the road.
Even you, for once. I like it.
I used to build snowmen with my sister. She always gave them my nose.
Your nose?
A carrot, but she made sure I knew.
We are leaving tracks a child could follow.
So is everything chasing us. Fair is fair.
How do they keep the roads open in {place}?
Old men with shovels and opinions.
I cannot feel my feet.
Good. They were complaining all morning.
Look, the {biome} has gone white from end to end.
Beautiful.
Beautiful and very, very cold.
Most beautiful things are. That is the deal.
Hot wine. Somewhere in {place} there is hot wine.
And we will find it. That is the only plan now.
I keep slipping.
Walk like a penguin. Small steps, low pride.
Do you think it will settle?
It has settled. It has settled into my boots.
It is moving in.
My breath is freezing on my scarf.
Mine too. We are slowly turning into statues.
At least statues do not have to walk.
There is a sledge in that yard. Nobody is using it.
Do not even think about it.
Too late. I have thought about it twice.
The snow makes every town look like a postcard.
From the outside. Inside the postcard, the pipes have frozen.
When I was a child, a snow day meant no school.
Out here a snow day means the same road, slower.
Life is unfair.
Life is cold. Unfair is a separate complaint.
Shake your hood before you come in. Last time you brought half the hill inside.
That was a souvenir.
clear: Not a cloud. Not one.
Do not say it out loud. The sky listens.
Days like this make the whole trip worth it.
Days like this make me forget the other days. That is the trick.
I can see three villages from here. And a church. And a goat.
The goat is the best part.
I agree. A very confident goat.
Let us eat outside today. Bread, cheese, a view.
We eat outside every day.
Today it is on purpose.
The {biome} looks almost friendly in this light.
Almost. Keep your eyes open anyway.
I am going to get burnt.
Wear a hat.
Then I am going to get burnt in a hat.
On a day like this my father would take us to the lake.
Did you swim?
He swam. We watched him and ate all the sandwiches.
Clever children.
You are whistling.
Am I? Well. It is that kind of day.
Washing would dry in an hour today.
Then let us wash something. Starting with you.
You can see the mountains from {place} today. Usually they hide.
They are showing off. Let them.
Good walking weather.
Good everything weather. Even my knee is in a good mood.
Lie down in the grass with me for five minutes.
Five?
Fine. Ten. Do not tell {leader}.
I want to remember this day. The light, the road, all of it.
Then stop talking and look at it.
Somebody in that farmhouse is hanging out sheets. Look how white they are.
Laundry and blue sky. It is like a soap advert.
Clear skies tonight too. We will see every star.
And freeze under every one of them.
Is it wrong that I am happy for no reason?
It is suspicious.
I will take suspicious.
Then so will I. Just for today.

birthday: It is my birthday today. I almost forgot.
Happy birthday, {name}. I did not forget. I just had nothing to give.
{age} today.
Happy birthday, {name}. You do not look a day over tired.
That is the nicest thing you have said all year.
Nobody has to make a fuss. It is only a birthday.
Too late. I bought a cake in {place}.
A whole cake?
Half a cake. It was a long road back.
My mother always made a lemon tart on my birthday.
We have no lemons, {name}. But I have a song.
Please do not sing.
Too late. I have been practising since dawn.
Another year older, and still walking.
Still walking is the whole present. Happy birthday, {name}.
I wonder if anyone at home remembered.
They did. They always do. They just cannot reach you on a road.
A postcard would reach me.
Then send them one first and shame them.
Today I would like no monsters, no rain and something fried.
Happy birthday, {name}. Two out of three, maybe.
{age}. When did that happen?
Somewhere between here and the last town, I think.
I wanted to be somewhere special for my birthday.
You are in {place}.
I said special.
Do not tell the others it is my birthday.
I told them yesterday. You have a surprise coming. Act surprised.
Birthdays used to feel like a door opening.
And now?
Now they feel like a door I have to remember to close behind me.
What did we do on my last birthday?
This. Walking. Together.
Then this is a tradition now.
Happy birthday, {name}. Same time next year.
I made a birthday wish this morning, on the last star I could still see.
What did you wish?
If I tell you, it does not come true. You know the rules.
When I turned {age}, I always thought I would have a house by now.
You have a house. It is just in pieces, in our packs.
Somebody owes me a drink today. It is my birthday.
Me. Happy birthday, {name}. The first round is mine, even if it is water.
I am going to be completely spoiled today. That is my decision.
Agreed. You carry nothing and you choose dinner.
And I complain freely?
You do that anyway, {name}. Today it is official.
homesick: There is a bakery in {hometown} that opens at five. I swear I can smell it from here.
You can smell wet grass and our socks. Your memory is doing the rest.
Do you know what the river in {hometown} sounds like at night?
No.
Neither do I, anymore. That is what bothers me.
In {hometown} the old men argue on the same bench every afternoon.
About what?
Nothing. Football, the weather, each other. I would give a lot to hear it.
Some mornings I wake up and for a second I think I am in {hometown}.
And then?
And then I see your face, {other}. No offence.
Some taken.
This square looks a bit like the one in {hometown}. Same pigeons, same tired fountain.
Every square in Europe has the same tired fountain.
I miss the trams in {hometown}. Loud, late, always full.
You are describing a misery.
When we get to {hometown}, I am taking you to my aunt's kitchen.
Will she feed me?
She will feed you until you beg. Then she will feed you again.
Nobody here knows my name. In {hometown} I could not buy bread without three conversations.
And now you would give anything for one of them. I can tell.
I keep looking for {hometown} on the postcard racks. Never there.
Maybe it is not a postcard sort of town. Those are usually the best kind.
The bells in {hometown} ring a little out of tune. You only notice when they stop.
And here they have stopped.
Here they never started.
My street in {hometown} smells of coffee and wet stone after rain.
This one smells of mud and something dead.
Thank you, {other}. Very grounding.
It has been months since I last saw {hometown}.
It will still be there. Towns are patient.
Sometimes I think of the cafe on the corner and wonder who is sitting in my chair.
Probably someone with fewer blisters.
If you ever pass through {hometown}, do not eat at the station. Walk two streets in.
Why would I be there without you?
Fair. Then wait for me. I will show you the place.
The light here is wrong. Too flat. It does not do what the light at home did.
Light is light.
Spoken like someone who never saw an evening where I grew up.
I miss being bored somewhere I knew every corner of.
You are bored here.
Yes, but anonymously. It is not the same.
My mother still keeps my room in {hometown} exactly as I left it.
Unmade bed and all?
She made the bed. The only thing she changed. It hurts more than you would think.
Do you know what I would give for one plate of something from home?
Everything we have, by the sound of it.
Less. We do not have that much.
Fair point, {name}.
past: Back in my {job} days, I knew exactly what tomorrow looked like.
Now you barely know what this afternoon looks like. Welcome to the club.
{job}. That was me, once. Pressed shirt and everything.
Hard to picture, {name}.
It is hard for me too, and I was there.
The {job} work paid badly, but it paid on Fridays.
We get paid when something stops trying to kill us.
Twelve years of {job} work and not one of them prepared me for a goblin.
Nothing prepares you for a goblin.
I still dream about the {job} shifts. Same faces, same clock on the wall.
Funny. Most people dream of escaping. You dream of clocking in.
Do you know what they gave me when I left the {job} post? A pen.
A good pen?
It ran out in a week. Very honest gift, in hindsight.
People hear {job} and assume I had a boring life.
Did you?
Deeply. And I was very good at it.
That I believe, {name}.
My hands still do the {job} motions when I get nervous.
I had noticed. I thought it was a spell.
If this falls apart, I suppose I could go back to {job} work.
Would they take you?
After what I have seen? I would have too much experience for everything.
The road was never for me. I had a desk, a radio and a pension waiting.
And yet here you are, outwalking all of us.
The thing about {job} work is that nobody notices you until something goes wrong.
Same out here.
Yes, but out here when it goes wrong it has teeth.
My old boss would not recognise me.
Is that good?
He never recognised me when I was there either. So, consistent.
I kept my {job} badge. It is at the bottom of my pack.
Why?
In case somebody asks me who I am and I have forgotten.
You know, the {job} trade teaches patience.
You have none.
I left the {job} life on a Tuesday. Did not even finish my coffee.
Regrets?
About the coffee, yes.
Before all this I had a routine. Same tram, same sandwich, same seat.
Sounds peaceful. You only notice that kind of thing once it is gone.
Do you think I would still be good at it? The {job} work, I mean.
Honestly? You would be terrifying at it now.
Good. I was never terrifying before.
When someone asks what I did before, I just say I travelled.
And the truth?
The truth involved forms. Many forms.
Then travel is the kinder answer, {name}.
family: I wrote my mother a letter in the last town. I did not post it.
Why not?
Because she would write back, and I would have to be somewhere for it to arrive.
My sister would hate this. Every single part of it.
And you love most of it. Just never tell her.
I called home from a payphone last week. My father answered.
What did he say?
He asked if I was eating. Then he passed me to my mother so she could ask the same.
My grandmother used to say a road is only a long way of getting home.
Wise woman.
She never left her village in eighty years. So, a theorist.
I bought a postcard for my brother three towns ago. It is still in my pocket.
Then it has seen more of Europe than he ever will.
Do your people know where you are, {other}?
Roughly. Do yours?
They know I am alive. I keep the details vague. It is kinder.
My father never said he was proud of me. He just mended my boots before I left.
That is saying it.
Every time a phone rings in a bar, I think it might be for me.
It never is.
No. But one day my mother will find a way.
My little cousin asked me to bring back a dragon.
We could manage a small one.

For luck?

Sounds like a fair trade, {name}.
My parents think I took a job abroad.
Technically you did.
My sister sends letters poste restante to towns we never reach.
So somewhere there is a pile of them waiting.

I miss arguing with my brother about nothing.
You argue with me about nothing.
You do not know where I hid his bicycle in nineteen ninety. It is not the same.
My mother packed me a jar of jam when I left. I still have not opened it.
Saving it?
If I open it, it is just jam. Closed, it is still her kitchen.

That is the hard part done.
No. The hard part is everything after it.
My grandmother would take one look at you, {other}, and start cooking.
Is that a threat?
It is the highest honour she gives. Also a threat.
sleepless: What day is it?
Thursday.
Are you sure? It feels like I have been awake for three of them.
I have not slept properly since the last town.
It shows, {name}.
I counted the stars last night. All of them. Twice.
And?

If I sit down I will sleep, and if I sleep I will not get up.
So keep walking.
Every time I closed my eyes, something made a noise.
That was me, I think.
Then I forgive you. But only after a nap.
My eyes feel like somebody filled them with sand.
Did you sleep at all?
I lay down. That is a different thing entirely.
I just agreed with you about something and I cannot remember what.

I would never. That is how I know I am exhausted.
I keep seeing things at the edge of my vision.
Real things?
That is the question, is it not?
Lie down for an hour, {name}. I will keep watch.

It is a very dedicated owl.
I tried to sleep sitting up. Then standing up. Then I gave up.
There is a bench right there.
Is it morning or evening?
Morning, {name}.
Already? I was just starting to feel tired.
I heard every snore you made last night, {other}.
I do not snore.
I have them catalogued. There are seven kinds.
I am too tired to be tired. I have come out the other side.
What is it like there?
Very bright. Everything hums.

If I drop my pack in the next hour, just leave it. And me.
We are not leaving you.

The weather?
Not that. That would finish me off.
wellRested: Good morning! What a morning! Look at that sky!
It is grey.
A magnificent grey!
I slept ten hours and I feel like I could fight a bear.
Please do not fight a bear.
Up you get, {other}! The road will not walk itself.
It has managed fine without your help so far.
I dreamed of nothing at all. Pure, perfect nothing.
That sounds lovely. I dreamed a wardrobe was chasing me.
I have already packed, made tea, and fixed that strap of yours.
It is barely light.
I know! Imagine what I can do by noon.
I would rather not, {name}.
Is it me, or are the birds singing better today?
It is you. They are the same birds.
I feel ten years younger. Maybe twelve.
Do not get carried away.
Eleven, then. Final offer.
That was the best bed I have had since I left home.
It was a haystack.
A very supportive haystack.
Shall we take the long way today? I feel like the long way.
Absolutely not.
Sleep is wonderful. Why does nobody talk about how wonderful it is?
Everybody talks about it. Constantly.
You look tired, {other}. Want me to carry something?
Do not be nice to me before breakfast. It is unsettling.
Guess who woke up before the rooster.
Was the rooster upset?
Visibly. I think I won.
I could walk to the coast today. Any coast. Pick one.
Can we pick the nearest bench instead?
Every joint works. Every single one. I checked.
Congratulations.
Thank you. It has been a while.
I am so rested I am being nice to everyone. Hello, {other}.
Hello. Please stop smiling like that.
I cannot. My face has decided.
I slept like a stone, {other}. A happy stone.
Stones are not happy.
You never asked them.
fed: That was a proper meal. With a plate. And a chair.
And a second helping, in your case.
I could forgive anybody anything right now.
Even me?
Do not push it. Ask me after the coffee.
I had forgotten food could be hot all the way through.
The stew was very hot.
My tongue will remember it fondly for a week.
Right. Now I can think again.
What were you doing before?
Being hungry. It takes up the whole head.
Was that soup or a small miracle?
Soup.
Then soup is a small miracle.
I feel like a person again. A full, slow, grateful person.
Can the person walk?
Not quickly. Give the person an hour.
That bread was still warm. I nearly wept.
You did weep a bit.
Over the soup. Different thing.
Of course, {name}.
If anything attacks us now, I am going to be very reasonable about it.
A full stomach makes you a diplomat.
Who knew the best cook in the region would be in a place like this?
{leader} knew. {leader} picked it.
Then {leader} chooses lunch from now on.
I am never eating trail biscuits again.
You will tomorrow.
My boots feel lighter. Is that possible?
Your mood is lighter. The boots are the same.
I asked for the recipe. She laughed at me.
Fair. You cook like a landslide.
Remember when we ate that thing from the tin with no label?
Do not bring that up now.
I only bring it up to appreciate this.
That was the kind of meal you tell people about.
Who would you tell?
Everyone. Strangers. The innkeeper, twice.
I am warm, I am full, and nobody is shouting. Is this what peace is?
Briefly.
Briefly is enough.
Thank you for paying, {other}.
I did not pay. I thought you did.
Then we should walk a little faster.
Calmly, {name}. Like people who have eaten well.
creed: My {creed} upbringing says we should be up at dawn.
And my {otherCreed} one says the dawn can wait.
That explains a great deal about you, {other}.
You {otherCreed} people fold your blankets so strangely.
We fold them correctly. You {creed} lot just roll them into sausages.
Do you pray before meals, {other}?
Not the way you {creed} folk do.
How, then?
Quickly. Before you finish yours.
I still say {creed} makes more sense than anything you believe.
And I say {otherCreed} has better songs.
That is not an argument.
It is the only one that wins at a campfire.
You light a candle every night. Is that {otherCreed}, or just you?
It is a dark-room thing. {otherCreed} simply approves.
In {creed} circles we would call this place a sign.
In {otherCreed} circles we call it a swamp.
Every time you talk about {otherCreed}, I learn something and disagree with it.
That is how I feel about your {creed} sermons.
Sermons? I was telling you about breakfast.
My {creed} grandmother would have liked you, {other}. Then tried to convert you.
My {otherCreed} uncle would have let her try. Then sold her a pamphlet.
How do you {otherCreed} people decide anything?
Slowly, with tea.
You nodded at that tree. Is that {otherCreed}?
Manners. It was there first.
We {creed} folk just walk past trees.
I know. The trees have noticed.
Honestly, the more I see of {otherCreed}, the less I mind it.
High praise, from someone raised on {creed}.
I do not understand how you sleep without a {creed} blessing.
On my side, mostly.
Your {otherCreed} habit of thanking the soup is growing on me.
The soup appreciates it.
My {creed} teachers would be horrified.
Then do not tell them. The soup will keep the secret.
We {creed} people do not haggle. It is undignified.
That is why you paid double for those boots.
Admit it. {creed} got us through that last mess.
{otherCreed} got us through. You were just loud nearby.
What does {otherCreed} say about walking in the rain?
That it builds character.
{creed} says it builds colds.
By my {creed} calendar, today is a day of rest.
Every third day is a day of rest on that calendar.
You {otherCreed} types always have an answer for everything.
And you {creed} types always have a question.
That is called curiosity.
It is called being awkward at dinner.
Before you ask, no, {creed} does not forbid card games.
Pity. I was hoping for an excuse to stop losing to you.
Sometimes I wonder if I would believe in {creed} if I had been born somewhere else.
Maybe you would be one of us, {name}. {otherCreed} through and through.
Do not wish that on me.
Too late. I have pictured it.
My {creed} teachers said people like you would be impossible to travel with.
And?
They were wrong. You are merely difficult.
Your {otherCreed} grace before dinner went on for ages.
Your {creed} grace was one word.
A very efficient word.
Spoken with your mouth full.

We had no clocks in the Fields. We had the light. I miss knowing the time by the light.
I wonder what the next town sells in its shop window. Something with buttons, I hope.
orc: Sun's hot. Good. Warms the tusks.
The goblin head hums. Like a radio in the next room. Can't turn it off.
Wonder if my old boss still has my mug. Big mug. Had to be.
Feet hurt. Not telling anyone. Orcs don't complain. Out loud.
Somebody keep watch. Fine. Me. Always me.
Half the Horde would love me. Half the town would hire me. I pick the town. Today.
Smells like rain. My bad knee agrees.
The goblin drums got louder. Somewhere up north, they're angry. Not my problem.
Mum said tusks are a gift. Dentists say otherwise.
Good road this. Flat. Honest. No surprises. Yet.
DA... no. No goblin words today. Human words. Nice ones.
Think I left the gas on in my flat. Two years ago. Probably fine.
I could eat a whole goose. I won't. Unless one offers.
Monk life taught me patience. I've forgotten most of it.
Every road ends somewhere. Hope this one ends at a pub.
Strange world. Gods in court, mages in charge, me in the middle. Fine.
Cars pass, they slow down to look at me. Then they speed up. Careful of the Rule of 80, mate.
My sword needs oiling. So do my elbows.
Nice bit of sky. Not too blue. Blue's for the Verden.
Haven't punched anything all day. Feels strange. Feels grown-up.
Wonder what the goblins in my head are singing about. Food, probably. Same as me.
I'm loyal. Loyal's simple. Simple's good.
Somebody's cooking onions nearby. That's a good somebody.
Tusk's chipped. Got it in a bar fight in Lyon. Won the fight. Lost the chip.
Quiet's nice. Don't get used to it.
When I was small, the goblin head scared me. Now it's just noise. Mostly.
My hands are too big for most things. Not for holding on.
Should write to Mum. I'll write to Mum. Tomorrow.
Long way yet. Good. Means more days with this lot.
Ever since 1992 the world's been wobbly. I just wobble with it.
Something's watching from the trees. Squirrel. Brave squirrel.
I miss bar work. Everyone tells you their problems. Nobody asks yours.
The goblin side wants to shout. The human side wants a nap. I'll do both later.
Wind's from the north. Smells of pine and somebody else's war.
My grandad fought goblins. My dad was one. Family dinners were tense.
Hm. Cloud shaped like a sausage. I'm hungry, aren't I.
Every town's got one person who crosses the street when I come. I wave at them.
Strong arms, soft heart. Don't tell anyone that one.
The road's teaching me something. I'll know what when it's done.
Can't hear the goblin head out here. Too many birds. Good birds.
Wonder if there's an orc bar in the next town. There's always one if you look.
Little one in the last village asked if my tusks hurt. Only when I laugh.
I'm not angry. I just look angry. Face came that way.
Feels like a fight's coming. Or a storm. Same smell.
Stretch. Crack. There. Back's back.
tourist: I wonder if the monument back home has a new wing yet. They were adding a room for kitchens.
Humans walk on the ground all day and never once think about gravity. Incredible trust.
Somewhere a television is on and I am missing it. This is the price of travel.
Thirty-nine years ago this sky was in a broadcast on its way to us. Or the broadcast was under it. Something like that.
I have been holding the camera so long my hand has its shape now. Good.
Nobody has asked me about Zeta Reticuli today. That is fine. Today is about them.
Somewhere up there is the mirror we tried to give you. Pieces of it, anyway. I am sorry about the pieces.
Note to self: humans say fine when it is not fine. Tested three times today.
I keep counting the party. Still all here. I count you the way you count sheep, but awake.
Every hedge here is different. Back home every hedge would be the same, if we had hedges.
I said thank you to a lamp post this morning. I stand by it.
The road is long. I like long things. Long roads, long films, long human stories about cousins.
If I fold space I get there sooner. If I walk I get there happier. Walking wins.
The Crimson Analyzers would want to open this whole country to see how it works. I want to sit in it.
I have learned to sigh. *sighs* Yes. It does help. Who knew.
Twelve photographs left on this roll. I must choose carefully. Everything wants to be one of them.
Things here fall down and stay down. On my ship things fall wherever I tell them. This is more honest.
A Pale Warper once told me, without speaking, that I talk too much. I said thank you. Out loud.
The humans in the advertisements are always running on beaches. I have not seen a single one doing it. Yet.
That bird has been following us. Or we are following it. Either way, we are a group now.
I tried to understand magic again. Still no. I will leave it to the humans. They are so good at it.
I wonder what my party will look like in the photographs in forty years. Exactly like this. Wonderful.
Humans keep their best stories for the evening. I am already waiting for the evening.
In 1975 we heard a song through the static and the whole home sphere stopped working for a week. I still hum it.
Nobody here is bleeding and somebody laughed at lunch. Five stars for today.
I keep a list of places to bring my family. The list is now just the word Earth, underlined.
I should write a postcard. Dear everyone. It is green here. Wish you were here. Will arrive in 2040.
The time bubbles are the most beautiful spacetime I have ever seen and also the most rude.
When I look up I think about the debris. When I look around I forget it. I prefer around.
I think I am getting a tan. No. I am still grey. Grey with ambition.
The others carry swords and spells. I carry a camera and a guidebook. We all have our weapons.
Today I learned the word cosy. I am using it on everything. This road is cosy.
Whoever invented the bench should be in the monument. Maybe they already are. I should check.
My people learned you existed from a radio. Now I am walking next to you. The radio would be proud.
A dog barked at me today. I barked back. We understood each other completely.
The weather report said sunny periods. I have been waiting for them all day like a guest at a party.
Every human I meet has a whole life behind them. It is like walking past thousands of programmes I have not seen.
Gravity here is set very sensibly. I would not change a thing. I checked.
I wonder if the people in this country know how lucky they are to have weather. I will tell them later.
Humming is better in a group. I have tried humming alone. It is just a noise.
If I had stayed home I would be watching this on a screen, thirty-nine years late. I am here instead. Live!
I must remember to buy a hat. Everyone in the costume dramas has a hat when things go wrong.
The ambassadors in 1999 told us to blend in. I am doing my best. I am very grey and very cheerful.
Somewhere a human is making soup. I can feel it. That is not psionics, that is hope.
I will never understand why the toast always lands on the buttered side. Gravity is my field and even I am stumped.
elf: Another sunset. I have seen around ninety thousand. This one is in my top thousand.
I should write to my sister. She is in Varlenia, and she will not reply until spring of next decade.
These mortals will be gone before my hair goes grey. I had better enjoy them now.
The Squishing is a crude business. Even the end of the world should have better manners.
A lark is singing a little sharp. I shall not correct it. I shall not. I shall not.
My bowstring needs waxing. My hair needs brushing. One of these is urgent.
How strange, to grow fond of people who will think of me as old long after they are.
I remember when this whole valley was forest. I also remember who cut it down, and I am patient.
Note to self: do not mention the eighteenth century at dinner. They all go quiet.
The Guild's pillars stopped ageing by sitting in a chair. Amateurs. We simply do it.
A falling leaf, a broken twig, a heron lifting off. The countryside is reciting for me.
They call it a long journey. I have had longer naps.
I wonder whether the falling bags in Varlenia ever stopped. My cousin swears they are decorative.
There is a cathedral in the next town I watched them build. Three generations. I brought sandwiches.
I could enchant my boots to stay clean. But then what would I complain about?
Every century somebody invents a faster way to arrive somewhere uglier.
My reflection in the camper window looks tired. Ridiculous. I am barely four hundred.
A good arrow is like a good sentence. Straight, light, and over before anyone objects.
I taught a prince to sing once. He became a general. I blame myself.
Eighty kilometres an hour, the Rule says. Who needs to go faster than a galloping stag?
The oak by the road is two hundred years old. A child. I want to tell it to stand up straight.
Mortal music is so short. Three minutes and it is gone. Then again, so is the rain.
Beauty is everywhere, if one has the time. I have nothing but time.
dwarf: Somewhere under these hills is a vein of something lovely. I can feel it in my teeth.
A good hammer is a promise. A good beard is a promise kept.
Must write to my mother. She keeps a grudge book too, and I am in it.
The tower they call Omega. Who poured the foundations, I wonder. Nobody, I suspect.
Rule of 80: nothing above eighty an hour. Good. Nothing worth building was ever built fast.
Varlenia appeared overnight. Nothing good was ever built overnight. Mark my words.
My feet are sore and my pack is heavy. Both are signs of an honest life.
I miss the sound of the hall: forty hammers, nobody in time, everybody happy.
Should have brought the small anvil. Always bring the small anvil.
