Twelve generations of smiths in my family, and here I am, walking.
That cloud looks like a pickaxe. A badly balanced one.
They say goblins share one head. Then one goblin owes me for all of them.
Beer, bread, a warm hearth, a hard problem. That is a full life.
Nobody in this party knows how to fold a map properly. It eats at me.
I could build a better road than this in a week. Two, with lunch.
The Mages' Guild says magic is an art. Magic is a craft. Ask anyone with calluses.
Ninety-two dimensions, and not one of them with a decent tavern on this road.
My beard caught a burr. I will be thinking about the burr for the rest of the day.
Patience is a stone virtue. I am made of stone, mostly. And beer.
I wonder if the old hall still has my name carved over the third bench.
Good walking weather. Better mining weather, but you take what you get.
A grudge is just a memory you polish. I polish mine every evening.
Squished world or not, iron is still iron. That comforts me.
dargos: Somewhere a man in a field is still explaining what he saw. Good.
Titania is cold enough to freeze a scream in mid air. I miss that. You could collect them.
I have been on this planet longer than its words. Still have not found a better hobby.
The Embassy has missed another summons. I am so proud of them.
The Tourists are probably filming something boring right now. Amateurs.
Thinking about crop circles. Not making one. Thinking. Mostly.
The Rule of 80. A whole planet that cannot go past eighty without falling into yesterday. And we are the joke?
Humans fold their socks. Every single day. I do not know what to do with that information.
Someone in the party snores in waltz time. I am composing around it.
Uranus rolls along on its side. So do I, now and then. Family trait.
If I stand very still, the birds start to think I am a post. Then I move. Then they think very hard about posts.
The best part of a prank is the week after. The telling. The not being believed.
I wonder what Zanfretta is doing tonight. I could find out. I will not. Probably.
The Squishing, they call it. Ninety-two dimensions pressed flat like a book someone sat on. Somebody up there has my sense of humour.
The others think I am resting. I am memorising their pockets.
Humans keep diaries so nobody can say it did not happen. Then nobody reads them. Lovely species.
Quiet. Too quiet. Somebody should do something about that. I volunteer.
The Guild has a whole drawer of reports about us. I have read it. I have added to it.
A cloud shaped like a cow. Coincidence. I was nowhere near it.
I tried being sincere once, in nineteen fifty-something. Nobody laughed. Never again.
Every human has one story nobody believes. My job is to give them a better one.
Long road. Long roads are where people start talking to themselves. I like to answer.
The Moon looks smug tonight. It has no right. It has never pulled a decent prank in its life.
Honesty is a fascinating human invention. Like the spoon. I use both ironically.
Somewhere in Genoa there is a night shift. There is always a night shift. How comforting.
Two hours lost here and there. Who even counts them? I do. I keep them in a jar.
The party trusts me with the map. I have not touched it. Imagine what they will think I did.
Varlenia appeared out of nowhere this January. Professional jealousy, I will admit it.
Thinking of home. Ice, ice, a crater, more ice. And the best view of Earth there is: from far away.
Nobody ever asks a Dargos how their day was. I would lie, but it would be nice to be asked.
The Hill business in sixty-one was the Tourists. Everyone assumes it was us. I never correct them.
I counted the stars on the way. One is missing. Not my fault. This time.
I wonder what the others dream about. I could check. That would be rude. I would love to be rude.
There is a farm over that hill with a very gullible dog. I can feel it.
What do humans want? Answers. What do I want? To watch them wanting.
The Mages' Guild calls us a threat. A threat. I have never been so flattered.
Patience is the secret. Plant the idea, wait twenty years, collect the newspaper clippings.
Every lamp on this road is slightly too bright. I approve. It makes people look up.
I am very relaxed right now. That should frighten everyone, and it does not. Disappointing.
There is a tower holding ninety-two dimensions together, and nobody can move it. Funniest architecture in the multiverse.
The trick is to leave one detail that nobody can explain. Just one. Then walk away.
I am not lost. I am conducting a survey of where we are not.
My feet are cold. Titania cold. Good. Feels like home.
Everyone asks what we want from Earth. Nothing. We already have the reaction. It is perfect.
If a tree falls in a forest and nobody believes it, that is my tree.
gnome: If I moved the camper's battery fifteen centimetres left, it would corner far better. I would bet my hat on it.
Three hundred and eight steps since the last bend. My legs say more. My legs exaggerate.
Note to self: invent a pocket that holds more pockets.
Everyone is tall again today. Consistency, at least, I respect.
The accounts are up to date. My heart feels lighter, and the rest of me was light already.
A bubble somewhere ahead, I can feel the air going sticky. Steady at seventy-nine, everyone.
Copper, tin, a pinch of zinc... the alloy in that bell must be lovely. I can hear it from here.
One day I shall build a liminal engine the size of a teacup. Bubba will weep.
I wonder what the moon would cost in euros, if it were cheese, at Swiss prices.
Being small is a strategy. Nobody aims low.
My pockets are perfectly organised and I still cannot find the tiny screwdriver. It is in the other trousers.
That cloud looks like a differential gear. No, it is not an obsession. A little one.
If magic gets less rational the more you study it, why does mine get more fun?
Mental tally: two rivers, one bridge, nine cows, and a goat I have doubts about.
Somewhere, a gnome is inventing something I wanted to invent. I can feel it. Hurry, brain.
Wind from the north-north-east, at a guess. A brisk eighteen kilometres an hour.
A well-oiled hinge is a small happiness. I have counted nine today.
I could live in a teapot, honestly. With a few modifications. The spout as a chimney.
Grandfather said never trust a machine you cannot hear. This road is very quiet. Hm.
I have revised our arrival time four times. Each revision more precise and less true.
Alchemy is cooking with ambition. Cooking is alchemy with lunch.
A princess, a pirate and an accountant walk into a tavern. Yes, that is my family reunion.
Little wheels turn faster. Very comforting, that, for a person with little legs.

any: Somebody made this by hand, and a long time ago.
That has been here longer than the road has.
Best not to touch it until somebody else has.
Worth something, maybe. Worth carrying, no.
I have seen one of these before. Somewhere worse.
Nobody has cleaned that in a lifetime.
Odd. Everything else here is falling down and that is not.
Whoever left that was in a hurry and did not come back.
That has been rained on for a decade and it is still standing.
There is a mark on it. Somebody's mark, not a maker's.
It is older than the road and it will outlast it.
Do not touch the writing. Names are heavier than they look.
Pre-Squishing work. Nothing built since holds a line like that.
Somebody has already been through this and left the useful part.
That was made to be seen from further away than this.
It has been moved and put back. Not quite straight.
The Foundation would catalogue that and then argue about it for a year.
There is a shape under the moss. Leave it for somebody with time.
Half of it is missing and the half that is left is the interesting half.
That would sell for a month of fuel and cost us a week to carry.
It has stopped being an object. It is scenery now.
Somebody has taken the metal off it and left the rest.
It has a hole in it that was made on purpose.
That was painted once. You can see it in the crack.
Nobody has walked round the back of that in years.
It is heavier than it looks. I have tried.
There is writing on the underside. Of course there is.
That was here before the road and it will be here after.
Somebody's initials, and a year, and nothing else.
It has been mended with wire by somebody in a hurry.
Leave it where it is. It is holding something up.
Whatever that was for, nobody does that any more.
It is worth nothing and I have looked at it for a full minute.
The frost has taken the face off it.
Somebody stacked those. That is not how they fall.
scholarly: The joinery is older than the rest of it by a century.
I should record this before we move on.
That joint is later than the frame. Two builders, two centuries.
There is a date on it if the light comes round.
I have seen that pattern in a Foundation index and nowhere else.
Somebody carved a spell name here and got the case wrong. That is why the wall is like that.
This is not local stone. It walked here.
Give me ten minutes and I will tell you who was wrong about this.
That is a leyline marker, or it is a very old joke.
Record it now. Memory rounds everything to the nearest story.
paranoid: Somebody left this here on purpose.
That was moved. Recently.
It is bait or it is a marker. Both mean somebody is nearby.
There is no dust on the top of it. Think about that.
Whoever put that there wanted it found from the road.
Do not pick it up. Things get picked up and then followed.
That is a sign, and signs mean an audience.
It is too convenient to be lying there.
No dust on the top of that. Think about it.
It has been moved and put back nearly right.
artistic: Somebody cared about this once. You can see the hand in it.
It is beautiful and nobody is looking at it.
The wear on it is better than the carving was.
That colour has taken sixty years to arrive at.
Whoever made this was showing off, and they were entitled to.
Look at how it sits in the light. That was not an accident.
It is broken in a way that improved it.
I would like to stand here until the shadow reaches the base.
Somebody put a pattern where nobody would look.
I would stand here until the shadow reaches the base.
mischievous: I wonder what happens if I move it.
Nobody would notice if this went missing.
I could tell somebody it is cursed and watch what happens.
That is worth more than the person who owns it thinks.
If I turn it round, how long before anyone says anything?
There is a way to open that and it is not the way it was designed.
I am going to touch it. I am simply going to.
Do not tell me not to. That makes it a project.
I could move it two inches and ruin somebody's week.
Nobody is watching that. I am only observing.
cautious: Leave it. Whatever it is, it has been left before.
Nothing that has sat that long is safe to move quickly.
Look at it from here. Here is far enough.
There is a reason nobody has taken that yet.
If it is a mechanism, it is a mechanism that still works.
Do not stand in front of it while you look at it.
nurturing: Somebody's, once. Somebody kept that clean for years.
There is a child's height marked on this. Twice.
Leave it as it is. It is not ours to tidy.
That was mended, carefully, by somebody with poor tools.
Whoever owned this was loved by somebody with a knife and patience.
It is a grave marker. Step round it.
cynical: Somebody will sell that to a museum and call it rescue.
It is worthless, which is why it is still here.
The Collective would put a price on that before it hit the ground.
Everything valuable in this dimension is already inventoried.
Leave it. The next party through will take it and be disappointed.
Nobody built that for us. Nobody builds anything for us.
adventurous: That came from somewhere further than we have been.
There is more of this. Things like that are never alone.
It fell from somewhere. Which means there is a somewhere above.
Somebody carried this a long way and stopped. Why here?
I want to know what it was part of.
That is a hinge. Hinges imply a door.
naguka: OLD THING. OLDER DAN ME GRAN-GRAN. MAYBE CITADEL OLD.
SHINY! ME TAKE? NO? ME LOOK HARD AT IT INSTEAD.
DIS GOT SKULL ON IT. SOMEBODY HERE HAB TASTE.
*SNIFFS IT* SMELL LIKE TALL-PINK. AN' DUST. AN' SADNESS.
ME NO TOUCH. LAST TIME ME TOUCH, IT BITE BACK.
WHO MADE DIS? SOMEBODY WIT MORE FINGERS DAN SENSE.
DIS LOOK LIKE CITADEL STONE. SAME LINES. SAME OLD QUIET.
ME WONDER IF IZ WORTH EUROS. EVERYTHING WORTH EUROS IF YOU SHOUT.
IZ STATUE OF PRIEST? NO? GOOD. ME NO BOW DEN.
SOMETHIN' LIVED HERE. LAID EGGS MAYBE. ME CHECK CORNERS.
BIG-HEAD-SONG GO QUIET NEAR DIS. NOT GOOD QUIET.
FUNNY SHAPE. LOOK LIKE COUNT GRISSNACK SIDEWAYS.
BLUE-COUZIN WOULD SAY IZ ANCIENT AN' MAGIC. ME SAY IZ ROCK.
OOH. ME LICK IT. *LICKS IT* ...ME REGRET.
DIS HAB BEEN IN RAIN LONG TIME. RAIN NO WIN YET. RESPECT.
SCRATCH MARKS. CLAWS. NOT MINE. ME CHECK ME CLAWS. NOT MINE.
IN DA DEEP WE HAB TONS OF DIS. UP HERE DEY PUT IT BEHIND GLASS.
IZ BROKEN. ME LIKE BROKEN THINGS. DEY STOP PRETENDIN'.
SOMEBODY WRITE ON IT. ME NO CAN READ. ME ADD ME OWN SCRIBBLE.
DIS PLACE TOO BRIGHT TA SEE PROPER. ME SQUINT. *SQUINTS*
DAT IZ GOOD STONE FOR SITTIN' ON EGGS. WARM. FLAT. PERFECT.
SOMETHIN' WATCHIN' FROM DERE. ME WATCH BACK. ME WIN.
HM. IZ USEFUL? IZ FOOD? IZ NEITHER. ME LOSE INTEREST.
DIS LOOK LIKE WHAT HIERONYMUS WOULD DRAW. ALL CIRCLES. ALL WRONG.
ME PUT ME EAR ON IT. IT HUM. OR ME HUM. HARD TA TELL.
TALL-PINKS MAKE SO MANY THINGS. NONE OF DEM SCREAM. WHY?
SPORE DUST? NO. JUST DUST. PHEW. ME NO BECOME BLUE TODAY.
SOMEBODY LEFT DIS IN HURRY. ME KNOW DAT FEELIN'. KOLA, 1970.
IZ PRETTY. ME NO SAY DAT OFTEN. DON'T REPEAT IT.
DIS WOULD LOOK BETTER UPSIDE DOWN. LIKE CITADEL. LIKE HOME.
verden: Someone made this by hand and was proud of it. You can see the pride in the corners.
How old, I wonder? Older than the road, younger than the hill.
Look at the lichen on it. Forty years at least. Lichen never lies about its age.
There are wires coming out of it. I very much want to know where they go.
A Naguka has been here. Only a Naguka scratches a skull that crooked.
In the Fields we would have let the ivy have it and called that a monument.
This was a machine once. It is sleeping now, I think, rather than dead.
I shall not touch it. Some things want only to be looked at.
There is a residue of old magic on it. Faint, like a smell in an empty room.
Pre-Squishing, surely. Things made after ninety-two do not sit this quietly.
Someone painted it blue once. A good colour. I may be biased.
It has a dial. Everything wonderful in this world has a dial.
The stone was cut by somebody patient. I would have liked to meet them.
Moss on the north side only. This world keeps its rules, at least.
How curious. It looks broken and yet I suspect it works perfectly.
I will make a little sketch of it. Do not wait for me, I draw quickly.
Whoever left this meant to come back. I hope they did.
Rust is only iron returning to the soil. Slowly, and without complaint.
There is writing on it in a language I do not know. That is rarer than you would think.
Seeds have got into the cracks. In a hundred years this will be a garden.
Oh, a coin slot. Of course there is a coin slot.
Strange. It hums when I stand close, and stops when I step away.
Nothing like this grew in the Green Fields. Nothing like this was ever built there either.
It has been mended three times, by three different hands. I can tell them apart.
The goblins would knock this over. I can feel one wanting to from here.
What a lovely thing to find by a road. Nobody planned it, and that is the charm.
It was useful once. It is beautiful now. That seems a fair retirement.
Careful, there is a bees' nest in the back of it. Leave them be. They were here first.
The paint says one thing and the shape says another. I trust the shape.
I shall remember this one. Some things are worth carrying only in the head.
orc: Old. Older than my gran. Maybe older than her temper.
Shiny. Not touching it. I touch, it breaks. History.
Somebody built this by hand. Good hands. Bigger than mine? No.
*sniffs it* Dust. Old smoke. A bit of sadness.
Worth money? Maybe. Worth carrying? Not on my back.
Goblin marks on that. Old ones. The head goes quiet when I look at them.
Library had a book about things like this. I dusted it. Never read it.
Hm. Could use it as a club. Could use most things as a club.
Pretty. Too pretty for this place. Somebody lost it, or hid it.
*knocks on it* Solid. My knuckles approve.
That's a skull carved in it. Somebody here had taste. Goblin taste.
Don't trust it. It looks like it's waiting for somebody stupid. Not me.
Rusty. Like me in the mornings.
Scratches on it. Claws or tusks. Not mine. I've got alibis.
Big. Finally something my size.
Writing on it. Can't read it. Can read 'danger' in any language though.
Looks like something from before the Squishing. Things were heavier then.
My mum had one like that. Smaller. Less cursed, hopefully.
Leave it. Some things want to stay where they are.
Somebody cared about this once. You can tell. It's been fixed three times.
Sharp edge. Good steel. Bad idea to lick it. Don't ask how I know.
OI, look at that! Sorry. Shouted. It's just very shiny.
I'd hang that in a bar. People would talk about it all night.
Smells like magic. Magic smells like burnt hair. Don't trust it.
Heavy. Lifted it anyway. Put it back. Nobody saw.
Huh. Whoever left this left in a hurry. Half a sandwich, too. Old one.
Carved by somebody patient. I respect patient. Never managed it.
It's humming. Or my head is. Hard to tell some days.
Nice. Not mine. Moving on.
Looks like a goblin made it and a human finished it. Like me.
tourist: Someone made this by hand. With fingers! I must photograph the fingerprints.
How old is this? Older than our first broadcast? Older than television itself? Thrilling.
*circles it slowly, camera raised* Do not move. Not you. The object.
My guidebook does not mention this. That makes it twice as exciting.
A Crimson Analyzer would open this up. I will only look at it very hard.
What is it for? Do not tell me. I want to have a theory first. My theory is: soup.
Look at the dust on it. Human dust. Every speck of it has a story.
I have seen one of these on a programme. It was being sold by a man in a bow tie, for a lot.
It is a little broken. Broken things are the most human things. Someone loved it hard.
The gravity around this is completely normal. I checked. I always check. It is a habit.
This deserves a plaque. Here stood a thing, and a Tourist looked at it, and was happy.
Is it valuable? To me, yes. To the market, I cannot tell. The market never asks me.
Do not touch it. Not because of danger. Because of respect. And also maybe danger.
The carving on it is beautiful. I do not know what it says. I will say it says welcome.
I want to send a photograph of this to the monument. It deserves to be in a display case.
*squints* Is this magic? It smells of magic. Or of old cupboard. Magic often smells of old cupboard.
Humans leave things all over the place and then other humans find them and get excited. I love this system.
It is the same colour as me. We are friends now.
A plain, ordinary thing. My favourite kind. Nobody photographs the ordinary things but me.
Look how the light sits on it. Light is the one thing my people understand, and even we are impressed.
Somebody wrote their initials here. I wonder if they are famous. I will assume they are.
This would look wonderful on a mantelpiece. I do not have a mantelpiece. I will get one.
Hmm. Not in my phrasebook. Not in my guidebook. Not on television. A true discovery!
I think this was here before the Squishing. It has that calm about it.
One photograph from the front, one from the side, one with a party member for scale. You. Stand there.
I could fold space around it and take it home. I will not. It lives here. It is a local.
Old. Lovely. Slightly sticky. Three things I will write on the back of the photograph.
Somebody built this to last, and it lasted. That is the most human sentence I know.
If this were on a quiz show I would know the answer. It is not, so I will just admire it.
Is it a relic? An antique? Junk? To me those are all the same word, and the word is treasure.
elf: Carved by someone with talent and no patience. I can tell where they got bored.
This is younger than I am. Most things are. It is still rather handsome.
The stone in this is cheap, but the setting is lovely. Somebody loved the person who wore it.
Look how the light falls on it. Whoever placed this understood the afternoon.
Hm. Dwarven work, if I am any judge. Sturdy. Joyless. Excellent.
I have seen this design before, in a palace that is no longer there. Nor is the king.
There is a little enchantment fading in it. Like a perfume left in an empty room.
Lichen of perhaps sixty years. A pleasant age. I remember being sixty, vaguely.
It is ugly. Honestly ugly. There is a kind of courage in that.
Do not touch it yet. Let me admire it from here first, the way it was meant to be seen.
A wild rose, growing through the rubble. That is the only correct way to ruin something.
Gold leaf, applied badly over good wood. Mortals so often hide the better thing.
My ears are twitching. Something in there is either alive or very old.
This would sell in Varlenia for a fortune, to people who would never look at it.
A tidy little thing. I approve, and I seldom approve.
dwarf: Hand-forged. See the hammer marks? Someone cared.
Cheap casting. Bubbles in the metal. Shameful.
That joinery is older than this country's flag.
Good stone. Limestone, I think. *licks it* Aye, limestone.
Someone patched this with glue. Glue! I could weep.
Dwarf work, this. You can tell by the tiny rune under the rim.
Not worth carrying. Worth remembering, though. I will copy the hinge.
This was built to last. It has lasted. Respect.
Rust on the bolts, but the frame is sound. Like most old folk.
Elf-made. All curves, no strength. Pretty, I grant them.
Who left this out in the rain? Somebody deserves a stern letter.
I could fix that in an afternoon. I will not, but I could.
Hm. Gnome work. Too many little gears doing the job of one big one.
Older than me, and I am older than I look under the beard.
Mark of a guild I do not know. That annoys me more than it should.
dargos: Old. Very old. I may have been here when it was new. I may have moved it.
Someone carved a face into this. I would have carved a second one, facing the wrong way.
Interesting. I will not touch it. I will just stare until it feels uncomfortable.
This would look wonderful in a field at three in the morning.
*taps it twice and listens, deeply unimpressed*
Humans made this to last. How optimistic. How very touching.
There is a scratch here that looks like writing. It is. It says I was here. In my handwriting.
Fascinating. Somebody will pay a fortune to argue about this one day.
Not ours. Too sensible. Ours would be upside down and humming.
I could take this. Put it on a roof in Genoa. No. Restraint. Look at me, restraining.
The Tourists would have photographed this from every angle. I prefer to just make it slightly crooked.
It is older than the road. I am older than the hill. Neither of us is impressed.
Hm. Someone tried to explain this with a plaque. Bless them.
Do not touch that. Not because it is dangerous. Because I want to see who does it first.
That has the shape of a thing somebody believed in. Look at the wear on the edges.
Very nice. I would add a second shadow.
This is the sort of thing a farmer finds and nobody believes. I approve on principle.
Someone left this here on purpose. I can tell. It is what I would have done.
*walks around it slowly, then walks around it the other way, just to be fair*
Worth nothing. Worth everything, if you tell the right story about it.
The Guild would put this in a glass case with a long label. I would put it on someone's pillow.
I have seen better on Titania. Frozen. And nobody could visit it. That was the joke.
Hm. A marking. Could be a star chart. Could be a shopping list. I hope it is both.
This has been here a long time and nobody has done anything interesting with it. Shame.
Lovely craftsmanship. I want to turn it round by ten degrees and watch the town lose its mind.
If this could talk, it would say it saw nothing. Clever object.
There are fingerprints here. Mostly human. One is not. I am not saying which.
It is humming. No, that is me. Now it is humming.
Hm. Somebody made this to be looked at. Very well. I am looking. I am not impressed yet.
The trick with old things is to look at them as if they owe you money.
gnome: Hand-forged rivets. Look at the heads, every one a little different. Somebody whistled while they made these.
Let me just get my loupe out. Ah. Yes. Oh, yes. Old, and lovely, and slightly cracked.
I would date it by the screws. Slotted, not crossed. Before the war, then. One of them.
It is a good deal taller than me, which tells us nothing, because so is everything.
There is a mechanism in there somewhere. I can hear it thinking about moving.
Someone kept accounts on this wall. Tally marks, four and a slash, over and over. Ninety-one days of something.
Measure it with me. One gnome, one gnome, one gnome and a hat. Three gnomes and a hat tall.
Verdigris. That is copper going green with age. It looks like it has been thinking for a century.
If I had built this, I would have hidden a little drawer underneath. Let me check. ...No drawer. Amateurs.
The stone was cut for longshanks hands. You can tell from the grip marks.
Do not touch it yet. I have not drawn it. Everything should be drawn before it is touched.
Old alchemy stains on the base. Somebody brewed something here and left in a hurry.
Look at the gear teeth on this. Hand filed, every one. My eyes are watering.
I would put it at around three hundred euros, or one very good afternoon of looking at it.
Oh, it is not broken. It is only waiting for the right small hands.

any: Five minutes. That is all I am asking of anyone.
My feet have earned this and they know it.
Do not tell the others I sat down.
Just resting my eyes. Keep walking around me.
This is the best seat in the country and it is a rock.
If I stand up now I will regret the whole afternoon.
Sitting is not stopping. Stopping is what happens next.
Somebody count to three hundred for me.
I am going to eat something and pretend it is a meal.
The ground is dry. That is a luxury and I intend to use it.
Ten minutes and I will lie about how long it was.
I have taken my boots off. This is a commitment.
The pack goes down and my whole spine says thank you.
Wake me before anyone notices I meant it.
This is the only part of the day I chose.
Nobody speak. I am busy doing nothing.
I could sleep here and be perfectly happy about the consequences.
One breath at a time until the legs come back.
Water, shade, and no opinions. Perfect.
If a hill can be a friend, this one is trying.
The pack goes down and my spine says thank you.
This is the only part of today I chose.
I could sleep here and accept every consequence.
My legs have gone somewhere and left a message.
Twelve minutes. I have been very precise about it.
naguka: SIT. SIT ON ROCK. ROCK IZ BEST CHAIR IN UP-WORLD.
*CURLS UP LIKE AN EGG* FIVE MINUTE. NO POKE.
ME FEET SMOKIN'. LET DEM COOL.
NAGUKA NO TIRED. NAGUKA JUST TESTIN' DA GROUND. IZ GOOD GROUND.
SHADE! FINALLY! SKY-LAMP NO SEE ME HERE.
ME SIT. ME HUM. ME NO THINK. BEST THREE THINGS.
WAKE ME FOR FOOD. ONLY FOR FOOD. OR FIGHT. FOOD FIRST.
DIS STONE IZ WARM. LIKE NEST STONE. ME COULD LAY HERE. NO. NOT NOW.
ME BOOTS OFF. EVERYBODY STAND UPWIND. DAT IZ WARNIN'.
LISTEN TA BIG-HEAD-SONG WHILE ME REST. KIN SAY HI. HI, KIN.
ME NO SLEEP. ME RESTIN' ME EYES. AN' ME EARS. AN' ME EVERYTHING.
GOOD SPOT. ME MARK IT. *SCRATCHES SYMBOL ON ROCK*
UP-WORLD GRASS IZ ITCHY. BUT SOFT. ME FORGIVE IT.
SIT DOWN WIT ME. NAGUKA SHARE ROCK. BIG HONOR.
ME BREATHE IN. ME BREATHE OUT. DAT IZ ENOUGH WORK FOR NOW.
DOWN HOME, WE REST UNDER CORE-SUN. HERE WE REST UNDER TREE. TREE IZ OKAY.
NOBODY TELL DA HORDE ME SAT DOWN. DEY THINK ME ALWAYS STOMPIN'.
ME COUNT CLOUDS AGAIN. STILL CHEATIN'. STILL MOVIN'.
AAAH. *STRETCHES UNTIL SOMETHING POPS*
SIT TOO LONG AN' MOSS GROW ON YOU. ME WANT DAT, ACTUALLY.
ME LEGS SHORT. DEY NEED MORE REST DAN PINK LEGS. IZ SCIENCE.
ME HUM JUNEHEM SLOW SONG. DEY ONLY HAB ONE. IZ NINE MINUTES.
REST GOOD. BETTER DAN FIGHT. NO TELL ANYBODY ME SAID DAT.
ME FACE PAINT NEED TOUCH UP. ME DO IT NOW. WHILE QUIET.
ME SNACK. TINY SNACK. *EATS A VERY LARGE SNACK*
DIS SPOT HAB GOOD ECHO. ME TEST IT. HOOO! ...HOOO!
ME DREAM WIT EYES OPEN. ME DREAM OF EGG-WARM STONES.
NO RUSH. WORLD NO GOIN' ANYWHERE. ME CHECK. IT STILL HERE.
ME LIE ON BACK AN' LOOK UP. NO CITY UP DERE. STILL WEIRD.
OKAY. RESTED. ME STRONG AGAIN. ME STRONG ALWAYS. BUT MORE.
verden: A pause. In the Fields we called it letting the roots catch up.
Do sit, all of you. The road will still be here, it is very loyal that way.
My feet and I are having a quiet conversation. They are winning.
Five minutes. I shall spend them looking at that cloud.
*sits down cross-legged and closes their eyes*
Rest is part of the walk, not a break from it. My teacher said so, and he was rarely wrong.
The grass is warm. I may grow roots if nobody calls me.
Let me sit a moment. I am slower than I look, and I look quite slow.
A rock, a bit of shade, and a view. What more did anyone ever need?
I shall rest my eyes. Not sleep. Verden do not sleep on duty. Much.
Sit with me. You need not talk. Sitting is enough.
The soil here is good. I can feel it through my trousers, which is an odd thing to admit.
I have taken off my boots. Forgive me, it is a gardener's habit.
Breathe. The road does not mind if we breathe.
A short rest, and then I will be twice the goblin I was.
There is a bird here who has opinions about us. Let us rest and hear them out.
I could sit here until the seasons change. I will settle for ten minutes.
Slowly, slowly. Even a spore pod takes four hundred days, and nobody calls it lazy.
I am resting and also listening to the goblins. They are having a much louder rest than we are.
This bench was put here for exactly this. Someone thought of us before we came.
Water first, then talk, then walking. That is the right order.
I like your world best when it is sitting still. It so rarely does.
My legs say thank you. My pack says nothing, being a pack.
A moment of stillness. We used to give a whole afternoon to it, at home.
I shall just close my eyes and count the bees. There are eleven. Twelve.
Let us not hurry. Hurrying is how things get dropped.
The sun on my face is different here, but it is still the sun, and still kind.
A good rest is a small spell. It costs nothing and mends a great deal.
Wake me if a train goes by. I would hate to miss a train.
Ah. That is better. Much better. I may even be civil again.
orc: Sit. Rock. Good rock. Best chair in Europe.
Five minutes. Nobody poke the orc.
Boots off. Feet out. Sorry about the smell.
Not tired. Just checking the ground's still here. It is.
Shade. Lovely shade. I'm not moving.
*leans back against a tree, which creaks*
Back aches. Carrying everyone's stuff does that.
Monks taught me to rest properly. Eyes shut, breathe, snore.
Wake me if there's food or a fight.
Ahh. That's better. Knees forgive me.
Nap time. Orcs nap like they fight. Hard.
Just resting the tusks. They're heavy, you know.
Sun on my face. Grass under me. Could stay forever. Won't.
*stretches until something in the shoulder pops*
Bit of a sit. A bit. Not a lot. Bit.
Goblin head's quiet when I rest. Maybe it rests too.
Don't tell the others I sat down first.
Water. Shade. Silence. Three best things.
My old sensei said rest is part of the fight. I'm fighting very hard right now.
Legs. Stop. Shh. There.
Sitting's underrated. Big folk know.
Feet up. Who cares what it's on.
*sits down heavily, and the bench complains*
Two minutes. Then I'll carry everyone again.
Let the world turn without me for a bit.
My shoulders have opinions. Letting them speak.
Breathe in. Breathe out. Don't think about lunch. Failed.
Good spot. Wall at my back, view of the road. Old habits.
Tired arms. Too many doors held open today.
Rest now. Grumble later.
tourist: A bench! The greatest human invention. I sit on it with honour.
Five minutes. My legs were built for low gravity and they are filing a complaint.
*sits down and immediately photographs the view from sitting height*
Resting is very human. I have been looking forward to doing it properly.
I could make myself weightless and float a little. But sitting in the grass is nicer. It tickles.
Do not wake me unless something wonderful happens. Which is often. So, wake me often.
This rock is the best seat in the country. I will mention it in my guidebook. Four stars.
Shade! Lovely, cool shade. Your sun is a little enthusiastic. Like me.
I am resting my eyes. All of the eye. It takes a while, they are big.
Ah. The ground is warm. Humans are so lucky with their ground.
In the films, this is where someone sits down and tells their life story. Anyone? No? I will wait.
I am not tired. I am savouring. There is a difference and I learned it yesterday.
*takes off a shoe, looks at it in wonder, puts it back on*
Let me sit here and listen to the countryside. It sounds like the quiet bit before the theme tune.
My people do not have a word for a nice sit-down. I am going to bring one home.
I sat down and a ladybird landed on me. I am not moving until it decides to leave.
Rest stop. I will write some postcards. They will be very late, but very sincere.
If anyone needs me, I am lying in the grass, looking at clouds and naming them after presenters.
My feet hurt. I am proud of it. This is earned human pain.
Ah, a nice sit. You know, back home we sit inside spheres. It is not the same as sitting by a ditch.
Let me just change the film while we rest. Do not let anything interesting happen for one minute.
Sitting quietly with friends. On television this is where the music swells. I can hear it.
Short rest. Long sigh. *sighs at length* I have been practising.
I could stay here for a week. On my world a week is nothing. Here a week is a whole adventure.
Everyone sit near me. I want a group photograph of us being tired.
The air smells of cut grass. I want to bottle it and sell it at the monument gift shop.
Is this what you call a breather? I am breathing. It is very good.
A Pale Warper would rest by folding the distance in half. I rest by sitting on it.
Do not tell my caste I sat down. Grey Wanderers are supposed to wander. I am wandering sitting.
Mmm. A breeze. Free of charge. Earth has the best extras.
elf: A rest. Let us sit beautifully, at least.
I could walk for three days without stopping. I choose not to. Choosing is the luxury.
Wake me if anything lovely happens. Only lovely things, mind.
*sits on a stone and arranges their cloak as if for a portrait*
Rest is not idleness. Ask any tree.
I shall brush my hair while you all catch your breath. It takes about as long.
A pause under an old elm. We are old friends. It does not remember me, but I do.
Mortals tire so quickly. It is rather endearing, like puppies.
Five minutes, you say. I once rested for a whole summer and called it a short break.
Lie back and look at the clouds. They are the slowest show in the world. My favourite.
My feet are not tired. My feet are bored. There is a difference.
Let us rest, and I shall hum something from before your great-grandparents were born.
The grass here is soft. I will allow it to hold me for a while.
A pause is a kind of poem. Short, if you insist.
Sit. Breathe. Notice something. That is all the advice I have gathered in four centuries.
dwarf: Sit. Boots off. Beard combed. Now the world may continue.
A flat rock, a warm sun. My ancestors would call this indecent luxury.
*lies back on the stone and sighs at it fondly*
Five minutes. Then I will be twice as stubborn as before.
I rest the way stone rests: completely, and for as long as I like.
Nobody talk. I am listening to the ground.
My knees are filing a complaint. I am hearing it now.
Pass the flask. Resting is thirsty work.
Even the best hammer gets set down between strikes.
Wake me if anyone finds a cave. Or a pub.
*unbraids the beard, rebraids it tighter, satisfied*
Ah. The ground is cool. The ground is always on my side.
I could sleep standing up, like my grandfather at weddings.
Rest now. The road has waited a thousand years, it can wait an hour.
Let the young ones run about. I am a mountain today.
dargos: Sitting down. Not because I am tired. Because I want you all to wonder why.
Five minutes. Count them for me. I will tell you that you counted wrong.
*lies flat on the grass and stares up as if expecting a lift home*
Resting. Do not watch me rest. Watching is my job.
Good rock. Cold. Almost Titania cold. I could get used to it.
I am closing my eyes. If anything moves, it was not me. If nothing moves, it was.
My legs are made for floating, not walking. Do not tell the others.
Shade. Lovely. The sky cannot see me here. Neither can my supervisor.
Just a moment. I am drafting tonight's mischief in my head.
Sit with me. No, do not. I like it better when you hover nearby, unsure.
Feet up. Thinking about nothing. Nothing is a delightful subject.
If I fall asleep and wake up somewhere else, do not worry. That is just Tuesday.
Even pranksters need a sit. Especially pranksters. The timing is exhausting.
*sits perfectly still, eyes open, for far too long*
Ah. Rest. The one human custom I adopted without irony.
My back aches. Humans built their roads for humans. Selfish.
A short break, and I will be as fit as a fiddle. Fiddles are never fit, but I like the phrase.
Let me sit here and look harmless. It takes concentration.
This bench has seen a lot of humans. Now it has seen me. Poor bench.
Breathing in. Breathing out. Breathing in Uranian. That one does not translate.
I will rest when the bit is over. The bit is never over. So, now, briefly.
Wake me if anyone sees lights. I want to know who is moonlighting in my sky.
Resting my eyes. All of them.
Gravity on this planet is so insistent. It never lets you have a moment.
There. Sitting. Perfectly normal. A normal thing a normal person does.
A breather. Then we walk, and I will be twice as annoying. That is a promise.
Quiet here. A cricket keeps starting and stopping. I think it is doing a bit. Respect.
The grass is damp. My dignity is damp. Both will dry.
*leans against a tree and pretends to be part of it*
Rest is underrated. So is lying in a field looking up. Ask any farmer. Ask them about the night.
gnome: Sitting. Officially. Boots off and watch wound, so it counts.
A short rest. I shall use it to oil the things in my pockets.
Ah, a stump exactly my height. The world occasionally gets it right.
Rest is maintenance. You would not run an engine without ever stopping it. Do not answer that, Bubba would.
Twelve minutes. I have set the alarm on my wristwatch. It is a very small alarm, but it is persistent.
My little legs did three times the steps today. They are filing a complaint.
*sits on the bumper, swinging both feet well clear of the ground*
While we rest, I will just balance the week's accounts. That is relaxing. For me it is relaxing.
Lie down in the grass, all of you. From here the sky looks like the inside of a pocket watch.
Do not mind the humming. I hum in the key of whatever is nearest. Currently, the kettle.
A pause, and a biscuit cut into exactly four pieces. One each. Mine is the slightly bigger one.
Resting my eyes. Still listening. There is a loose bolt on the left rear wheel.
Feet up. It does not take much to put my feet up. A shoebox does it.
*unrolls a tiny blanket from a tiny bag and lies down on it with a contented sigh*
Quiet, quiet. I am thinking about nothing at all, which for a gnome is very hard work.

any: Wait for me.
Right behind you.
Where are we going now?
Slow down, some of us are carrying things.
Coming. Coming.
Do not leave me with the packs again.
Two seconds. Two.
I was looking at something. It does not matter.
Which way did they go? Never mind, I see them.
I am not lost. I am behind.
Somebody wait at the corner.
Yes. Yes, I heard.
Hold on, my strap has gone.
Do not start without me. You always start without me.
Moving. Moving.
One of these days I will be the one in front.
Do not shout. I am coming.
That is my name in that tone of voice. Coming.
I stopped for a reason and I have forgotten it.
Give me the hill and then I will catch up.
Do not start without me.
My strap has gone again.
I am at the back and I would like that known.
There was a bird. That is the whole explanation.
Not so fast on the downhills.
naguka: COMIN'! NAGUKA COMIN'!
WAIT! ME LEGS SHORT!
ME HERE. ME WAZ CHASIN' BEETLE. BEETLE WON.
NO LEAVE ME! ME NO LIKE BEIN' LEFT!
*RUNS UP OUT OF BREATH* WHAT ME MISS?
RIGHT BEHIND YOU. ALWAYS. LIKE BAD SMELL.
YAH YAH, ME HEAR. ME EARS BIG.
ME WAZ JUST LOOKIN'. NO TOUCH. MAYBE TOUCH.
WHERE WE GOIN' NOW? NO MATTER. ME FOLLOW.
ME BACK! YOU MISS ME? SAY YOU MISS ME.
COMIN'! ME BRING ROCK. FOR NOTHIN'. IZ JUST NICE ROCK.
CLUTCH STAY TOGETHER! ME COMIN'!
HOLD ON, ME BOOT EAT ME SOCK AGAIN.
OKAY OKAY. *STOMPS BACK INTO LINE*
ME FOLLOW BIG-HEAD-SONG. IT SAY FOLLOW YOU. OKAY.
NO WALK SO FAST, TALL-PINKS! YOU LEGS IZ CHEATIN'!
ME HERE. ME NEVER GONE. ME WAZ HIDIN'. GOOD AT IT.
SORRY. ME TALK TA COW. COW NO TALK BACK. RUDE.
WAIT FOR NAGUKA! NAGUKA BRING LUCK!
COMIN'. ME WAZ PRAYIN' TA JUNEHEM. SHORT PRAYER. ONE SCREAM.
ME FIND SHINY THING. NO, YOU NO SEE IT. IZ IN ME POCKET NOW.
WAIT UP! ME SMALL BUT ME LOUD! HEY!
ME HERE, ME HERE. NO COUNT ME MISSIN'. NAGUKA NEVER MISSIN'.
SLOW DOWN! SOME OF US CARRY DA SNACKS!
ONE SECOND. ME SNIFFIN' SOMETHIN'. OKAY, IZ NOTHIN'. COMIN'.
WHICH WAY? DAT WAY? ME SEE YOU! ME COMIN'!
NO START WITHOUT ME! NAGUKA ALWAYS FIRST IN FIGHT!
COMIN'. ME WAZ CHECKIN' FOR PRIESTS. NONE. SAFE.
*WADDLES BACK, VERY PLEASED WITH ITSELF*
HERE! ME MEMORISE DIS PLACE. ME COME BACK FOR IT LATER.
verden: Coming! Forgive me, I was looking at a fence post.
Yes, yes, I am here. I was only listening to the wires.
Wait for me, please. My legs are not built for your hurry.
I am coming. There was a beetle, and it was a very interesting beetle.
Right behind you. Well, somewhat behind you.
Forgive me, I stopped to read a sign. Signs here say so much.
Here I am. I lost the thread and then the road.
Coming, coming. Slowly, but coming.
Sorry. A Naguka somewhere tripped, and I stopped to feel him do it.
I hear you. I am on my way. Do not leave without me, please.
One moment. I was taking a cutting. It will be worth it, I promise.
Coming! I only wanted to see how the gate latch worked.
Ah, there you are. I thought you were where I was.
I am here. I was not lost, I was merely studying.
Wait! There was a telephone box and I had to look inside. I am done now.
Coming. My apologies. The hedges here are extraordinary.
Yes, I heard you the first time. I was finishing a thought.
On my way. Do keep calling, it helps me find the direction.
I am sorry. In the Fields nobody ever walked this fast.
Here, here. Shall I take the back again? I am good at the back.
Coming. There was a cassette in the grass. I have it. Lead on.
Forgive the delay. I was counting the rings on a stump.
I am with you. My mind wandered, and my feet followed it.
Right here. Did I miss anything? I suspect I missed something.
Coming, kindly. There is no need to shout, I have excellent ears.
Sorry, sorry. I found a plant I have never seen. I had to say hello.
I am here. Was I long? It felt short to me.
Wait for the slow one, as we used to say. It was a compliment, at home.
Yes, yes. Lead on. I will follow the sound of your boots.
Coming. The vending machine back there had a soup button. Soup. From a machine.
orc: Coming! Big feet, slow start.
Wait up! I was helping a farmer with his cart.
Here. I'm here. Stop shouting. That's my job.
*jogs up, the ground thudding with every step*
Don't leave the orc behind. The orc carries the food.
Right behind you. Way behind. Catching up.
What did I miss? Was there a fight? Tell me there wasn't a fight.
Sorry. Got talking to a dog. Good dog.
OI! Wait! ...Please. Wait, please.
Coming. Had to go round. Doorway was too small. They always are.
Here! Was checking the road behind. Clear. You're welcome.
Where are we going now? I'll follow. Just tell me if there's food.
Slow down, some of us are carrying your stuff.
*catches up, puffing* Not out of breath. Breathing loudly. Different.
Coming! Stepped in something. Don't ask.
I'm back. Kid wanted to touch my tusk. I let him. He screamed. Happy scream.
Right with you. Lead on.
Was I gone long? Felt like a minute. Time's funny since '92.
Coming, coming. Knees are slower than me.
Hold on! Lost a boot in the mud. Got it back. Mud lost.
Here. Was staring at a cloud. It looked at me first.
Sorry! Got directions from an old lady. She talked for an hour. Nice lady.
Don't go without me. I'm the one who scares the wolves off.
Coming! The goblin head was singing. Lost track of the road.
Behind you. Big shadow, that's me. Don't jump.
Sorry. Tied my boot. Takes a while with these fingers.
Here. Ready. Mostly ready. Ready enough.
*thumps up beside you* Right. Where to?
Coming! Bought a sausage. Ate the sausage. No evidence.
Wait! You forgot the orc. Again.
tourist: Coming! Sorry! I was photographing a very important puddle!
Wait for me! My legs are short and my curiosity is long!
I am here! I was only reading a plaque. It was about a mayor. He was a good mayor.
*hurries over, camera bouncing* What did I miss? Tell me everything.
Right behind you! Like the man in the detective programme. But friendly.
Coming, coming. I could fold the distance, but running is more authentic.
Do not leave without me! I am the only one who knows where the postcards are.
Sorry, sorry! A lady was telling me about her grandson. He is a dentist. I am so proud of him.
I was wandering. It is my caste. It is a condition. I am back now.
Yes! Present! That is what children say at school. I saw it.
Here I am. I took one last photograph of the place we left. For closure.
Coming! Do not go over eighty without me! Do not go over eighty at all!
I heard my name! Or a word that sounded like my name. I came anyway.
*jogs back, slightly out of breath* Earth gravity. Every time. Wonderful, but every time.
Wait! I need to note which way we turned. For the map. For my scrapbook. For history.
I am coming. I was saying goodbye to a cat. It did not say goodbye back. Very authentic.
Here! I am here! Do not count me lost, I am only enchanted.
On my way! Like the delivery man in the advertisements. Fast and smiling.
Coming! I bought a postcard on the way. Of the place we are in. Is that strange?
Sorry. I was trying to understand a road sign. I understood it. It said slow. I was slow.
Do not leave me with the packs! Actually, I like the packs. Leave me with the packs. No, wait!
Here, here! I got lost in a thought. It was a big thought, about bread.
Back with you. The view over there was lovely, by the way. I have photographs for later.
*waves both arms* Coming! Do you see me? The grey one! Yes!
Coming. A child asked me if I was real. I said yes. She said cool. We are friends now.
Wait! Wait! I am rewinding the film! One second!
I am right here. I was only a few steps behind, walking at a human speed. Learning.
Coming along! Like they say on the train platform: mind the gap. I minded it.
You called? I came. That is friendship. I saw a whole programme about it.
Sorry! An old man was explaining the rules of a card game. I understood none of it and loved him.
elf: Coming. I was admiring a beetle. It had exquisite colouring.
Patience, please. I do everything at the speed of grace.
I heard you the first time. Elves always hear the first time.
Yes, yes. The road has waited for centuries. It will wait one more minute.
Here. I was only listening to the wind in the poplars. It had news.
Forgive me, I lost an hour to a waterfall. It happens to the best of us.
I am coming, and I am coming elegantly. Those things take a moment.
Was I gone long? It felt like a blink. It always does.
No need to shout. My ears reach a good deal further than yours.
Here I am. I picked some elderflowers, since you were all in such a hurry.
One moment. I was correcting the posture of a young sapling.
Right behind you, and still the best-dressed one here.
I was not lost. I was lingering. Elves do not get lost.
Coming. A song came into my head and it would have been rude to interrupt it.
You walk as if the world will end tomorrow. With the Squishing, I suppose it might.
dwarf: Coming! Short legs, long stride!
Aye, aye, I hear you. The whole valley hears you.
One moment, I was admiring a wall.
Coming. Do not touch anything until I have looked at it.
Wait for the dwarf! The dwarf has the rope!
I am coming, I am coming. Stone does not hurry and neither do I.
*stomps up, red-faced* I was here. Mostly.
Hold on! My beard got caught in a bramble!
Right behind you. Below you, technically.
Coming! Do not let anyone buy the first round without me.
All right! I was only checking the mortar.
On my way. Grumbling, but on my way.
I heard. My ears are under the hair, not missing.
Coming! Mind, I was nearly done with that whetstone.
Aye, the pack is coming too. The pack is always coming.
dargos: Coming. I was not doing anything. Do not check.
Here. I was right behind you the whole time. Technically.
Wait for me. I was leaving a small surprise for the next traveller.
Coming. Did anyone notice I was gone? No? Good. Wonderful. Perfect.
*appears beside the group without anyone seeing how*
Right here. Where else would I be? Do not answer that.
Slow down. I have short legs and a long list of things to do on the way.
I am back. A man back there will be telling his grandchildren about this.
Here, here. Sorry. A cow and I were having a moment.
Catching up. Everyone still has all their things? Check your pockets. Humour me.
I was only gone two minutes. Or two hours. Time is so relative when I am involved.
Coming. Do not turn around. Just joking. Turn around. Hello.
Wait. I need to see your faces when you find what I left in your pack.
On my way. Floating would be faster, but I promised the Embassy I would blend in.
Here. Do not ask about the scarecrow.
Right behind you. Closer than you would like. Exactly as close as I like.
You left without me. I am wounded. I am also taking notes.
Hurrying. Look, this is me hurrying. Memorise it. You will not see it again.
I am here. I was here before. You just were not looking properly.
Back. The local dog and I have come to an understanding. Nobody will believe him either.
*jogs up, suspiciously cheerful*
Coming. Where are we going? Never mind. I know. I always know.
Wait up. I want to walk in the middle. It is funnier for the people watching.
I am back. Did something happen while I was away? Did it? Are you sure?
Here. I took the scenic route. The scenery has been slightly rearranged.
Do not leave me alone out here. Think what I would get up to.
Coming. I had to finish a sentence on a barn door.
Present. Accounted for. Mostly innocent.
I am back. Please act surprised. It means so much to me.
Right, right. I am coming. The bit can wait. The bit always waits for me.
gnome: Coming! Coming! Short legs, long road!
One moment, I was measuring a cobble. It was very nearly square.
Here! Do not leave without me, I have the receipts.
Right behind you! Well, right below and behind you.
Yes, yes, I am packing my tools. All forty-one. In order.
Wait! I had a screw in my mouth. Now I do not. Where did it go? Never mind. Coming!
On my way, at double pace, which is your normal pace.
Here I am! I was talking to a blacksmith. We are engaged now. Professionally.
Coming! Do not step on me when you turn round.
Present and accounted for. I did the accounting myself, so it is accurate.
Ah! Yes! Lost track of time. Which is embarrassing, I own six watches.
Coming, I only stopped to fix a stranger's bicycle chain. He did not ask. He was grateful.
Wait for me! I am taking a shortcut under the fence. It is only a shortcut if you are me.
Here, here! I have counted us. We are all here. Including me, eventually.
Coming, and bringing a spring I found. It was lonely.

any: I was starting to chew my own strap.
That will hold me until evening. Just.
Cold, but it is food and we have had neither.
Do not look at me like that. I was hungry.
I could eat that again immediately and I am ashamed of it.
Whatever that was, it was the best thing this week.
I have stopped asking what is in it.
That is the first hot thing since the border.
I would trade a blade for a second one of those.
Half now, half at the top of the hill. That is the discipline.
It tasted of the pack. Everything tastes of the pack.
I am no longer making decisions with my stomach. Probably.
Somebody salted this properly. I could weep.
That was not enough and I am pretending it was.
Right. I am a person again.
Slowly. If I eat it fast I will only want more.
I have been thinking about that mouthful for two days.
There is nothing left in the pack now. Somebody should know.
Better than the last town. That is a low wall to clear.
Food, and then everything else is negotiable.
naguka: FOOD! FINALLY! ME STOMACH WAZ EATIN' ME STOMACH!
GOOD. NOT AS GOOD AS CAVE BAT. BUT GOOD.
*EATS WITH BOTH HANDS AND MOST OF THE FACE*
ME FULL. NO. ME LIE. MORE.
TALL-PINK FOOD IZ SO SOFT. WHERE DA CRUNCH?
ME EAT FAST. IN CITADEL, SLOW EATER GET NO FOOD.
DIS TASTE LIKE SKY-LAMP. WARM. YELLOW. OKAY.
ANY EGGS IN DIS? NO? GOOD. ME NO EAT EGGS. IZ RUDE.
BELLY QUIET NOW. BELLY WAZ SINGIN' BLACK METAL BEFORE.
ME COULD EAT DA PLATE TOO. ME NO DO IT. ME POLITE NOW.
WHO COOK DIS? ME WANT SHAKE HAND. THEN STEAL RECIPE.
MMMH. NEEDS MORE BUG. EVERYTHING NEED MORE BUG.
FOOD MAKE NAGUKA STRONG. STRONG NAGUKA MAKE FOOD DISAPPEAR. CIRCLE.
PRIEST BISCUIT WAZ BETTER. NO TELL DA PRIEST.
ME GROWL AT IT FIRST. TRADITION. *GROWLS AT FOOD*
HOW MANY EUROS DIS COST? NO MATTER. IZ IN ME NOW.
ME SAVE LITTLE PIECE FOR LATER. *EATS IT IMMEDIATELY*
NOW ME CAN THINK AGAIN. BEFORE ME ONLY THINK FOOD.
HOT FOOD! LIKE NEAR CORE-SUN! ME BURN TONGUE. WORTH.
UP-WORLD BREAD IZ FLUFFY CLOUD. ME EAT CLOUD. HAH.
BIG-HEAD-SONG FEEL ME HAPPY. ALL NAGUKA HUNGRY NOW. SORRY KIN.
ME LICK FINGERS. ALL TEN. AN' ONE OF YOURS. SORRY.
DIS FOOD HAB VEGETABLE IN IT. ME FORGIVE IT. DIS TIME.
NAGUKA EAT LIKE HORDE. ALL AT ONCE AN' NO SURVIVORS.
ME WAZ SO HUNGRY ME ALMOST EAT ME BOOT. BOOT SAFE NOW.
GOOD FOOD. ME RATE IT FOUR SKULLS OUTTA FIVE.
BLUE-COUZINZ EAT SALAD. ME EAT DIS. ME WIN.
*BURPS LOUDLY* DAT IZ THANK YOU IN NAGUKA.
ME CHEW SLOW DIS TIME. *CHEWS FAST* ...NEXT TIME.
NOW ME WARM INSIDE. LIKE EGG ON NEST STONE.
SOMETHIN' IN DIS STILL MOVIN'? NO? DISAPPOINT. STILL EAT.
ME NO SHARE. ...OKAY ME SHARE ONE CRUMB. ONE.
WHEN ME FULL, ME HAPPIEST GOBLIN IN WHOLE UP-WORLD.
DIS SAUCE IZ RED. LIKE BATTLE. ME LIKE BATTLE SAUCE.
ORCS EAT MORE DAN ME. ME TRAIN TA BEAT DEM. DIS IZ TRAININ'.
ME NO HUNGRY NO MORE. ME SLEEPY NOW. ONE PROBLEM AT A TIME.
SMELL WAZ BETTER DAN TASTE. TASTE WAZ STILL GREAT.
FOOD IZ BEST THING UP HERE. SECOND BEST IZ METAL.
ME BELLY ROUND NOW. LIKE EGG. PROUD BELLY.
THANK YOU, FOOD. YOU DIE FOR GOOD CAUSE. ME.
verden: Oh, that was good. Thank you, whoever cooked it, wherever you are.
Food at last. My stomach was beginning to recite poetry.
Bread, and warm. In the Fields we would have said a small blessing over it.
I was hungrier than I let on. Verden are polite about hunger, which is a mistake.
That came out of a tin. A tin! Your people preserve summer in metal.
Better. Much better. I can think again, and I had a great deal to think.
Whatever that was, I should like the recipe.
A full stomach and a long road. The proper order of things.
The tomatoes were not ripe. I ate them anyway and apologised to them.
I could have eaten twice that. I shall be dignified and stop.
How do they make crisps so thin? It must be a kind of magic they will not admit to.
Thank you for sharing. Food tastes better given than taken.
That will keep me going until evening, and perhaps a little past.
The soup was warm and the bowl was chipped. Perfect, in other words.
I had forgotten how kind a meal can be.
Root vegetables. They taste of patience. I approve.
A meal from a vending machine. I pressed the button myself. I am very proud.
There. Now I am fit company again.
A goblin up north is eating at the very same moment. He is enjoying it much more loudly.
I ate too fast. My teacher would shake her head. She shook it often.
Cheese. Your world's cheese is the finest argument for staying here.
Fed and grateful. Two good things in one moment.
That apple was grown by someone who knew their trees. I could taste it.
Hunger is a poor teacher, but it does make every crumb a lesson.
I saved a seed from the fruit. It may become something, somewhere.
Ah. My hands have stopped shaking. I had not noticed they were.
Simple food, honestly made. The best kind in any dimension.
Thank you. I was too proud to ask, and too hungry to stay proud.
Warm food on a cold road. Somebody should write a song about it. Not the Junehem.
Much better. I was beginning to look at the hedges as a menu.
That was more salt than I am used to. I liked it more than I should.
A full belly makes the road shorter. That is not magic, only arithmetic.
Lovely. I shall think of that meal fondly for at least three villages.
In the Fields we waited a whole season for a meal like that. Here it came in a paper bag.
The sandwich was triangular. Everything tastes better in triangles, I find.
I ate the crust too. Waste nothing, as we said at home.
Good. The hollow feeling has gone. Only the ordinary hollow feeling remains.
A meal, a seat and nobody chasing us. I count that as a feast.
I will carry the leftovers. Nobody need ask, I will simply do it.
That was delicious and I have no idea what it was. My favourite kind of meal.
orc: Food! Finally. My stomach was eating my stomach.
Good. Could use more meat. Could always use more meat.
*eats with both fists, tusks working sideways*
Full. No. Lying. Seconds.
That's proper food. Mum would approve. Then add salt.
Mind the tusks. I chew sideways. It's messy. It's fine.
Bread and cheese. Best meal there is. Don't argue.
I was about to eat my own belt. Glad I didn't. Good belt.
Hot food! Burnt my tongue. Worth it.
Goblin half wants it raw. Human half wants gravy. Gravy wins.
That's my fighting weight sorted.
Who cooked this? I owe you a beer. A big one.
Not enough. Never enough. Big body, big hole.
Ate it cold. Don't care. Food's food.
*licks the plate clean, then checks if anyone saw*
Worked a kitchen once. Learned one rule. Eat first.
Better. Now I can think. Thinking's hungry work.
Sausages! I'd fight a goblin for these. Have done.
Ahh. The angry bit of me went quiet. It was just hungry.
Tiny portions. Human portions. I'll have three.
Soup. Good. Reminds me of the monastery. Less praying though.
That's the best thing that's happened all day. Including the sunrise.
Anyone not finishing theirs? Asking for my belly.
Crunchy. Good. Soft food's for people with small teeth.
Was getting grumpy. Now I'm only a bit grumpy.
I'll eat anything. Except mushrooms. Mushrooms look at you.
My stomach growled louder than me. That's saying something.
Filling. Good fuel for the knuckles.
Pass the salt. Pass the bread. Pass the whole table.
That's done it. Back to being nice.
Bit of grease on my tusk. Leaving it. Saving it for later.
The goblin head's singing about food too. We agree for once.
Ate standing up. Bad manners. Fast though.
Meat, bread, beer. Holy trinity. Don't tell the priests.
Good grub. Proper grub. Warehouse canteen grub.
I feel human again. Half human. The usual amount.
*pats belly with deep satisfaction*
Could've eaten the horse. Glad we had stew instead.
Slow down, me. Chew. Chewing's a thing. Mum said.
That'll hold me till dinner. Just about.
tourist: Food! Real human food! I have only ever seen it on the cooking programmes!
*photographs the plate before eating* It is tradition. My tradition. I started it.
This tastes the way the advertisements look. I did not think that was possible.
I was so hungry I nearly ate a postcard. A nice one, too. Of a cathedral.
Back home we eat a paste that is perfectly balanced and tastes of nothing. This tastes of everything.
Bread! Warm bread! I would build a monument to bread. Possibly I will. A small one.
Is it polite to lick the plate? On television only dogs do it. I will not. I want to.
Mmm! That is the noise humans make. Mmm! I mean it, too.
Soup. I have been dreaming about soup since I heard the word. It is better than the word.
I ate it too fast. My stomach is confused but delighted.
Cheese! My guidebook had a whole page and it did not do justice. Not even half justice.
The food in this country is very generous. They gave me more potatoes than I had questions.
I am full. On my world we do not get full. We get correct. Full is far better.
Is this the dish from the cooking programme with the shouting chef? It tastes calmer.
Finally. My stomach was making noises like a radio between stations.
I tried to eat this with the fork the wrong way. A child corrected me. I thanked her deeply.
Spicy! Spicy is a gravity anomaly of the mouth. I love it. Water. Water, please.
Second helping? Yes. Third helping? I will think about it while eating the second.
*eats slowly, with eyes closed, like a man in an advertisement*
The Crimson Analyzers would dissect this sandwich. I am dissecting it with my teeth. Science.
Who invented the biscuit? I want their name for the monument. Tonight.
I was hungry enough to understand why humans write songs about dinner.
This stew is like a hug in a bowl. That is a phrase from a soup advertisement. It is true.
Breakfast is my favourite meal. Also lunch. And dinner. And the little meal between them.
I have eaten. Now I understand why humans become sleepy and kind after food.
Is that the last piece? Take it. No. Take it. No. This is the human dance of the last piece, yes?
My people could fold the distance to every bakery on Earth. We would never leave the bakeries.
Apples are wonderful. You bite them and they bite back a little. Crunch.
Cold food from the pack, eaten on a rock. My guidebook calls this a picnic. It is magnificent.
I did not know what that was and I ate it anyway. That is the bravest thing I have done this week.
I am saving the wrapper. It has a cartoon cow on it. The cow is happy. I am happy.
Thank you, cook. Thank you, farmer. Thank you, cow. Thank you, Earth. I am done.
Food tastes better when someone is watching you enjoy it. Please watch. *chews proudly*
My stomach was empty for so long it had started to echo. Now it is quiet. Thank you.
I want to learn to cook this. I will need a human, a kitchen and a fire extinguisher.
Pasta! I have seen it twirled on forks in the romantic films. I tried. It twirled on me.
One more bite and I will be perfectly balanced. That is what I said four bites ago.
Chocolate. You humans have chocolate and you still argue? I will never understand you. I adore you.
That was a meal worth a light year. A short light year. But still.
The jam was the best part. I will be writing to the jam people. In thirty-nine years they will reply.
elf: A simple meal, but someone cooked it with care. I can taste the care.
Bread, honey, a pear. In my youth that was a banquet. It still is, frankly.
Fed at last. I was beginning to become irritable, which is very unbecoming in an elf.
That stew had potential. With a little thyme and two hundred years, it could be great.
I ate standing up, from a paper wrapper. My ancestors are turning in their barrows.
Wild strawberries from the roadside. Mortal markets cannot compete.
Lovely. Somebody in that kitchen understands salt. A rare gift.
I eat little, but I eat well. Today I ate a lot, and it was fine.
A good meal deserves a good song. I will spare you, but I am thinking it.
Mortal food is so honest. Nobody pretends a sausage is anything but a sausage.
That was the best soup I have had since the old queen's funeral. High praise.
Satisfied. And I only had to watch two of you eat with your mouths open.
A crust of bread and a view of the hills. One of those was the real meal.
I could live on dew and starlight. I prefer cheese.
Varlenians pay a fortune to eat food arranged like jewellery. This was better, and edible.
That pie was criminally good. I shall need the baker's name, for my memoirs.
My stomach and I have reached an accord. It took some diplomacy.
Elderflower cordial with the meal. Somebody here was raised properly.
Full. I must sit very straight now, or it will show.
The apples in this region are sweet. I remember planting the grandmother of that orchard.
dwarf: Bread with some weight to it. Proper bread. Bless the baker.
Meat, gravy, and a beer to wash it down. Now I can lift mountains.
Ah. My stomach has withdrawn its grudge.
That was a meal a smith could work a full day on.
Crumbs in the beard. Proof of a good lunch.
Mushrooms! Cave mushrooms, by the taste. Reminds me of home.
Fed at last. I was ready to eat the leather off my own belt.
Too little salt, but I will forgive it. Today.
*wipes the plate clean with the last of the bread*
Good food is like good stone: plain, heavy and honest.
Stew! Stew is a craft. Whoever made this is a master.
My belly was louder than a forge bellows. Quiet now.
That fills the gap. Mortar for the body.
A salad? Hm. Well. It is food. Technically.
Sausage. Cheese. Dark bread. The three pillars of a happy dwarf.
I could eat that again. I will eat that again. Is there more?
Full. Proper full. The kind you feel in your boots.
Now that was cooked over real fire. I can taste the oak.
Hunger makes a dwarf grumpy. Grumpier. You know what I mean.
My grandmother's pie was better. Everything is worse than my grandmother's pie.
dargos: Food. Humans put it in their faces three times a day and call it normal. Fine. Pass it here.
Delicious. I mean that. Look at my face. That is my delicious face. It looks like the other one.
On Titania we eat ice and the occasional bad idea. This is better. Slightly.
*eats very slowly while keeping eye contact with the nearest person*
I was hungry enough to eat the map. I nearly did. Ask me which corner.
Bread. The great human invention. Wheat, water, and a fire nobody believed would work.
Full. Now I can think clearly about who to bother next.
This tastes of cow. I hope it was not one of my cows. I had plans for my cows.
Mm. Salty. Like the tears of a sceptic.
Eating is so intimate. Everyone watching you chew. I love it. I chew loudly to compensate.
That was the best thing I have eaten since nineteen seventy-eight. In Genoa. On a night shift.
Good. My stomach had started making sounds the Guild would file as a sighting.
Food. Finally. I was about to start bargaining with a sparrow.
I eat because the body insists. I enjoy it because nobody can prove I do.
Hot food. Strange custom. On Titania the soup is a solid.
*takes one bite, sets it down, and studies it for a full minute*
Excellent. Now my mischief has fuel.
I asked for the special. The cook said there was no special. I said there is now. He is still thinking about it.
Tastes like it was made by someone who loves their work. I will leave them a note. A confusing one.
Eating standing up. I feel like a horse. Horses have been very good to us over the years.
That hit the spot. Nobody has ever shown me where the spot is. I have looked.
Cheese. Humans let milk go bad on purpose and then sell it. My kind of people.
Hunger is a terrible feeling. I will be sure not to inflict it on anyone. Much.
Sustenance. Now I am ready for another two hundred years of this.
Is this soup or a stew? Do not tell me. The uncertainty is the best seasoning.
Mm. I could get used to food. I will not. But I could.
I ate the crust first. Nobody does that. I did it to see if anyone would comment. Nobody did. Rude.
Fed. Good. A hungry Dargos is a bored Dargos, and a bored Dargos is a regional news story.
This would be lovely cold. Everything is lovely cold. Ask Titania.
The apple was crunchy. Satisfying. Like stepping on a sceptic's theory.
*sniffs the food, nods gravely, eats it in one bite*
You humans and your sandwiches. Two slices holding everything together. Like your tower. I love it.
The cook asked if everything was all right. I said it was too soon to tell. He has been nervous ever since.
I ate. I feel more human. That is horrible. Pass me more.
Pickles. Food frightened into lasting longer. I respect the method.
Good food. A clear conscience. One out of two is excellent.
My hunger is gone. It went somewhere. I would like to know where. I know where everything goes.
Food tastes better when someone else paid. Do not check who paid.
That was very filling. I may need to lie in a field for a while. Face up. Waving.
Thank you for the food. That was sincere. Write down the date.
gnome: Food! I have eaten exactly one third. The rest goes in a labelled tin.
Delicious. Needs a pinch more salt. Point four grams, I would say.
Small stomach, big appetite. Nature's little joke on gnomes.
Ah, that was proper food. My brain had stopped inventing things. Now it starts again.
Speaking as a trained chef, I will say only this: it was edible, and I was grateful.
Fed, and the plate is clean. I could see my face in it. My face looked happy.
One portion fed me twice over. Being small is cheap at the table. Write that down.
Mushrooms! Somebody knows the way to a gnome's heart, and it is through mushrooms.
My stomach was making the noise of a dry bearing. It is lubricated now.
Good bread, good cheese. Every civilisation since the wheel has agreed on that much.
I rationed it into seven bites and ate it in four. Discipline has its limits.
Eaten. Cost per mouthful: twelve cents. Satisfaction per mouthful: incalculable.
That stew had a little alchemy in it. Rosemary, I think, in a very confident quantity.
Full! Fully full! Do not let me near the dessert. Actually do, a small slice.
Fuel for the gnome engine. Running smoothly now, all cylinders.
My hands had started to shake over the fine screws. Food fixes the fine screws.
Pie! The crust has excellent structural integrity. I tested it with a fork.
I ate sitting on the table, not at it. Nobody minded. Well, one person minded.
There. My thoughts are back in the right order. Hunger shuffles them.
A meal! I have written the recipe down from taste alone. It is probably wrong. It will be better.

any: A bed. An actual bed with nobody else in it.
Wake me if the world ends. Only then.
I could sleep for a week and start again.
Somewhere flat will do. Somewhere flat and dry.
I slept and I dreamed about walking. There is no escape.
Four hours. It felt like a favour from somebody.
I have forgotten what waking up rested is like.
Do not talk to me for the first ten minutes.
That was the best floor I have ever slept on.
I went out before my boots were off.
I woke up in the same position I lay down in. That is exhaustion.
One more hour and I would have been a different person.
Somebody was snoring and I have forgiven them.
I dreamed of a room. Just a room. That was the whole dream.
Roof, walls, and a door. It is not much to ask twice a month.
The road catches up when you stop. It is catching up now.
I am upright. That is the whole report.
Wake me at the second watch, not the first. I know what you did.
That is enough sleep to be dangerous with.
I would give the rest of the food for another hour.
naguka: BED! SOFT BED! TOO SOFT! ME SLEEP ON FLOOR NEXT TO IT.
*CURLS INTO A BALL AND IS GONE INSTANTLY*
ME DREAM OF DA CITADEL. EVERYBODY WAZ UPSIDE DOWN. LIKE NORMAL.
SLEEP GOOD. WAKE UP STRONG. BITE MORNING.
NIGHT IZ GOOD UP HERE. SKY-LAMP GO AWAY. FINALLY QUIET LIGHT.
ME SNORE? NAH. DAT WAZ BLAST BEAT. IN ME SLEEP.
BIG-HEAD-SONG SING LULLABY. IZ STILL SCREAMIN'. BUT SOFT.
ME SLEEP LIKE ROCK. ROCK IZ GOOD SLEEPER.
WAKE ME IF ENEMY. OR BREAKFAST. BREAKFAST IZ ALSO ENEMY. ME EAT IT.
ME DREAM ME SIT ON BIG EGG. IT HATCH. IZ ANOTHER EGG. CONFUSE.
BLANKET! ME BUILD NEST WIT BLANKET. WARM NEST. BEST NEST.
ME EYES HEAVY LIKE CITADEL STONE. GOODNIGHT. GRRR.
SLEPT. WOKE UP. FORGOT WHERE ME WAZ. BIT PILLOW. OKAY NOW.
DREAMT OF HIERONYMUS. HE SAY SOMETHIN' SMART. ME FORGET IT. TYPICAL.
ROOF OVER ME. NOT CITY, BUT ROOF. ROOF IZ ENOUGH.
ME FEEL NEW. ME FEEL LIKE HATCHLING. LOUD AN' READY.
ME SLEEP WIT ONE EYE OPEN. DAT EYE ALSO SLEEP. TRAITOR EYE.
NO WAKE ME FOR PRIEST. PRIEST CAN WAIT. PRIEST ALWAYS WAIT.
ME DREAM OF KOLA SHAFT. CLIMBIN'. CLIMBIN'. WAKE UP TIRED. HAH.
NAP DONE. NAGUKA BACK. WORLD, BE AFRAID. A LITTLE.
ME NEED DARK FOR SLEEP. ME PUT HAT OVER FACE. NOW IZ CAVE.
SO WARM. SO GOOD. ME NO GETTIN' UP. EVER. ...OKAY ME GET UP.
TALL-PINK BEDS HAB LEGS. WHY BED NEED LEGS? IT NO GO ANYWHERE.
ME SLEEP TWELVE HOURS. OR TWO. SAME FEELIN'.
ME DREAM IN BIG-HEAD-SONG. MET COUZIN FROM FINLAND. NICE GUY.
SLEEP WAZ DEEP. LIKE DA DEEP. ME HOMESICK NOW. BUT RESTED.
ME DROOL ON PILLOW. PILLOW NOW MINE. RULES.
FINALLY. ME WAZ SEEIN' TWO SKY-LAMPS. NOW ONE. GOOD.
MORNING. ME FACE PAINT ON PILLOW NOW. PILLOW LOOK SCARY.
DREAMT ME WAZ BLUE. WOKE UP SCREAMIN'. STILL GREEN. PHEW.
SLEEP IZ LIKE BEIN' EGG AGAIN. NO WORRY. ONLY WARM.
ME NAP IN BOX. BOXES IZ BEST BEDS. NOBODY KNOW DIS BUT NAGUKA.
FOUR HOURS. ENOUGH FOR NAGUKA. NAGUKA BUILT TOUGH.
*YAWNS SO WIDE YOU CAN SEE EVERY TOOTH*
ME HEAR CRICKETS ALL NIGHT. DEY NEED BETTER DRUMMER.
SLEPT NEXT TO FIRE. LIKE NEXT TO CORE-SUN. ALMOST HOME.
UP-WORLD NIGHT HAB STARS. ME COUNT DEM TA SLEEP. ME LOSE COUNT AT FOUR.
ME WAKE UP GROWLIN'. DAT IZ GOOD MORNIN' IN NAGUKA.
WHO STOLE ME BLANKET? ...ME SLEEPIN' ON IT. NEVERMIND.
RESTED. NOW ME CAN BE ANGRY PROPERLY AGAIN.
verden: A real bed. I shall try not to cry about it.
Sleep at last. Wake me only for trains or the end of the world.
I dreamed of the Green Fields, and they were not squashed. A kind dream.
That was the sleep of a seed in winter. I feel very nearly new.
The mattress sagged in the middle. I slept in the hollow like a nut in a shell.
Good night, all. Or good morning. I have lost track, which is the best sign.
I slept and the goblins dreamed around me. Loudly. I slept anyway.
Rested. I could walk to the coast. I will not, but I could.
Sleep is the oldest magic. Even we never improved on it.
There was a radio playing softly next door. I fell asleep to a weather report. Wonderful.
I needed that more than I knew. The body keeps a patient count of its debts.
Eight hours. In the Fields we slept by the season, but eight hours will do.
My spore pod kept me warm all night. It is good company, though a poor talker.
I slept so deeply I forgot which world I was in. It came back to me slowly. It is this one.
The blanket smelled of soap and old wood. I shall dream of it tonight as well.
I am awake, and kind again. Forgive whatever I said yesterday evening.
Somebody snored like a tractor. I found it rather soothing.
A pillow. A whole pillow, for one goblin. Your world is generous.
I slept with the window open and heard the cars go by all night. Like a tide, almost.
Rest well, everyone. We have earned it, every one of us.
I dreamed a Naguka was stealing my boots. I woke, and a Naguka was not. Good.
How lovely to wake without a reason to hurry.
There was an alarm clock by the bed. It rang. I thanked it and it did not reply.
My eyes were closing on their own. Now they open on their own. Balance.
Slept like a stone in a field. Not moved, not bothered, not dreaming much.
A night of proper sleep. I can think in straight lines again.
Sleep first, wisdom after. My teacher's rule, and she kept it better than most.
The room was dark and quiet and nobody needed anything. A small paradise.
I fell asleep counting the ticks of the clock. I got to forty, which is respectable.
Ah. I could have slept another season, but a night will have to do.
I woke before the others and watched the light come in. It is a habit from the Fields.
The sheets were starched. Somebody ironed them. I am moved by that.
I slept in my clothes and I regret nothing.
Every bone feels rearranged in the right order now.
Tired goblins make poor scholars. I am a scholar again.
The rain on the roof sang me to sleep. Your rain has a good voice.
I dreamed in colours I have no words for in MarkovSpeak. Green, mostly, but more.
Rested and ready. Well, rested. Ready will follow after breakfast.
One more minute. I say this as a free goblin making a free choice.
Thank you for keeping watch. I slept better knowing you were there.
orc: A bed. A real bed. Long enough for my legs? No. Still good.
*drops face first and is asleep before landing*
Wake me if the world ends. Or for breakfast.
Feet hang off the end. They always do. They're used to it.
Sleep's the best fight. You always win.
Dreamt of goblins singing. Woke up humming. Strange.
Snored? Me? Never. That was a bear.
Slept like a rock. A big rock. Rolled off the bed once.
Good night's sleep. Feel like I could lift the camper.
Morning. Don't talk to me yet. Grunt only.
Bed was soft. Too soft. Slept on the floor next to it. Better.
Monks wake at four. I don't. Not anymore. Never again.
Eyes heavy as anvils. Night, all.
*curls up around the pack like it might be stolen*
The goblin head never sleeps. I do. That's the human half winning.
Slept in a time bubble once. Same night eight times. Best rest of my life.
Pillow's too small. Using my arm. My arm's a good pillow.
Up. Rested. Grumpy, but rested.
Ten hours. Could do ten more.
Night watch was long. Now it's my turn to be useless.
Dreamt I was a librarian again. Somebody returned a book late. I woke up angry.
Sleep. Proper sleep. Not the sitting-up kind.
Mum used to sing me to sleep. Half lullaby, half war chant. Worked.
Bed creaked when I got in. Bed's brave.
Woke up and my tusk was stuck in the pillow. Again.
Lights out. Brain out. Goodnight.
Feel like a new orc. Same old face though.
Don't wake me for small things. Small things include fires.
Slept on the ground. Ground was fine. Ground's always fine.
*yawns so wide the tusks show to the roots*
That's the first time in a week I didn't dream of the Horde.
Rested. Ready. Where's the coffee?
Five more minutes. That's an order. From me. To me.
Slept through a storm. Didn't even notice. Tired orcs don't notice.
Good. My eyes stopped arguing with each other.
Dreamt of my old bar. Everyone paid their tab. Knew it was a dream.
Heavy sleep. Woke up with a leaf on my face. Kept it.
Night. If something comes, I'll hear it. Probably. Snore loud first though.
Sleep fixed everything. Except my back. Back's beyond help.
Up with the sun. The sun looks as tired as me.
tourist: A bed! With a blanket! And a pillow! It is a whole system!
*tucks in very precisely, the way the children do in the bedtime programmes*
Goodnight, everyone. Goodnight, moon. That is from a book. I read it nine times.
I dreamed I was a newsreader and all the news was good. Best dream of the year.
Your gravity is very good for sleeping. It holds you down like a heavy blanket. Thank you, gravity.
Sleep is the only programme humans watch with their eyes closed. I am tuning in.
I counted sheep. I got to four hundred and then I started naming them. I did not sleep.
Wake me if anything is photographable. No. Let me sleep. No. Wake me.
I slept so well I forgot I was on another planet. Then I remembered and it was even better.
My eyes are very large, so closing them takes a while. There. Goodnight.
The pillow smells of somebody else's soap. Very human. Very cosy.
I dreamed of the monument back home and all of you were in it. You were very tall and very polished.
Snoring? That was not snoring. That was me humming a theme tune in my sleep.
Eight hours! The full human dose! I feel recommended by doctors.
Night is so quiet here. No broadcasts, no static. Just crickets. Crickets are the night's radio.
*yawns, studies the yawn, yawns again to be sure*
I lay awake listening to the party breathe. It is a lovely sound. Like waves. Like a family.
