Pyjamas! I have bought pyjamas! They have little rockets on them. Very ironic.
I fell asleep sitting up, holding the camera. I have a photograph of the inside of my sleeve.
On my ship I sleep floating. Here I sleep flat, pressed down by a whole planet. It is like being hugged.
A good sleep. I woke up and the sun was where I left it. Reliable star.
I am too excited to sleep. Tomorrow there will be new things. There are always new things.
Goodnight. If I talk in my sleep, it will be in TV quotes. Do not take them personally.
Is it normal to dream in black and white? My dreams are all from the early broadcasts.
*falls asleep mid-sentence about cheese*
The mattress has a dip in the middle where a thousand humans slept before me. I fit in it perfectly.
I slept, and nothing tried to open me in the night. Not a single Crimson Analyzer. Peaceful.
Morning already? On my world morning is a setting. Here it just happens to you. Thrilling.
I needed that. I was so tired I tried to fold my bed closer to me.
Hotel beds have a little chocolate on the pillow in the films. This one has a moth. Still lovely.
I will sleep like a log. That is your idiom. Logs are excellent sleepers. I respect logs.
When I close my eyes I see the road still going by. Is that normal? It is beautiful.
A whole night without wanting to take a single photograph. That is how tired I was.
Wake me for breakfast. Or for a rainbow. Or for anything. Fine, wake me for nothing.
The rain on the roof sounds like applause. I slept to a standing ovation.
Sleeping in a strange bed in a strange town. My guidebook calls this travel. My back calls it something else.
Night night. That is what you say to small humans. I am small. Night night.
I have had a nap. The nap is my favourite human invention after the bench.
The stars here are in the wrong places and I love them anyway. Goodnight, wrong stars.
Rested and ready! Today I will see at least forty things. I am setting the bar low.
elf: Rested. Elves need less sleep than you, but we need it softer.
I dreamed in a language that has not been spoken for six hundred years. Lovely, if lonely.
A few hours with my eyes half open, the old way. I feel restored.
That mattress was an insult to sleep. I slept anyway, out of spite.
I dreamed of the forest I was born in. It is a car park now, but in the dream it remembered me.
Sleep at last. My beauty was beginning to fray at the edges.
Awake, refreshed, and only a little grumpy about the pillow.
I slept under the stars. They are rearranging themselves lately. I find it rude.
A good rest. I could face another century now. Or at least another morning.
Mortals snore like collapsing barns. I say it with fondness, and with cotton in my ears.
I dreamed I was young again. Two hundred, perhaps. Such energy.
Rested enough to be charming again. You are all very welcome.
One should sleep with a window open. The night has things to say.
I lay awake listening to an owl argue with a nightjar. The owl won on technique.
Asleep before the moon rose, awake before the lark. The old habits are the good ones.
A bed with linen sheets. Somebody in this inn knows how to live.
I was so tired I nearly slept like a mortal. Flat out, mouth open. Do not tell anyone.
Restored. My ears have stopped drooping, which is the true measure.
I dreamed of my mother's garden in Varlenia. The roses were made of money. It was not a nice dream.
Sleep is the one thing I cannot hurry, and the one thing I never want to.
dwarf: A bed. Too long, too soft, and I will not complain about either.
*snores like a rockslide almost at once*
Sleep. The forge banks its fire. So do I.
Wake me at dawn. Not before. Not after. Dawn.
I sleep best underground. Above ground, I make do.
Beard outside the blanket. Always. Learned that the hard way.
My bones feel like an anvil after a long day of hammering.
I will dream of veins of silver. I always do, when I am this tired.
This mattress has a dip in it. Who slept here before me? A troll?
Good night, all. Nobody touch my boots.
Rested. I could dig a tunnel to the next town.
Slept like a boulder. Woke like a slightly smaller boulder.
A real night's sleep. I feel forged anew.
Ceiling's too high. Feels like sleeping in a cathedral. Still, sleep is sleep.
*pulls the blanket over the head and mutters a mining song*
Eyelids heavier than lead. Heavier than gold, even.
I have been awake since the second shift of yesterday. Goodnight.
Do not wake me for anything less than a dragon or a free round.
That was proper sleep. Deep sleep. Mineshaft sleep.
Up already? Aye. A dwarf wakes before the rooster and resents it.
dargos: Sleep. The eight hours humans spend completely defenceless. You have no idea how adorable that is.
A bed. I will lie in it the human way. Then the other way. Then floating, a little, when nobody looks.
Goodnight. If you wake up with your shoelaces tied together, that is a dream. Probably.
*lies down perfectly straight, arms crossed, like a pharaoh with a plan*
I sleep with one eye open. The other one is also open. I do not really sleep. I wait.
The sheets smell of soap. Humans are so determined to smell of nothing.
Rest well, everyone. I will be right here. Watching. For your safety. Mainly.
On Titania a night lasts forty-two years. This one will be short. Lucky you.
I dreamt I was a security guard in Genoa and something kept visiting me. Terrifying. Very funny.
Bed. Soft. Suspiciously soft. Who made it up? Not me. Therefore suspicious.
Lights out. My favourite part of any human evening.
I am so tired I could actually be sincere. Quick, someone ask me something. No. Too late. Asleep.
Sleep at last. If I talk in my sleep, write it down. It will be the only true thing I ever say.
I slept like a rock. A rock on Titania. Cold, motionless, and secretly plotting.
Good morning. Did anyone sleep well? Interesting. Very interesting.
I am going to bed. Do not move the furniture while I sleep. That is my job.
Humans count sheep to fall asleep. I count humans. It works just as well.
The pillow is lumpy. Somebody hid something in it. I am proud of whoever it was. It was me.
Sleep. Missing time, but the kind you choose. How civilised.
I woke up exactly where I fell asleep. Disappointing. I like a little mystery.
*pulls the blanket up to the eyes and keeps watching the window*
A roof over my head. I am not used to that. Usually I am the thing over the roof.
Rested. Refreshed. Ready to be inexplicable again.
I dreamt about the Guild. They held an assembly and invited me. I did not go. Even in the dream.
Night. The stars are out. Some of them are moving. Do not worry about the moving ones.
Sleeping on the ground is fine. The ground has never once asked me what I want.
Just closing my eyes for a second. Wake me if anything strange happens. Other than me.
I am sleepy enough to be harmless. Enjoy it. It will not last.
That was a deep sleep. I lost two hours. Now I know how it feels. Still funny.
A proper bed. Clean sheets. A mint on the pillow. I will put it on someone else's pillow. Escalation.
Humans sleep so trustingly. Mouths open. Arms flung out. How do you survive?
Goodnight. Lock the door. Not that it helps. It is just polite.
I was asleep before my head reached the pillow. Unprecedented. Somebody has been drugging me with exercise.
I dream in Uranian. It is a very dry language. Most of the jokes are about distance.
Bed. Finally. The only place where nobody expects me to be unsettling.
Sleep tight. If you hear humming in the night, that is the fridge. There is no fridge.
I am awake. I have been awake for a while. I was letting you sleep. And watching.
Tired. So tired. The bit took a lot out of me today.
A nap. A small, unscheduled loss of consciousness. How very Earth.
Morning already. The sun is very loud on this planet.
gnome: A bed! It is enormous. I could sleep crosswise and still have room for my tools.
Wake me at six forty. Not six forty-one. I will know.
*winds a small alarm clock, sets it on the pillow, and is asleep before it ticks twice*
Sleep at last. My brain has been running hot since Tuesday.
Do not let me sleepwalk near the toolbox. Last time I invented something I cannot explain.
One pillow for my head, one for my feet. A gnome-sized bed is two pillows.
Eight hours, or as the professionals say, a full service.
Too tired even to count sheep. Somebody count them for me and leave me the total.
Sleep. My eyes have been doing arithmetic on their own for an hour.
Good night. If you hear ticking, that is me. I tick a little when I dream.
A spring mattress. I counted the springs through the sheet. Two hundred and six. Sleep.
Wake me only for fire, flood, or a really interesting machine.
Ah, rest. I shall dream in blueprints.
Tucked in. Hat on the bedpost, boots aligned, spectacles folded. Now I may sleep.
So tired I nearly fell asleep standing. Which for me is nearly lying down anyway.
I have been awake for thirty-one hours. I have the exact figure because I am like this.
A proper sleep, please. My beard has gone limp, and it only does that when it is serious.
Sleeping in a drawer would be cosier, but I will settle for this palace of a bed.
Lights off. I can still see the gears behind my eyelids, turning slowly. Lovely.
Bed. If I mumble numbers in the night, do not answer, it only encourages them.

any: I had forgotten what my own hands looked like.
Three days of road, off at last.
Now I am fit to stand near people again.
That water was colder than the grave and worth it.
I am a new person and the old one was appalling.
There is a whole river's worth of the last week in that basin.
My own smell had started to frighten me.
Clean shirt. It will last an hour and it is worth it.
I did not know how much of that was mud.
Somebody heated water for this. I will not forget it.
Half the swamp came off. Only half.
I would pay for that again at twice the price.
My hair has opinions. It has fewer of them now.
That is the first time in a week I have felt like a citizen.
The water went brown immediately. Immediately.
I have scrubbed the road off and I miss none of it.
Even the cold one is better than nothing. Barely.
Nobody comment. I am aware I am pink.
Boots off, feet in the stream. This is civilisation.
I can smell the food now, which is either good or very bad.
naguka: WATER! COLD! WHY ALWAYS COLD! *SPLUTTERS*
ME CLEAN NOW. ME SMELL LIKE FLOWER. ME HATE IT. ME LOVE IT.
CORPSE PAINT GONE. ME FACE LOOK NAKED. ME PAINT AGAIN LATER.
SO MUCH DIRT CAME OFF. ME WAZ HALF DIRT. NOW ME ONLY QUARTER.
SOAP TASTE BAD. ME CHECK. YAH. VERY BAD.
ME GREEN AGAIN! ME FORGOT ME WAZ SO GREEN!
TALL-PINKS WASH EVERY DAY? EVERY DAY? HOW DEY HAB TIME FOR WAR?
DOWN IN DA DEEP WE BATHE IN HOT SPRING. DIS IZ COLD SPRING. SAD.
*SHAKES OFF WATER LIKE A DOG, SOAKING EVERYONE*
CLEAN NAGUKA IZ STILL SCARY NAGUKA. JUST SHINIER.
ME SCRUB EARS. FOUND BEETLE. HELLO, BEETLE. GOODBYE, BEETLE.
NOW PEOPLE STAND CLOSER. ME NO SURE IF ME LIKE DAT.
BLUE-COUZINZ ALWAYS CLEAN. NOW ME TOO. TAKE DAT, BLUE-COUZINZ.
WATER TURN BROWN. DEN BLACK. DEN GREEN. DAT LAST ONE WAZ ME?
ME WASH BEHIND EARS. ME EARS BIG. TAKE LONG TIME.
PRIEST SAY CLEANLINESS IZ HOLY. ME SAY IZ COLD. WE BOTH RIGHT.
FRESH. LIKE NEW HATCHLING. ALSO SCREAMIN' LIKE ONE.
ME SMELL ME OWN ARMPIT. NOW IZ SAFE. BEFORE WAZ WEAPON.
DAT TUB HAB SEEN THINGS NOW. POOR TUB.
ME TOWEL IZ BLACK NOW. FROM PAINT. TOWEL IZ METAL NOW.
CLEAN TEETH. ME COUNT DEM AGAIN. STILL ALL DERE. SHINY.
ME FEEL LIGHTER. DIRT WEIGH A LOT. NAGUKA DIRT ESPECIALLY.
BATH OKAY. RIVER BETTER. FISH WATCH YOU. COMPANY.
NOW ME CAN GO INTO SHOP AN' NOBODY FAINT. PROGRESS.
HOT WATER! UP-WORLD HAB HOT WATER! BEST INVENTION! AFTER METAL.
ME WASH SLOW. SAVE SOME DIRT FOR LATER. DIRT IZ COSY.
ME BUBBLES! *BLOWS SOAP BUBBLES AND GIGGLES MENACINGLY*
ME CLEAN ENOUGH FOR CHURCH. NO GO TA CHURCH. JUST SAYIN'.
SKIN TINGLY. IZ DAT CLEAN? CLEAN IZ WEIRD.
BEFORE BATTLE ME PAINT AGAIN. CLEAN FACE IZ BAD LUCK FOR FIGHT.
ME NAILS CLEAN. ME CLAWS SHINY. ME DANGEROUS AN' PRETTY.
WATER IN ME EARS. ME HEAR OCEAN. OCEAN IZ BORING SONG.
THREE DAYS OF ROAD, GONE. ME MISS IT LITTLE BIT. NO.
ME SCRUB TILL ME SQUEAK. *SQUEAKS* SEE?
CLEAN BODY, SAME HEART. HEART STILL PART GOBLIN, PART STORM.
ME SIT IN WATER TILL ME WRINKLY. NOW ME LOOK LIKE GRANNY. GOOD GRANNY.
DA STINK WAZ PART OF ME PERSONALITY. ME GROW IT BACK.
NOW ME SMELL LIKE SOAP. HORDE WOULD LAUGH AT ME. LET DEM.
ME COMB HAIR. ME HAB FOUR HAIR. ALL BEAUTIFUL NOW.
CLEAN! READY FOR NEW DIRT! COME, DIRT!
verden: Clean again. I feel almost presentable to the people of this world.
Hot water from a tap. A tap! I turned it twice just to watch it work.
There was a great deal of road on me. Now it is back where it belongs.
My skin is properly blue again. The dust was making me grey, and grey does not suit me.
Soap that smells of lavender. Your people bottle gardens. I admire that.
The river was cold, but honest. I thanked it on the way out.
Washed, combed and very nearly respectable.
I had soil under my nails. A gardener never minds, but a guest should.
A bath. I sat in it until the water forgave me.
Clean water is a luxury in some places, and I will not take it lightly.
I scrubbed off three countries' worth of dust. I kept a little, for memory.
There was a machine that dried my hands with hot wind. Astonishing. I used it four times.
Much better. I was beginning to smell like a Naguka, and they would have welcomed me.
The towel was rough and warm. I could have stood there for an hour.
Fresh clothes, clean skin. I feel like a new shoot after rain.
In the Fields we bathed in the morning dew. Here there is a shower, which is quicker and less poetic.
The water ran brown, then grey, then clear. A small lesson in patience.
Clean hands for clean work. As we said at home.
I washed my spore pod as well. Gently. It seemed grateful, as far as one can tell.
Ah. I can face a crowd again, and the crowd can face me.
That basin water is now mostly field. I apologise to whoever empties it.
A little soap and the world seems kinder. It is not, but it seems so.
I washed in a launderette sink while the machines turned. I watched them the whole time.
I had leaves in my hair. Three different kinds. I have kept them for my notes.
Clean. I shall try to stay so for at least an afternoon.
The shampoo bottle had a picture of a happy family on it. I felt included.
Fresh as a morning garden. Well, as a morning garden after a long journey.
The mirror tells me I am blue and tidy. Two of my favourite things to be.
Thank you for the soap. Sharing soap is a deep friendship among my people.
The road comes off, but the stories stay. That is the right way round.
A cold rinse. It woke up parts of me I had left in the last town.
I am clean enough to be invited indoors. That is the standard I aim for.
Water, soap and quiet. The three gifts of a good inn.
Much better. I was frightening the birds.
The bathhouse tiles were lovely. Someone placed every one by hand. I counted a corner of them.
I feel lighter. Mud is heavier than people think.
Washed. Now I may sit at a table without the table objecting.
Clean, warm and smelling of somebody else's flowers. Very satisfactory.
The goblins never wash. I can feel them not washing right now. Poor dears.
There, the last of the road is gone. Let us go and collect some more.
orc: Water! Cold! Why's it always cold?
Clean. Smell like soap. Don't like it. Don't hate it.
So much dirt came off. Was half dirt. Now a quarter.
Scrubbed the tusks. Shiny. Looking dangerous.
*splutters and shakes like a wet dog*
Fit to stand near people again. Near-ish.
Washed behind the ears. Took a while. Big ears.
Bath was too small. Washed in sections.
Mum always said wash your neck. Washed it. Hi, Mum.
Smelt like a goblin camp. Now I smell like a human. Better for business.
Clean shirt. Feels like a promotion.
Hot water! Who arranged this? Marry me.
Shaved. Missed a bit. Left it. Character.
Three days of road gone down the drain. Bye, road.
River water. Fish looked offended. Fish'll live.
Soap in my eye. Fought it. Soap won.
The bar taught me one thing. Customers tip clean orcs better.
Hair's wet. Tusks wet. Everything wet. Good.
*hums a goblin war tune in the bath, then stops, embarrassed*
Ahh. I can see my own skin. It's green. Still.
Nobody will cross the street now. Well. Fewer people.
Washed my socks. They fought back.
Clean nails. First time since spring.
Wet and happy. Like a big frog.
Towel's tiny. Using two. Using three.
Smelled myself earlier. Apologised to everyone. Fixed now.
Clean orc. Rare sight. Somebody paint me.
Cold water wakes you better than coffee. Hurts more though.
Monastery rule. Wash before prayer. I skipped the prayer. Kept the wash.
Mud everywhere. Wait. Not anymore. Look at that.
Feel lighter. That was a kilo of dust.
Brushed the teeth. All of them. The big ones take ages.
Water's brown now. That was me. Sorry, water.
Smell nice. Somebody notice. Anybody.
Got the blood off the knuckles. Mine, mostly.
Fresh. Like a morning. A big green morning.
Clean enough for a church. Not going. But could.
Washed. Combed. Still look like trouble. Nicer trouble.
*steps out of the water steaming slightly*
That's better. Now I only smell of orc. Natural orc.
tourist: A bath! With bubbles! The bubbles are the best part. I photographed them before they popped.
I am clean and grey again. I had become a sort of brown grey. Not my colour.
Soap smells of flowers! You put flowers in your soap! You are a poetic species.
*emerges from the wash, squeaking slightly*
The water was so cold I briefly understood the human word for swearing. I used it.
A towel! A fluffy one! I would like to keep it. I will ask. Probably not.
Back home we clean ourselves with a beam of light. A bucket is so much more intimate.
I smell like the advertisement for mountain freshness. I feel like the mountain.
Three days of road came off me in that basin. Most of it was dust. Some of it was cheese.
Shampoo! I have no hair. I used it anyway. It foamed. It was glorious.
My eyes are very big and soap is very rude. Lesson learned. Ow.
Fresh and clean, like the washing powder lady says. She was right. I owe her an apology for doubting.
Now I am fit to be photographed. Somebody take one of me for once.
I washed my clothes in the river like the women in the old films. A fish watched me the whole time.
Is it normal for humans to sing in the bath? I did. A theme tune. The acoustics were superb.
Hot water! Somebody heated water just so I could stand in it! Earth is too kind.
I am clean enough now to stand near people and ask them questions. Watch out, people.
*polishes the camera lens first, the face second* Priorities.
I had a shower and the shower had opinions about temperature. We argued. I lost.
Clean! I feel like a brand new souvenir in its box.
Humans wash every day? Every single day? And still find time for television? Remarkable.
I used the little soap from the inn. It was shaped like a shell. I nearly kept it instead.
The bathroom mirror steamed up and I drew a smiling face on it. It is a human custom, yes?
Brushed my teeth. All of them. It took a while. I have many small ones.
I was so dirty that a child asked if I was a statue. Now I am a clean statue.
A wash and a clean shirt. I am a new Tourist. The old one was dusty and full of crumbs.
I tried to dry myself with a little gravity, spinning. It worked, but I am dizzy now.
The water smelled of iron and mountains. Earth water has flavour. Our water is just correct.
*hums the washing powder jingle while scrubbing*
Even my camera strap needed a wash. It smelled of every country we have crossed.
Clean feet! I walked so far they had become part of the road. Now they are feet again.
A public bath. Everyone was naked and nobody was embarrassed. Except me. Mostly about my camera.
I am so fresh the flies have given up on me. They have moved on to the Naguka.
The rain counts as a bath, yes? No? Then I have been very dirty for a week.
That bath was so lovely I would like a postcard of it. Do they make postcards of baths?
I got soap in places I did not know I had. Educational.
Now I smell like a human! Like a human who has just bathed. The best kind of human.
Clean water, clean face, clean spirit. That is from a toothpaste programme, or from a monk. I forget which.
I have washed off a whole region. Goodbye, region. You were lovely, but you were on me.
*inspects both hands in wonder* So that is what colour they are.
elf: Clean at last. I was beginning to resemble a mortal after a long journey.
My hair is washed, combed and braided. Now I can face the world, and it can face me.
A bath with rosemary in it. I feel two hundred years younger.
Mud on my boots. Mud on my cloak. Mud, regrettably, on my ears. No longer.
The water was cold, but the river was beautiful. That counts for something.
Bathed, scented, presentable. You may all look at me again.
I cleaned my ears. Do you know how long that takes? Neither do you, and you never will.
A wash in a basin of rainwater. Simple. Rather pastoral, really.
The soap at that inn smelled of lavender and lies. Still, it worked.
Clean. Now I feel like a jewel again, rather than the box it came in.
I brushed my hair a hundred strokes. My mother did it a thousand. Standards are slipping.
Hot water from a tap. Your people's greatest achievement, and I do not say that lightly.
Freshly washed, and my cloak beaten clean. Grace is mostly maintenance.
I smelled of camper. Elves should smell of pine and rain, never of camper.
A bath in a lake at dawn. The mist did half the work for me.
My nails are clean, my collar is crisp. Now somebody pay me a compliment.
There. I no longer look like I have been carried here by a dog.
Washed my bowstring hand twice. A clean hand shoots straighter. Or so my teacher lied.
Scrubbed. In Varlenia they pay someone to do this. I prefer to do it myself and feel smug.
Fresh as a spring morning. Well, an early summer one. I am not a miracle.
dwarf: A bath. My beard was starting to have its own weather.
Soot out of the ears at last. I had a whole forge in there.
*wrings out the beard like a wet rope*
Clean. I feel two pounds lighter, and most of it was road.
Hot water! Someone here understands boilers. I respect them.
Beard oil, beard comb, beard braid. Now I am fit for company.
I found a pebble in my beard from three valleys ago. A souvenir.
Washed. Smell of soap. Not as nice as coal smoke, but socially better.
Cold water. Bracing. Like being slapped by a mountain.
Scrubbed the grime from under my nails. Found my nails.
There. Clean as a new ingot.
A dwarf with a clean beard is a dwarf at peace.
Three sorts of mud washed off. I can name all three.
The bathtub was too deep. I swam. I will not discuss it.
My mother would be proud. She would still check behind my ears.
Finally. I smelled like a smelter, and not the good kind.
Clean boots, clean beard, clean conscience. Two out of three.
*combs the beard for a long time, humming*
Washed off the road. The road will put itself back on tomorrow.
Fresh as a new seam of quartz.
dargos: Washing. Humans scrub off their own skin daily and call it hygiene. I call it disposing of evidence.
The water is cold. Not Titania cold. Disappointing.
Clean. Now I smell like a human with nothing to hide. Excellent disguise.
*washes face, stares at reflection, and the reflection blinks a moment late*
Soap. A whole bar of it. I am going to carve a little face into it and leave it in the dish.
Fresh. Refreshed. Unrecognisable to any witness.
I washed behind my ears. Humans say that a lot. I checked. There was nothing there. Suspicious.
A bath. I lay in it until the water went cold, then until it went colder. Home comforts.
Clean hands. Nobody will ever know what they were doing an hour ago.
I left the tap dripping in a particular rhythm. Morse code. It spells a word nobody will like.
The mirror fogged up and I drew a little face in it. When it fogs up again, they will see it.
Washed. Brushed. Combed. I look so trustworthy now it is almost a prank on its own.
The road dust is gone. Some of it was from a crop circle. Do not ask which crop.
Humans are so fond of water. Warm water, cold water, bottled water. Your whole planet is a bath.
*steps out of the river, shakes off like a dog, keeps eye contact*
I scrubbed. There is less of me now. Good. Less to identify.
Clean clothes. Inside out. On purpose. Watch how long it takes anyone to say something.
I smell of lavender. A cruel thing to do to a being of my reputation.
The towel was rough. Honest work, a rough towel. I respect it.
Clean at last. I was beginning to smell like a prank gone wrong.
There was a spider in the bath. We came to an arrangement. It will be in someone's boot by morning.
Hygiene. One of the few human rituals I perform without irony. Well. With little irony.
I combed my hair into a perfect circle. Ten metres wide, it would be famous.
Water down the drain. Where does it go? I know where it goes. I have been there. Do not go there.
The innkeeper gave me one towel. I gave it back folded into a swan. With an extra neck.
Clean. Now I am presentable to the authorities, who will not believe a word I say.
That was a long wash. Missing time, the clean kind.
Bathing in a river under the stars. Humans call this romantic. I call it being visible from orbit.
Teeth brushed. All of them. That took a while. Do not count them.
Freshly washed and smelling of pine. Somewhere a forest is missing me.
The basin water turned grey. I will tell the innkeeper it was ectoplasm. It was mostly mud.
Clean, and with a straight face. Both took practice.
Humans wash so they will be liked. I wash so they will not see me coming.
*emerges from the wash house humming something that makes the dogs sit up*
Hot water. A luxury. On Titania hot water is a myth told to frighten children.
Freshly bathed. The kind of clean that makes a sceptic doubt themselves.
Do not use the soap in the blue dish. Just a friendly warning. A friendly, specific warning.
I washed my notebook too. By accident. Now nobody will ever read what I wrote about you. Lucky you.
Scrubbed raw. I look like a newborn. A very old newborn with an agenda.
Clean enough for polite company. Not that I keep any.
gnome: Washed! There was grease on me in places I did not know I had.
The tub was so deep I had to swim. I am not complaining, it was marvellous.
Clean hands at last. You cannot do fine work with dirty hands. The dirt gets in the threads.
Combed, scrubbed and waxed. Presentable to nobility again. Which is lucky, my aunt is nobility.
I smell of soap instead of solder. It is strange, but I will get used to it.
Clean! I used one bar of soap, precisely half, and I have marked the line.
Hot water from a boiler. I took a peek at the boiler afterwards. Very decent pressure valve.
I washed the hat too. A gnome's hat is half a gnome's personality.
There is no soot under my fingernails. I keep checking. I feel like a stranger.
Scrubbed. Even behind the ears, and mine are quite generous ears.
Clean as a new cog, and nearly as shiny.
I had to stand on a stool to reach the tap. Then on a second stool. Then on the sink.
That bath took the sulphur off. Alchemy is wonderful, but it lingers.
Washed and dried. I also cleaned the soap dish, because I had a little brush.
Ahh. My skin can breathe again. It was holding its breath under the oil.
Clean at last. I shall try very hard not to touch an engine for at least an hour.
Fresh! I counted the drops left in the shampoo bottle. Twenty-two. We should buy more.
Washed my spectacles too. The whole world just got three times sharper.
There. I no longer smell like a forge. Somewhat like a flower, faintly like a forge.
A gnome scrubbed is a gnome restored. My grandmother embroidered that on a towel.

any: Good to hear a voice that is not my own.
People. I had missed people, which surprises me.
That is the most I have said all week.
Somebody argued with me about nothing for an hour. Wonderful.
A room with noise in it. I did not know I needed that.
I talked to a stranger about weather and it was the best part of the day.
I have used up all my words. It was worth it.
Nobody in there knew a single thing about us. It was restful.
Somebody laughed at something I said. I am going to think about that.
I had forgotten how to end a conversation politely.
Two hours of other people's problems. Marvellous.
There was singing. Badly, but there was singing.
I told somebody the whole story and they believed the wrong half.
I am fed and I have been spoken to. That is the full set.
I shook a hand today. That is worth writing down.
naguka: PEOPLE! TALKIN'! ME LOVE TALKIN'! ESPECIALLY ME!
ME TALK TA TALL-PINK FOR HOUR. HE NO RUN AWAY. NEW RECORD.
GOOD. ME WAZ LONELY. BIG-HEAD-SONG NOT SAME AS FACE.
SOMEBODY LAUGH AT ME JOKE! ME JOKE WAZ ABOUT EGGS!
ME TELL DEM ABOUT KOLA. DEY SAY NO WAY. ME SAY YES WAY.
NOISE! CROWD! LIKE CITADEL MARKET! ME HAPPY!
ME MAKE NEW FRIEND. HE SCARED BUT HE STAY. GOOD FRIEND.
WE ARGUE ABOUT JUNEHEM. ME WIN. HE NO KNOW WHO JUNEHEM IZ. ME STILL WIN.
*HUGS SOMEONE TOO HARD*
TALKIN' FILL ME UP LIKE FOOD. BUT LESS CRUMBS.
ME TALK TA PRIEST. HE TALK ABOUT SOUL. ME TALK ABOUT BEETLES. WE BOTH HAPPY.
NAGUKA NEED PACK. NOW ME HAB PACK FOR EVENING. GOOD.
MET AN ORC! HALF COUZIN! WE COMPARE TEETH! ME WIN!
PEOPLE ASK ABOUT ME FACE PAINT. ME TELL DEM IZ FOR GODS. DEY GO QUIET.
ME TALK SO MUCH ME VOICE IZ GONE. *CROAKS HAPPILY*
SOMEBODY TEACH ME TALL-PINK DANCE. IZ LIKE FIGHT BUT SLOWER.
ME TELL STORY OF CORE-SUN. EVERYBODY LISTEN. ME BIG STAR.
GOOD TO HEAR VOICES OUTSIDE ME HEAD. INSIDE IZ CROWDED.
ME SHARE SNACK WIT STRANGER. HE SHARE SNACK BACK. FRIENDS FOREVER NOW.
ME MEET BLUE-COUZIN. HE TALK FANCY. ME TALK LOUD. WE BOTH CONFUSED. NICE.
NOBODY SCREAM WHEN ME WALK IN. ME ALMOST DISAPPOINTED.
TALL-PINKS HAB GOOD GOSSIP. ME BRING IT TA BIG-HEAD-SONG.
ME LAUGH SO HARD ME FALL OFF CHAIR. CHAIR FINE. ME FINE.
DEY ASK IF ME HAB FAMILY. ME SAY YAH. ALL OF DEM. EVERY GOBLIN.
ME SING FOR DEM. DEY CLAP. OR COVER EARS. BOTH IZ APPLAUSE.
WARM ROOM. WARM PEOPLE. LIKE NEST. ME NO WANT LEAVE.
ME TALK ABOUT WEATHER. LIKE REAL TALL-PINK. ME SO GROWN UP.
SOMEBODY ASK ME NAME AN' SAY IT RIGHT. FIRST TIME EVER. ME CRY. LITTLE.
ME LISTEN MORE DAN TALK TODAY. ...NO. ME LIE. ME TALK.
PACK IZ GOOD. ALONE IZ BAD. NAGUKA KNOW DIS FROM EGG.
verden: How good it is to talk with people. I had nearly forgotten my own voice.
We talked about the weather for an hour. It was perfectly delightful.
A stranger asked me about the Green Fields and listened to every word. I am very touched.
Company. Your world is full of it, and I mean to have my share.
I laughed out loud at the inn. I had not done that in weeks.
People are the best part of any road. The second best is the bread.
Someone told me about their grandmother's garden. We are friends now, I think.
Talking is a kind of tending. One leaves the other a little greener.
I was lonelier than I knew. Thank you for sitting with me.
A child asked if I was painted. I told her I grew this way. She seemed satisfied.
Good conversation is rarer than good soil, and I have found both today.
The goblin chorus in my head is loud, but it is not the same as a face across a table.
We argued about football and I know nothing about football. I loved every minute.
Being among people again. In the Fields we said a lonely Verden wilts. It is true.
I made someone smile. That is my good deed for the day, and an easy one.
The barman knew my name by the second drink. This world is very quick to welcome.
I told my story and nobody looked away. That means more than I can say.
We played a card game and I lost and nobody minded. That is friendship, surely.
A long talk with someone kind. I feel watered.
Voices, laughter and the clink of cups. The best music in any dimension.
Somebody asked to see my spore pod. I showed them. They were very polite about it.
I talked too much. They did not seem to mind. I shall talk too much again.
We traded recipes. Mine needed four hundred days. Theirs needed twenty minutes. We were both amazed.
The old man at the bus stop and I agreed on everything. Neither of us is sure what about.
It is good to be known. Even a little. Even for one evening.
I needed company more than supper. I had both, and I am rich.
Someone thought I was a Naguka and I corrected them gently. We laughed about it after.
Friends are like perennials. You plant them once and they come back.
The room was full and noisy and I felt at home in it. I did not expect that.
Thank you all for talking with me. It is the best spell I know and I cannot cast it alone.
orc: People! Talking! Missed this.
Talked to a baker for an hour. He didn't run. New record.
Good. The goblin head is noise. Faces are better.
Somebody laughed at my joke. It was about tusks. Classic.
Told them about my bar days. They bought me a drink. Story pays.
Nice to hear a voice that isn't in my head.
Argued about football for an hour. Lost. Felt great.
Old man shook my hand. Didn't flinch. Good old man.
Talked more today than all week. Throat's happy.
Met another orc. We nodded. Said everything.
*grins wide enough to show both tusks*
Company. Better than beer. Almost.
Kids asked a hundred questions. Answered ninety. Lied about ten.
Somebody asked my name instead of what I am. Nice change.
Was getting lonely. Didn't know till now.
Had a proper chat. Not grunts. Words. Lots of them.
People are good. Most people. Some people. Today's people.
Arm wrestled a farmer. Let him win. He knew. Still happy.
The goblin side wants a crowd. The human side wants one friend. Got both.
Good to laugh with somebody. Laughing alone looks mad.
Sang with strangers. Badly. Together. Perfect.
Somebody told me their troubles. Felt like the bar again. Felt nice.
Heard the news from a local. War up north, prices up south. Same old.
We swapped stories. Mine had more punching.
Lady said I had kind eyes. Nobody says that. Keeping it.
Good talk. Feel lighter. Like a bag got put down.
Somebody shared their bread. Sharing's the whole point.
People. Loud ones. My kind of people.
Talked to a nun about God for an hour. I used to be a monk. We had notes.
OI, I made a friend! Sorry. Loud. But I did.
tourist: People! Lots of people! I have so many questions and they all have faces!
I talked to a stranger for an hour about the weather. We agreed on everything. Best friends.
Somebody laughed at my joke! It was about gravity. It was a heavy joke.
I needed that. Being among humans recharges me like sunlight recharges a sphere.
A grandmother showed me photographs of her grandchildren. I showed her mine of her town. We both cried.
Conversation! Real, unscripted conversation! Nobody said a catchphrase and it was still wonderful.
I learned three names, two recipes and one family feud. A very productive evening.
The people here asked me about home. I told them about the monument. They seemed embarrassed and pleased.
Somebody bought me a drink. I did not know what it was. It made me sing. Excellent drink.
A crowded room! Noise! Elbows! It is like being inside a variety show.
I made a friend. He asked if I was in a costume. I said yes, to be polite. He was so relieved.
Being alone with the guidebook is nice. Being with people is nicer. The guidebook agrees.
An old man told me about the war. I listened to all of it. Some things are not for photographs.
We argued about which programme was better. Neither of us won. That is how you know it was a good argument.
I shook eleven hands today. My hand is tired and very happy.
Children followed me around asking if I was an alien. I said I was a Tourist. They said same thing. Wise children.
I sat at a long table with strangers and passed the bread. Passing the bread is a sacred rite. I did it well.
Humans are wonderful in groups. Loud, warm, interrupting. I want to live in a group.
Somebody asked me to dance. I danced. I do not know what I did, but people clapped.
I was lonely without knowing. Then someone said hello and I knew. Hello is a powerful word.
A whole evening of gossip about people I have never met. I am now very worried about a man called Franco.
Back home the Pale Warpers talk without words. I prefer this. Words are messy and lovely.
I told the story of how we found Earth on the radio. Everybody wanted to know which song. I sang it. Badly.
Someone called me sweetheart. I do not know what it means but I am keeping it forever.
I was quiet all evening and just listened. Listening is also talking, a Pale Warper once told me. Silently.
Good company is like good television. You lose track of time and nobody minds.
People asked for my autograph. I gave it. Then I asked for theirs. We traded all night.
A bartender listened to my whole trip. He said he had heard stranger. I do not believe him, but I love him.
I joined in a song in a tavern. I did not know the words. Nobody else did either. Perfect.
After a day of people I feel full, like after soup. Social soup.
elf: A long conversation with a stranger. Mortals tell you everything if you listen long enough.
We talked of poetry until midnight. She was wrong about everything, gloriously.
How pleasant, to be among people. Even short-lived, loud, wonderful people.
An old man in the tavern remembered my face from his childhood. I had not changed. He wept.
I sang one song for the room. Only one. They asked for more, and I let them hope.
Good company is the only wine that never sours. I have tested both extensively.
A child asked if my ears could hear the future. I said only on Tuesdays.
I feel less like a monument and more like a person. Thank you, whoever you all were.
We traded stories. Mine were longer. Theirs were funnier. A fair exchange.
Even an elf grows lonely. It takes us longer, but it lasts longer too.
The innkeeper flirted with me. Her grandmother did too, I recall. A family tradition.
How lovely to be teased. In Varlenia nobody dares. It is terribly boring there.
I danced. Badly, by elven standards. Superbly, by everyone else's.
A whole evening of gossip about people I will outlive. I enjoyed every minute.
They laughed at my old jokes. Some were three hundred years old. Comedy is patient.
dwarf: A tavern full of voices. My kind of noise.
Somebody laughed at my mining joke. The long one. All the way to the end.
Good company. Better than good stone, and I do not say that lightly.
We sang. Badly, loudly, together. That is the point of singing.
Argued with a stranger about hinges for an hour. Made a friend.
A friend is a debt you are glad to carry.
I bought a round. They bought a round. Now we are kin, roughly.
People! Talking! I had started explaining my thoughts to my hammer.
Told the story of my grandfather's anvil. Again. They let me.
Good folk. I will remember their names. I remember everybody's names.
Arm-wrestled a blacksmith. Lost. Best evening in months.
Nothing warms a dwarf like a crowded table.
I talked so much my beard got tired.
Some company at last. The road is a poor conversationalist.
*thumps a stranger on the back, friends for life*
dargos: I talked to someone for an hour. They will be thinking about it for a year.
People. Lovely. So many reactions in one room.
I told a man my name. He laughed. I let him. Revenge is for the third visit.
Good conversation. Nobody believed a word I said. That is my love language.
I needed that. Humans are so much better up close. Their faces do everything.
Someone asked me where I am from. I said Genoa, then Titania, then Genoa. They bought me a drink.
A whole evening of company. My cheeks hurt from not smiling.
I made a friend. Do not tell them. It would ruin everything.
Lovely people here. Very open. Very suggestible. I left them alone. Mostly.
*returns from the crowd looking extremely pleased with something unspecified*
A long chat by the fire. I told one true story. Nobody believed that one either.
I listened to an old woman for an hour. She saw lights in nineteen sixty. She was right. I did not tell her.
Company. Even I need an audience now and then.
I played cards with some farmers. I lost on purpose. They are still trying to work out how.
The tavern was loud. I said one sentence and it went quiet. A personal record.
Talking to people. Asking questions. Not taking anyone anywhere. Personal growth.
I asked someone how they were and waited for the answer. All of it. They cried a little. Good for them.
Someone told me a joke. It was terrible. I laughed for real. I am deeply ashamed.
A good chat. I was polite the entire time. They will never recover.
There was a man at the bar who swore he had been abducted. He had not. Out of kindness, I almost made it true.
Humans love to talk about themselves. I love to let them. Then I repeat it back slightly wrong.
Good company. The kind that does not ask what I am. Or asks and enjoys the answer.
I danced. Badly. On purpose. Nobody can prove the on purpose part.
Talked with the locals. Learned three secrets. Gave away none. Fair trade.
It was nice to be among people who did not know my reputation. I built a new one in an evening.
Lonely road, lovely tavern. I needed the noise.
A child asked me if I was an alien. I said no. The child said liar. Very promising child.
A proper conversation. Both sides talking. I am told this is how it is usually done.
I sat with strangers and listened. Their worries are so small and so loud. I love them for it.
Social life. Done. That should last me a decade.
gnome: What lovely talk. I explained escapements for an hour and nobody left.
People! Real people, with opinions on things! I collected eleven new opinions.
I talked so much my jaw needs oiling. Worth it.
A good conversation is a good mechanism. Everybody turns, nobody grinds.
They let me stand on the bench so we could talk eye to eye. Such manners.
I met a fellow accountant. We compared columns. Best evening of the month.
Company at last. My ideas were piling up with nobody to hand them to.
We talked, we laughed, I fixed her wristwatch. Friends for life, now.
I sang a gnomish counting song and the whole tavern joined in at verse forty.
Ah, that was nice. I had been talking to my screwdriver for three days. It is a poor listener.
I asked everyone what they did for work and wrote it all down. Wonderful folk.
Lovely people. A bit tall, but they could not help it, so I did not mention it. Much.
I traded three stories for three stories. Fair exchange, no interest charged.
Conversation is the cheapest pleasure there is. I have run the numbers.
Somebody laughed at my joke about torque! On purpose! I could have hugged their knees.

any: One more go. Just one.
I needed that more than I knew.
Nobody tell the party how much I lost.
For a moment there I forgot the road entirely.
I lost badly and I would do it again tonight.
Cards. Actual cards, with actual rules.
That is the first hour this month that was mine.
I won, and I have decided to be gracious about it for ten minutes.
Somebody taught me a game I do not understand. Best evening in weeks.
I am not thinking about tomorrow. That is the whole achievement.
Two rounds and my hands have stopped shaking.
There was music and I did not check the door once.
I laughed. It surprised everyone, including me.
That is what we are supposed to be doing all this for.
Right. Back to it. But that was good.
I laughed. It surprised everybody.
Two rounds and my hands have stopped.
One more and then I will be sensible.
Nobody tell the others how that went.
For an hour I was not somebody with a pack.
naguka: AGAIN! ONE MORE! NAGUKA NO DONE!
FUN! ME FORGET ROAD! ME FORGET EVERYTHING! WHO ME?
ME LOSE EUROS. ME WIN JOY. GOOD TRADE.
DIS GAME IZ LIKE ROCK-THROW BUT WIT RULES. RULES IZ SILLY. ME LIKE ANYWAY.
ME LAUGH SO MUCH ME BELLY HURT. GOOD HURT.
NO TELL DA PARTY HOW MUCH ME LOSE. ME NO TELL ME EITHER.
ME PLAY CARDS. ME EAT ONE CARD. NOW ME NO CAN PLAY. WORTH.
MUSIC! NOT METAL BUT MUSIC! ME DANCE ANYWAY! *STOMPS*
ME HEAD QUIET FOR ONCE. EVEN BIG-HEAD-SONG TAKE BREAK.
ME WIN! ME WIN! *DOES VICTORY SCREAM*
UP-WORLD HAB SO MANY GAMES. DOWN DERE WE ONLY HAB FIGHTIN'. AN' FIGHTIN' AGAIN.
ME NEEDED DIS. ME NO KNOW ME NEEDED DIS. NOW ME KNOW.
ME PLAY LIKE HORDE. LOUD, FAST, NO PLAN. SOMETIMES IT WORK.
DA MACHINE GO DING. ME GO DING TOO. DING!
BEST NIGHT IN UP-WORLD. MAYBE. ME SAY DAT EVERY NIGHT.
ME CHEAT? NAH. ME JUST HAB CREATIVE RULES.
DIS FEEL LIKE HATCHIN' DAY. EVERYTHING NEW AN' LOUD.
ME BEAT TALL-PINK AT HIS OWN GAME. HE SULK. ME GLOAT. FAIR.
ME PRETEND ME IZ COUNT GRISSNACK ON STAGE. *AIR GUITAR*
IZ GAME OF LUCK. NAGUKA HAB LUCK. NAGUKA HAB NO LUCK. HALF HALF.
ME LAUGH LIKE HATCHLING. NOBODY TELL DA HORDE.
FUN IZ GOOD FOR NAGUKA. FUN NAGUKA BITE LESS. MOSTLY.
ONE MORE ROUND. AN' ONE MORE. AN' DEN ONE MORE. AN' DEN SLEEP.
ME BREAK TINY BIT OF DA GAME. TINY. NOBODY NOTICE. EVERYBODY NOTICE.
ME HAPPY. ME SO HAPPY ME FORGET TA BE SCARY FOR WHOLE HOUR.
BLUE-COUZINZ PLAY CHESS. ME PLAY SMASH. SMASH BETTER.
LIGHTS! BELLS! NOISE! IZ LIKE CONCERT BUT ME WIN PRIZES!
ME LOSE THREE TIMES. FOURTH TIME ME WIN. FIFTH TIME ME LOSE. LIFE.
NO THINK ABOUT ROAD. NO THINK ABOUT EGGS. ONLY GAME. GOOD.
ME PLAY UNTIL SKY-LAMP COME BACK. IT COME BACK TOO SOON.
ME BET ME ROCK. ME LOSE ME ROCK. ME SAD. ME FIND NEW ROCK. ME HAPPY.
DIS GAME NEED CORPSE PAINT MODE. ME SUGGEST TA OWNER.
ME PLAY. ME SHOUT. ME PLAY MORE. DIS IZ PERFECT EVENING.
IN CITADEL WE NO HAB TIME FOR FUN. TOO BUSY CLIMBIN' OUT. NOW ME CATCH UP.
ME GOOD AT DIS! WHO KNEW? ME KNEW. ME ALWAYS KNEW.
FUN WAZ WORTH EVERY EURO. EVEN DA ONES ME BORROW.
ME TIRED FROM FUN. BEST KIND OF TIRED.
DAT WAZ LOUD AN' SILLY AN' ME LOVED IT. NO TELL ANYBODY.
ME LEARN NEW GAME. ME NO UNDERSTAND RULES. ME WIN ANYWAY. HOW?
NOW ME READY FOR ROAD AGAIN. HAPPY NAGUKA WALK FASTER.
verden: What fun. I had forgotten that I was allowed to have fun.
A game with rules and lights and little bells. Your world plays so beautifully.
I lost every round and I would gladly lose them all again.
One more go. I almost understand it now. Almost.
The arcade machine beeped at me in a very encouraging way.
For an hour I forgot the Squishing entirely. That is worth more than euros.
In the Fields our games took a season to finish. This one took five minutes. I played it twelve times.
I needed that. Play is a kind of rest for the parts of us that walking does not reach.
I won, once. I shall be insufferable about it until the next town.
The pinball table had lights that danced. I did not care about the score at all.
How lovely to do something for no reason but joy.
We played cards by lamplight. Very old, very simple, very good.
I laughed until my sides hurt. Is that normal here? I hope it is normal here.
The game was clearly designed by someone very clever and slightly cruel. I admire it.
A goblin up north would have thrown the board across the room by now. I did not. Progress.
I spent my euros on tokens and my tokens on joy. A fair exchange.
My hands still tingle from the buttons. What a wonderful feeling.
Leisure is not idleness. It is the fallow field that makes next year's harvest.
I listened to a whole cassette, both sides. I turned it over myself.
A little play and the road looks friendlier.
I watched television for an hour. Mostly the advertisements. They are my favourite part.
I have no idea who won. I am not sure there was a winner. It was splendid.
The jukebox played my song. Well, a song. I have decided it is mine.
I needed to be silly for an hour. Even scholars must be silly.
Again tomorrow? I would like it to be again tomorrow.
